title: feat(cua-driver-rs): rename to com.trycua.cuadriver + /Applications/CuaDriver.app
body:
## Summary

Rename the Rust port's bundle identity so it matches the Swift driver's brand minus the `Rs` suffix. Going forward, the Rust port IS the canonical cua-driver: installs at `/Applications/CuaDriver.app`, identifies as `com.trycua.cuadriver`, and **replaces** the Swift driver's `.app` at the same path on install (the two don't coexist).

Per Francesco's direction: "they don't have to coexist; it's either one or the other. We need to handle the fact that the user at some point will have to override the Swift cua driver with the Rust, so better start keeping them the same name."

## What changes

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `.app` bundle dir | `libs/cua-driver-rs/scripts/CuaDriverRs.app/` | `libs/cua-driver-rs/scripts/CuaDriver.app/` (git-tracked rename) |
| Install path on macOS | `/Applications/CuaDriverRs.app` | `/Applications/CuaDriver.app` (replaces Swift at the same path) |
| `CFBundleIdentifier` | `com.trycua.cuadriverrs` | `com.trycua.cuadriver` |
| `CFBundleName` / display name | `Cua Driver RS` | `Cua Driver` |
| Rust source TCC heuristic | `is_executable_inside_cuadriverrs_app()` | `is_executable_inside_cuadriver_app()` |

## Swift-takeover handling

`_install-rust.sh` now detects whether the existing `.app` at the install path is the Swift driver (reads `CFBundleIdentifier` via `PlistBuddy` before `rm -rf`-ing). When the prior bundle id is `com.trycua.driver`, the post-install message surfaces the `tccutil reset` commands so the user can clear orphaned Swift grants — Swift's grants attributed to `com.trycua.driver` become orphaned and unused when the Rust bundle (`com.trycua.cuadriver`) takes over the path. macOS will surface the Accessibility + Screen Recording dialogs for the new bundle id on first action.

## Files

- `libs/cua-driver-rs/scripts/CuaDriver.app/Contents/Info.plist` — new content (bundle id, names, header doc rewritten).
- Rust source: `bundle.rs`, `cli.rs`, `proxy.rs`, `main.rs` — string/path/function rename.
- `libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh` — `APP_NAME`, install path, post-install `tccutil` hint block, comments.
- `libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.sh` — comment updates only.
- `libs/cua-driver-rs/scripts/install-local.sh` — dev-loop bundle path.
- `.github/workflows/cd-rust-cua-driver.yml` — macOS bundle assembly step + codesign/notarize/staple paths.
- `docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guide/getting-started/installation.mdx` — install dir + Swift-replacement note.

## What this does NOT do

- **No release-tag prefix change.** Tags stay `cua-driver-rs-v*`; only the inner bundle moves. Existing one-liners (`cua-driver/scripts/install.sh`, the `cua-driver-rs/scripts/install.{sh,ps1}` redirect shims) all keep working.
- **No binary rename.** `cua-driver` on PATH stays the same. Hermes and anything else calling the binary by name is unaffected.
- **No package-home rename.** `~/.cua-driver-rs/` stays where it is. A future `cua-driver migrate` verb can move it under `~/.cua-driver/` once it has somewhere safe to land.
- **No auto-uninstall of legacy Swift state beyond the .app replacement.** `~/.cua-driver/` (Swift's config), `~/Library/Application Support/Cua Driver/`, Swift TCC grants — all left in place. The post-install message points at `tccutil reset` for the orphaned grants; the user runs it manually if they want.

## Conflicts with #1558

The in-flight uninstall convergence PR ([#1558](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/1558)) still references `/Applications/CuaDriverRs.app` + `com.trycua.cuadriverrs` in `_uninstall-rust.sh`. After this PR lands, `#1558` needs a small rebase: update the install-path string + bundle id in `_uninstall-rust.sh` to the new names, and optionally keep the old `tccutil reset` lines as a legacy-cleanup branch (for users upgrading from the older bundle id who never re-ran the install).

## Test plan

- [ ] CD workflow_dispatch run on this branch: published `darwin-universal` tarball contains a `CuaDriver.app` with `com.trycua.cuadriver` bundle id (verify via `plutil -p` after unzipping the asset).
- [ ] macOS clean install: `curl …/libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.sh | bash -s -- --experimental-rust` → `/Applications/CuaDriver.app` lands, `cua-driver --version` works, `tccutil reset Accessibility com.trycua.cuadriver` then `cua-driver check_permissions` fires the dialog for the new bundle id.
- [ ] macOS Swift-takeover: pre-install Swift, then run Rust install — "Replaced the Swift cua-driver bundle" note prints with the tccutil reset commands.
- [ ] No regression on Windows (this PR doesn't touch `install.ps1`).
- [ ] No regression on Linux (this PR doesn't touch the Linux install path; `.app` is macOS-only).

Don't auto-merge — substantial change, deserves review.

title: cua-driver check_permissions reports stale accessibility=true after `tccutil reset Accessibility com.trycua.driver` (macOS)
body:
**Affects:** `cua-driver-rs` (Rust port) — observed on `cua-driver-rs-v0.2.4` post-rename. Likely also affects Swift `cua-driver` because both backends use the same underlying call (see "Code-as-read" below).

**Platform:** macOS

## Repro

1. Install `cua-driver-rs` (or the Swift `cua-driver` — same bundle id `com.trycua.driver` post v0.2.4).
2. Reset the Accessibility grant for the driver's bundle id:
   ```bash
   tccutil reset Accessibility com.trycua.driver
   ```
3. Confirm TCC has no row for the bundle id:
   ```bash
   sqlite3 ~/Library/Application\ Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db \
     "SELECT * FROM access WHERE client='com.trycua.driver'"
   # returns zero rows
   ```
4. Kill any running daemons so nothing is cached in-process:
   ```bash
   cua-driver stop 2>/dev/null
   pkill -f "cua-driver mcp"
   pkill -f "cua-driver serve"
   ```
5. Run `check_permissions`:
   ```bash
   cua-driver check_permissions
   ```

## Actual

```json
{"accessibility": true, "screen_recording": true}
```

## Expected

After `tccutil reset Accessibility com.trycua.driver`, the bundle id has no AX grant on file. A fresh `check_permissions` should report:

```json
{"accessibility": false, "screen_recording": <whatever ScreenCapture's TCC row says>}
```

…until the user re-grants in **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility**.

## Code-as-read

`libs/cua-driver-rs/crates/platform-macos/src/permissions/status.rs` (lines 42-45):

```rust
/// Live AX trust state — `AXIsProcessTrusted()`.
pub fn accessibility_granted() -> bool {
    unsafe { crate::ax::bindings::AXIsProcessTrusted() }
}
```

`libs/cua-driver-rs/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/check_permissions.rs` (lines 47-55):

```rust
async fn invoke(&self, args: Value) -> ToolResult {
    let should_prompt = args.get("prompt").and_then(|v| v.as_bool()).unwrap_or(true);
    if should_prompt {
        let _ = request_accessibility();
        let _ = request_screen_recording();
    }
    let accessibility = accessibility_granted();
    let screen_recording = screen_recording_granted();
    ...
```

There's **no caching layer** between the tool call and `AXIsProcessTrusted()` — every invocation makes a fresh `unsafe` C call. So the stale value isn't coming from in-process memoization.

## Hypothesis

`AXIsProcessTrusted()` reports the AX trust state for whoever TCC attributes the **calling process** to. For a CLI binary invoked from a shell (Terminal.app, iTerm, VS Code's integrated terminal, etc.), macOS attribution can route to the *responsible* parent process — usually the terminal application — rather than the codesigned bundle id. If the parent terminal already has Accessibility granted, `AXIsProcessTrusted()` returns `true` even though TCC has no row for `com.trycua.driver`.

This is consistent with the live evidence:
- `tccutil reset Accessibility com.trycua.driver` succeeded and the TCC.db row was confirmed gone.
- No daemon was running, so the call ran fresh in the CLI process.
- The terminal launching `cua-driver` had Accessibility granted at the parent level.

Also worth ruling out: `Command::Call` (`libs/cua-driver-rs/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs:584-593`) proxies tool calls through the daemon's Unix socket when a daemon is listening. The user reports killing the daemon first, so this path shouldn't apply — but worth confirming during diagnosis that the daemon really wasn't listening (e.g. `lsof ~/Library/Caches/cua-driver/daemon.sock 2>/dev/null` returns empty).

## Parity with Swift

`libs/cua-driver/Sources/CuaDriverCore/Permissions/Permissions.swift` (lines 29-35) uses the **same** `AXIsProcessTrusted()` call:

```swift
public static func currentStatus() async -> PermissionsStatus {
    async let screen = probeScreenRecording()
    return await PermissionsStatus(
        accessibility: AXIsProcessTrusted(),
        screenRecording: screen
    )
}
```

So this is **not** a Rust-port drift bug — the Swift binary would behave identically under the same repro. Worth confirming live: install the Swift `cua-driver`, run the same repro, see if Swift also reports `accessibility: true` after `tccutil reset`. If yes, the issue is shared and deserves a fix in both backends (probably: don't rely on `AXIsProcessTrusted()` alone — cross-check with a direct query of the TCC.db row for our bundle id, or document the limitation and surface it via `cua-driver diagnose`).

## Suggested next steps

1. **Confirm the hypothesis live** on the same box that reproduced this:
   - Repro under `Terminal.app` with AX **not** granted to Terminal (should return `false`).
   - Repro under `Terminal.app` with AX **granted** to Terminal (should return `true` if the parent-attribution theory is right).
2. **If confirmed**, options for the fix:
   - Read TCC.db directly for our bundle id (`com.trycua.driver`) and report on that as the source of truth. `cua-driver diagnose` already has access to the bundle id; reuse that here.
   - Or surface both states in `check_permissions`: `{"accessibility_for_bundle": <TCC.db lookup>, "accessibility_for_process": AXIsProcessTrusted()}` so callers can distinguish "the daemon has AX" from "the calling shell has AX".
3. **Document the caveat in `check_permissions`'s description string** until a real fix lands.

## Out of scope

This issue does NOT cover:
- The screen-recording probe (`CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess` + window enumeration fallback) — that's a separate question and the user reports it was returning `true` in the same run, but I haven't audited its repro shape.
- The first-launch permissions gate (`platform_macos::permissions::run_if_needed`) — that runs at `serve` startup, not on `check_permissions` invocation, so it's unrelated.

## Labels

`bug`, would also want `cua-driver-rs` + `macos` + `papercut` (none exist yet on the repo as of this writing).

## Related

- The cua-driver-rs v0.2.3 → v0.2.4 rename to `/Applications/CuaDriver.app` + bundle id `com.trycua.driver` (PR #1559) doesn't change this behaviour — the underlying call is the same. But it does mean the same `tccutil reset com.trycua.driver` invocation now affects both the Swift and Rust binaries, which makes this bug more visible (you can hit it the moment after a clean re-install).

title: fix(cua-driver-rs): drop bogus window-enum fallback in screen-recording probe
body:
## Summary

`permissions::status::screen_recording_granted()` had a heuristic fallback when `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess` returned false: `!crate::windows::all_windows().is_empty()`. The theory was that getting non-empty results from `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` implied the Screen Recording grant was active. That theory is wrong — `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` returns window IDs and bounds for any process **without** requiring the Screen Recording grant; only window **titles** are gated. So the fallback returned \`true\` on any populated desktop regardless of grant state.

Two user-visible bugs follow from this:

1. **\`check_permissions\` false positive after \`tccutil reset\`** — observed live: after \`tccutil reset ScreenCapture com.trycua.driver\` clears the SR row, the freshly-spawned daemon still reports \`screen_recording: true\`. This is half of #1561 — the SR half, anyway; the AX half is a separate concern (see below).
2. **Startup permissions gate skipped** — \`permissions::gate::run_if_needed\` short-circuits when \`status.all_granted()\` (\`gate.rs:213\`). With the bogus fallback, users who had never granted SR would have the gate silently no-op on first \`cua-driver serve\` start, and only hit the failure inside \`screenshot\` / \`record\` tool calls later.

The fix is to remove the fallback entirely and trust \`CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess\` — Apple's documented preflight API for this grant, accurate on macOS 11+.

## Files changed

- \`libs/cua-driver-rs/crates/platform-macos/src/permissions/status.rs\` — strip the \`all_windows()\` fallback in \`screen_recording_granted()\`; expand the doc-comment to record the rationale so the heuristic doesn't get re-introduced.
- \`libs/cua-driver-rs/Cargo.lock\` — refreshed to match the v0.2.4 workspace version (the \`release-bump-version.yml\` workflow didn't update the lock when it bumped \`Cargo.toml\`; \`cargo check\` on this branch catches that up). No new direct deps; only the workspace package version + transitive dep additions that were already present in \`crates/cua-driver/Cargo.toml\` (\`tar\`, \`flate2\` from the skills tarball reader).

## On the AX side of #1561

The umbrella issue (#1561) reported that **both** \`accessibility\` and \`screen_recording\` come back \`true\` after \`tccutil reset\`. The SR side is a probe bug, fixed here. The AX side is a TCC attribution question: \`AXIsProcessTrusted()\` is the right API, but TCC attributes shell-invoked CLI processes to the parent terminal — so any shell that already has AX granted (Terminal, Claude Code, iTerm) will make \`cua-driver check_permissions\` see \`accessibility: true\` no matter what \`com.trycua.driver\` has in TCC. That's a fundamentally separate problem from this fix; tracking it on #1561.

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo check -p platform-macos\` — clean, no new warnings on the changed file
- [x] Reproduced original bug on installed v0.2.4: \`tccutil reset ScreenCapture com.trycua.driver\` then \`cua-driver check_permissions '{\"prompt\":false}'\` → \`screen_recording: true\` (BUG)
- [x] Debug binary built from this branch ran against shell-attributed process (shell has SR) → \`true\` (correct: shell-attributed probe sees real shell grant)
- [ ] End-to-end \`com.trycua.driver\`-attributed validation (run inside \`/Applications/CuaDriver.app\` after \`tccutil reset\`, expect \`false\`) — pending the released artifact, easiest to verify post-merge via the next CD-published \`cua-driver-rs\` build

## Related

- Issue: #1561
- Sibling: #1560 (\`fix(uninstall): stop running cua-driver daemon before removing the binary\`)

title: Harden computer server launch and auth defaults
body:
## Summary

Fixes the `launch` command injection path by removing shell execution from the computer-server and cua-auto launch helpers.

Also tightens the exposed computer-server control surface:

- require explicit local unauthenticated mode with `CUA_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_LOCAL=1`
- gate `run_command`/`shell`/`exec` and PTY command creation behind `CUA_ENABLE_RUN_COMMAND=1`
- protect `/cmd`, `/ws`, `/playwright_exec`, `/responses`, and mounted `/mcp`
- default server binding to `127.0.0.1`
- lazy-init native handlers so importing/listing commands does not initialize macOS automation code
- update critical dependency ranges and lockfiles for litellm, fastmcp, crawl4ai, nltk, and authlib-related alerts

Fixes #1097.

## Testing

- `cd libs/python/computer-server && uv run --frozen --with pytest --with pytest-asyncio pytest tests/test_auth_availability.py tests/test_import_safety.py tests/test_window_launch.py`
- `cd libs/python/cua-auto && uv run --no-project --python 3.12 --with pytest pytest tests/test_window_launch.py`

title: feat(cua-driver-rs): Phase 2 panel + structural fixes (opt-in)
body:
## Summary

Builds on #1565 (Phase 1 panel). Lands Phase 2 of the native NSPanel onboarding gate AND a handful of structural macOS fixes that surfaced during live testing on this Mac. Key user-facing change: the panel is now **opt-in** via `CUA_DRIVER_RS_PERMISSIONS_PANEL=1` rather than auto-shown when the daemon is launched from the bundled `.app`. The terminal banner is the documented default again.

## Why opt-in

During live testing the panel works once you grant TCC manually — but a chain of macOS behaviours makes the "auto-shown" default fragile in dev environments:

- **Cargo linker-signing identifier**: Cargo's default ad-hoc sign uses a per-build random identifier like `cua_driver-9402b19cac15ebc5`, not the `com.trycua.driver` bundle id. TCC keys registrations under the codesign identifier, so dev builds never appear in System Settings → Privacy & Security. Manual `codesign --force --sign - -i com.trycua.driver` after build fixes it; CD's Developer-ID signing step already does. (Follow-up: bake this into `install-local.sh` and/or a Makefile target.)
- **`tccutil reset` doesn't invalidate the session-level TCC trust cache**: an in-process `AXIsProcessTrusted()` call still returns the cached "trusted" state after a reset, so the gate short-circuits before the panel can be presented. Only a logout/reboot fully clears the cache.
- The panel relies on `[NSApp runModalForWindow:]` + a 1Hz `NSTimer` in `NSModalPanelRunLoopMode` (NOT `NSRunLoopCommonModes`, which silently drops timer fires in modal sessions); that needed a specific fix and is fragile to future changes.

Until those are stabilised end-to-end, terminal flow remains the default. The panel can be exercised by power users via `CUA_DRIVER_RS_PERMISSIONS_PANEL=1`.

## What's in this PR

### Phase 2 panel code (\`crates/platform-macos/src/permissions/panel.rs\`)

- **Live status rows**: each row's NSImageView + title NSTextField are stashed as \`RowHandles\` in a thread-local. The poll callback swaps the SF Symbol (\`checkmark.circle.fill\` / \`xmark.circle.fill\`), tint (systemGreenColor / systemRedColor), and label text colour (\`labelColor\` → \`secondaryLabelColor\` on grant) in place.
- **Dynamic heading + subheading**: \`heading_for(status)\` and \`subheading_for(status)\` produce verbatim parity with Swift's matrix (\"CuaDriver needs your permission\" → \"One more permission\" → \"CuaDriver is ready\"). Rebound via \`setStringValue:\` on every tick.
- **Auto-dismiss on all-green**: the 1Hz \`NSTimer\` calls \`[NSApp stopModal]\` when both grants flip green, and \`show_modal\` returns \`PanelOutcome::AllGranted\` so the gate caller can skip the trailing \`wait_for_grants\` loop entirely.
- **Modal-mode timer fix**: timer constructed with \`timerWithTimeInterval:\` (non-scheduled) and added to \`NSModalPanelRunLoopMode\` explicitly. The previous Phase 1 approach of adding to \`NSRunLoopCommonModes\` doesn't fire during \`runModalForWindow:\` — that bit me live.
- **Ready strip**: green pill at the bottom (initially hidden, shown when both green) for the case where the panel is opened while already-granted.
- **Opt-in env var**: \`panel_enabled()\` requires \`CUA_DRIVER_RS_PERMISSIONS_PANEL\` set to \`1/true/yes/on\` (case-insensitive). Default unset → terminal flow.

### Gate restructuring (\`crates/platform-macos/src/permissions/gate.rs\`)

- **Hoist \`request_accessibility()\` / \`request_screen_recording()\` to before any UI**: these calls have the critical side effect of *registering* the calling process with TCC. Without the hoist, when the user clicked \"Open System Settings\" mid-panel they landed in a Privacy & Security pane where cua-driver was missing from the list. Now the registration happens first, so the list is populated whichever path the user takes.
- **New \`PanelPresentation::ShownAllGranted\` variant**: when the panel's poll resolves before the user clicks anything, the gate skips the trailing \`wait_for_grants\` loop entirely.

### Structural macOS fixes

- **Bundle-skeleton rename**: \`libs/cua-driver-rs/scripts/CuaDriver.app/\` → \`scripts/CuaDriverBundle/\`. The previous \`.app\` suffix on the repo template caused macOS LaunchServices on developer machines to index it as a *second* installed app with the \`com.trycua.driver\` bundle id, surfacing a \"ghost CuaDriver\" entry in System Settings → Privacy & Security pointing at an empty \`Contents/MacOS/\` directory. Dropping the \`.app\` suffix kills the indexing.
- **CD workflow** + **install-script comments** + **PARITY.md** updated to point at the new path.
- **Docs** (\`docs/.../getting-started/installation.mdx\`) rewritten to describe opt-in semantics.

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo test -p platform-macos --lib permissions::\` — 13/13 green (2 new parity tests for the heading-text matrix).
- [x] \`cargo build --release -p cua-driver --bin cua-driver\` — clean.
- [x] Live: panel opt-in (\`CUA_DRIVER_RS_PERMISSIONS_PANEL=1\`) renders with live rows updating as grants flip, auto-dismisses on all-green.
- [x] Live: default (no env var) takes the terminal flow with no regression.
- [x] Live: ghost-bundle entry gone from System Settings after the rename.
- [ ] CD lane builds correctly with the renamed skeleton.
- [ ] Post-merge full re-install via canonical install script verifies the end-to-end flow.

## Related

- Built on top of #1565.
- Issue #1561 (permissions onboarding parity gap).

title: fix(cua-driver): percent-encode non-ASCII paths in launch_app urls
body:
Fixes #1519.

launch_app crashed the daemon when urls contained CJK / Cyrillic / accented characters (e.g. /Users/me/器材控/templates/file.key).

Root cause: resolveLaunchURL() used URL(string:) to detect the scheme, which returns nil for bare non-ASCII characters. The fallback URL(fileURLWithPath:) path was reached, but without .standardizedFileURL the resulting URL could carry unencoded bytes that LaunchServices rejected mid-request, disconnecting the daemon.

Fix:
- Extract resolveLaunchURL into CuaDriverCore/Apps/URLResolver.swift as a public function so it can be unit-tested independently.
- For plain file paths: use URL(fileURLWithPath:).standardizedFileURL, which correctly percent-encodes non-ASCII before handing to LaunchServices.
- For file:// URLs: strip scheme, decode existing percent-encoding, then re-encode via fileURLWithPath for a clean round-trip.
- For http/https URLs: addingPercentEncoding before URL(string:) so non-ASCII query params don't return nil.
- LaunchAppTool.resolveLaunchURL now delegates to the core function.

Tests (URLResolverTests):
- CJK absolute path (/Users/me/器材控/...)
- Cyrillic path
- Accented Latin path
- Emoji path
- ASCII path (regression guard)
- Tilde expansion
- file:// passthrough
- file:// with percent-encoded CJK
- http/https URLs
- Non-ASCII in HTTPS query string
- Empty string returns nil

title: fix(cua-driver-rs): warn + force prompt:false for check_permissions in CLI mode
body:
## Problem

`cua-driver check_permissions` reports stale/wrong results after `tccutil reset Accessibility com.trycua.driver` when called from a shell or IDE terminal without a running daemon.

**Root cause:** macOS attributes the calling CLI process to the *responsible* parent application (Terminal.app, VS Code, Cursor, etc.) rather than to CuaDriver.app. `AXIsProcessTrusted()` therefore reflects the parent's Accessibility grant, not CuaDriver.app's.

The Swift binary already handles this in `CallCommand.swift` lines 148-171. The Rust CLI had no equivalent guard.

## Fix

Ports the Swift fix to the Rust CLI:

- **`cli.rs`**: when no daemon is listening and `tool == check_permissions`, emit a stderr warning and force `prompt:false`. Prevents a TCC dialog being attributed to the wrong bundle identity.
- **`check_permissions.rs`**: add the caveat to the tool description so MCP clients and `cua-driver describe` surface the limitation.
- **`status.rs`**: document the `AXIsProcessTrusted()` attribution caveat in the `accessibility_granted()` doc comment.

No behaviour change when the daemon is running (requests are forwarded through the Unix socket and run inside CuaDriver.app where attribution is correct).

Fixes #1561

title: fix(cua-driver/install.ps1): auto-add bin dir to User PATH
body:
## Summary

Today's Windows install one-liner copies `cua-driver.exe` into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\trycua\cua-driver-rs\bin\` but does NOT touch the user's PATH. The post-install message prints a multi-line `[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(...)` recipe and expects the user to paste it. This is the **only** step of the canonical Windows install that doesn't just work — every new install hits the friction.

Hit live on the Windows VM today: `cua-driver --version` failed with "not recognized as the name of a cmdlet" immediately after the install. Had to manually:

```powershell
$old = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path', 'User')
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('Path', "$old;$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\trycua\cua-driver-rs\bin", 'User')
$env:Path += ";$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\trycua\cua-driver-rs\bin"
```

Fix: after the binary install + junction wire-up, the installer appends `$VisibleBinDir` to the **User-scope** `Path` via `[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('Path', ..., 'User')`. User scope (not Machine) keeps the installer non-admin.

- **Idempotent.** Re-running the installer never duplicates the entry — the existing "already on PATH" short-circuit handles that case unchanged.
- **Opt-out via `-NoPathUpdate`** switch for users who manage `Path` out-of-band (chezmoi, dotfiles, group policy). Fetch + invoke explicitly to pass it through `irm | iex`:

  ```powershell
  & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.ps1))) -NoPathUpdate
  ```

- **Graceful fallback.** If `SetEnvironmentVariable` throws (locked-down account, GPO-managed HKCU, OneDrive-redirected profile), we catch, warn, and print the same manual command we used to print unconditionally — install otherwise succeeds.
- The calling shell's `$env:Path` is untouched (Windows env semantics — registry writes don't propagate into the running process). Success message tells the user to open a new PowerShell window or stitch `$env:Path` for the current session.

The legacy `libs/cua-driver-rs/scripts/install.ps1` shim is a fetch-and-`iex` redirect to this canonical script, so it picks up the new behavior automatically — no edit needed there.

## What changed

- `libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.ps1`
  - Add `-NoPathUpdate` switch param.
  - Extract `Get-UserPathEntries` / `Test-OnUserPath` / `Add-UserPathEntry` / `Write-ManualPathInstructions` helpers.
  - Replace the info-only "we don't auto-edit on Windows" block with an auto-add path that falls through to manual instructions on failure or when `-NoPathUpdate` is set.
- `docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guide/getting-started/installation.mdx`
  - Update the `CUA_DRIVER_RS_NO_MODIFY_PATH` row of the env-var table — Windows now points users at the `-NoPathUpdate` switch instead of saying "Windows installer never auto-edits PATH" (no longer true).
  - Add a short paragraph in the Windows install section documenting the auto-add behavior and the opt-out switch.

Net diff: 85 insertions, 29 deletions across two files. The bulk of the install.ps1 delta is comments + helper extraction; logical behavior change is ~20 lines.

## Test plan

- [ ] On the Windows VM: fresh install via the canonical one-liner, then verify `cua-driver --version` resolves in a newly-opened PowerShell window without manual `SetEnvironmentVariable` gymnastics.
- [ ] Re-run the installer; verify the post-install message reports "$VisibleBinDir is on your user PATH" (idempotent — no duplicate entry).
- [ ] Run with `-NoPathUpdate`; verify the manual `[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(...)` instructions print and the User `Path` registry value is untouched.
- [ ] Simulate locked-down account by temporarily denying HKCU write to `Path`; verify the `try/catch` falls back to the manual instructions and the install still reports success.
- [ ] Spot-check `Get-Content $env:USERPROFILE\.cua-driver-rs\install.lock` after install to confirm nothing else regressed.

title: cua-driver 0.2.0: mcp command hangs in AppKit run loop on M4 Mac mini (macOS 26.3.1)
body:
## Description

`cua-driver mcp` produces zero output on stdout/stderr and hangs indefinitely (enters AppKit run loop without processing stdin). This happens on a **specific Mac** — identical binary (SHA256 match) works fine on another Mac with the same macOS version.

`cua-driver serve` also exhibits the same AppKit path behavior (no socket created when run directly).

## Environment

**Affected machine:**
- Mac mini M4 (T8132), Apple Silicon
- macOS 26.3.1, Build `25D771280a`, ProductVersionExtra `(a)`
- cua-driver 0.2.0, installed via manual tar extraction
- Binary SHA256: `ba89c48a94a07bea27011a7b158190a09b6a7c2b44e573eef35bc609f40eb343`
- SIP: enabled, AMFI developer_mode: enabled

**Working machine (for comparison):**
- MacBook Pro M3 (T6000), Apple Silicon
- Same macOS version, same build, same binary SHA256
- cua-driver works correctly: `echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0",...}' | cua-driver mcp` returns proper MCP initialize response

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Kill any existing daemon: `pkill -9 cua-driver`
2. Start daemon via LaunchServices: `open -n -g -a CuaDriver --args serve`
3. Verify daemon is running and socket exists:
   ```
   $ pgrep -fl cua-driver
   3381 /Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver serve
   $ ls ~/Library/Caches/cua-driver/cua-driver.sock
   (exists)
   $ cua-driver call check_permissions
   ✅ Accessibility: granted.
   ✅ Screen Recording: granted.
   ```
4. Test MCP:
   ```
   echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"test","version":"1.0"}},"id":1}' | cua-driver mcp
   ```
5. **Expected:** JSON-RPC response with serverInfo
6. **Actual:** Process hangs indefinitely, zero stdout/stderr output

## Diagnostic Evidence

### `sample` output of hung `cua-driver mcp`:

```
Call graph:
    826 Thread_66666   DispatchQueue_1: com.apple.main-thread  (serial)
    + 826 start  (in libdyld.dylib)
    +   826 static CuaDriverEntryPoint.main()  (in cua-driver)
    +     826 protocol witness for ParsableCommand.run() in conformance MCPCommand
    +       826 static MainActor.assumeIsolated<A>(_:file:line:)
    +         826 AppKitBootstrap.runBlockingAppKitWith(_:)
    +           826 -[NSApplication run]
    +             826 -[NSApplication nextEventMatchingMask:untilDate:inMode:dequeue:]
    +               826 _DPSNextEvent
    +                 826 _BlockUntilNextEventMatchingListInMode
    +                   826 RunCurrentEventLoopInMode
    +                     826 mach_msg2_trap
```

The process is stuck in `NSApplication.run()` → `mach_msg2_trap`, running a full AppKit event loop. It never sets up stdin as a run loop source, so MCP messages on stdin are never read.

### `cua-driver serve` has the same problem:

```
ServeCommand.run()
  → AppKitBootstrap.runBlockingAppKitWith()
    → NSApplication.run()
      → mach_msg2_trap
```

When run directly (not via LaunchServices), `serve` also enters AppKit path and never creates the Unix socket.

### Working scenarios (non-MCP):

- `open -n -g -a CuaDriver --args serve` — works, creates socket ✅
- `cua-driver call list_windows` — works when daemon is running ✅
- `cua-driver call screenshot` — works with specific window_id ✅

## Key Observation

The `mcp` command goes through `AppKitBootstrap.runBlockingAppKitWith` and enters `NSApplication.run()`. On the working M3 machine, despite likely going through the same AppKit path, stdin IS processed and MCP responses are returned. On the M4 machine, stdin is never added to the run loop as a readable source.

The binary is byte-identical between the two machines.

## Possible Direction

The `AppKitBootstrap.runBlockingAppKitWith` path seems to fail to register stdin (or the daemon socket proxy) as a run loop source on M4 Mac mini. This could be related to:
- How `AppKitBootstrap` detects the execution context on different hardware
- A race condition in the daemon auto-launch + proxy setup
- M4-specific behavior in NSApplication event loop initialization

title: fix(cua-driver-rs): proxy MCP through daemon on Windows/Linux when one is up
body:
## Summary

\`cua-driver mcp\` is the entrypoint Claude Code (and every other MCP client) spawns. On macOS it can optionally proxy through a LaunchServices-attributed daemon so TCC bundle-id grants apply. On Windows and Linux the proxy was a no-op — \`should_use_daemon_proxy\` hard-coded \`false\` — which meant the in-process MCP server always ran in the calling session.

**Concretely on Windows**: an \`cua-driver mcp\` spawned by Claude Code over SSH lands in **Session 0** (the sshd service session). Session 0 has no desktop attached, so the window/UIA/screen tools return empty regardless of whether a daemon is up in the user's Session 1+. The \`cua-driver call\` CLI did not have this problem because \`run_call\` already had its own \`is_daemon_listening\` shortcut, but \`mcp\` (the path Claude Code actually uses) didn't.

## Repro live on the Windows VM today

\`\`\`
# Daemon running in Session 2 (RDP user's interactive session)
\$ ssh winvm 'cua-driver call list_apps' | head
{ "apps": [ {"pid": 3040, "name": "cua-driver.exe", "running": true},
            {"pid": 11552, "name": "WindowsTerminal.exe", "running": true},
            {"pid": 9956, "name": "Windows PowerShell ISE (x86)", "running": true},
            {"pid": 10516, "name": "Microsoft Edge", "running": true},
            {"pid": 2748, "name": "explorer.exe", "running": true} ] }

# Claude Code, via the SAME stdio MCP transport:
\$ ssh winvm 'claude --print "List running apps via cua-driver"'
"No apps have running:true in the listing."
\`\`\`

Before this fix: claude's spawned \`cua-driver mcp\` ran in-process in Session 0 → saw no desktop apps. After: it proxies through the Session-2 daemon → sees what \`call\` already sees.

## What changed

- **\`crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs\` \`should_use_daemon_proxy\` non-macOS branch**: returns \`true\` when \`is_daemon_listening\` finds a daemon on the default socket. Same opt-out knobs as macOS (\`--no-daemon-relaunch\`, \`CUA_DRIVER_RS_MCP_NO_RELAUNCH\`); plus \`CUA_DRIVER_RS_MCP_FORCE_PROXY\` for test harnesses.
- **\`crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs\` \`run_mcp_via_daemon_proxy\`**: drop the \`#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]\` gate. The macOS-only auto-launch step (\`launch_daemon_and_wait\` → \`open -n -g -a CuaDriver\`) stays macOS-only. On Linux/Windows, when no daemon is up, we bail with an actionable error pointing at \`cua-driver autostart enable && kick\` rather than silently falling through to a Session-0-attributed in-process server.
- **\`crates/cua-driver/src/main.rs\` non-macOS Mcp arm**: now calls the proxy router (mirroring the macOS arm).

## Test plan

- [x] macOS \`cargo check -p cua-driver\` — clean
- [ ] Windows PR pre-release-binaries CI builds the artifact (this PR is the test)
- [ ] Install the resulting binary on the Windows VM, daemon already in Session 2 via \`autostart kick\`, run \`claude --print "List running apps via cua-driver"\` from SSH — should now see real GUI apps
- [ ] \`cua-driver mcp --no-daemon-relaunch\` opt-out still runs in-process

## Related

- Built on top of #1567 (TCC cache re-exec) and the macOS daemon-proxy infrastructure from PRs #1525/#1479-equivalent.
- The Windows SSH workflow we verified end-to-end today depends on this fix to be useful for actual Claude Code usage.

title: chore(deps): bump ws from 8.18.3 to 8.20.1 in /examples/computer-example-ts
body:
Bumps [ws](https://github.com/websockets/ws) from 8.18.3 to 8.20.1.
Release notes

Sourced from ws's releases.

8.20.1

Bug fixes

  • Fixed an uninitialized memory disclosure issue in websocket.close() (c0327ec1).

Providing a TypedArray (e.g. Float32Array) as the reason argument for websocket.close(), rather than the supported string or Buffer types, caused uninitialized memory to be disclosed to the remote peer.

import { deepStrictEqual } from 'node:assert';
import { WebSocket, WebSocketServer } from 'ws';

const wss = new WebSocketServer(
{ port: 0, skipUTF8Validation: true },
function () {
const { port } = wss.address();
const ws = new WebSocket(ws://localhost:${port}, {
skipUTF8Validation: true
});


ws.on('close', function (code, reason) {
  deepStrictEqual(reason, Buffer.alloc(80));
});



}
);


wss.on('connection', function (ws) {
ws.close(1000, new Float32Array(20));
});

The issue was privately reported by Nikita Skovoroda.

title: screenshot tool returns native-resolution images incompatible with click coordinate system (+ two related bugs)
body:
## Summary

Three bugs discovered during a real agent session using `cua-driver` CLI (v0.1.9) to smoke-test a macOS Tauri app. The session involved ~60 CUA calls over 5+ hours. The agent repeatedly failed to click targets in a native Open File dialog despite correctly identifying them in screenshots.

## Bug 1 (High): `screenshot` ↔ `click` coordinate space mismatch on Retina

### Problem

`screenshot` returns images at **native Retina resolution** (2× logical), while `click`'s x/y coordinates are designed to work with images from `get_window_state`, which applies `max_image_dimension` resizing and registers the ratio in `ImageResizeRegistry`.

An agent that uses `screenshot` to see the screen and then calls `click` with pixel coordinates from that image will miss every target.

### Evidence

```
$ cua-driver call list_windows ...
  → window_id=135, bounds: 720×813 (logical points)

$ cua-driver call screenshot '{"window_id": 135}' --screenshot-out-file /tmp/test.png
  → 1440×1626 PNG (native 2× resolution)
```

Same window, different resolutions. The `click` tool has no way to know which image the coordinates came from.

### Root cause

- `ScreenshotTool.swift` calls `captureWindow(windowID:, format:, quality:)` **without** `maxImageDimension` — defaults to 0 (no resize)
- `GetWindowStateTool.swift` calls `captureWindow(...)` **with** `maxImageDimension: config.maxImageDimension` and registers the resize ratio in `ImageResizeRegistry`
- `ClickTool.swift` reads from `ImageResizeRegistry` to reverse the resize — but `screenshot` never populates this registry

### Reproduction

```bash
# 1. Get a window
cua-driver call list_windows '{"on_screen_only": true}'
# Note bounds width/height (logical points)

# 2. screenshot returns native (2x) resolution
cua-driver call screenshot '{"window_id": WID}' --screenshot-out-file /tmp/raw.png
file /tmp/raw.png  # Shows 2x logical dimensions

# 3. get_window_state returns resized resolution  
cua-driver call get_window_state '{"pid": PID, "window_id": WID}'
# screenshot_width/height capped at max_image_dimension=1568

# 4. Click using screenshot coordinates — misses the target
```

### Proposed fix

`ScreenshotTool` should apply `maxImageDimension` and register the ratio in `ImageResizeRegistry`, matching `get_window_state` behavior. Alternatively, `ClickTool` should detect when no resize ratio exists and handle native-resolution coordinates correctly.

---

## Bug 2 (Medium): Every `click` reports "Action opened new window(s): Cua Driver"

### Problem

Every `click` response includes:
```
🪟 Action opened new window(s): Cua Driver.
```

This is the `AgentCursorOverlayWindow` being detected as a "new window" by `WindowChangeDetector`.

### Root cause

`ClickTool` calls `WindowChangeDetector.snapshot()` → `AgentCursor.animateAndWait()` (creates overlay) → `detectChanges()` (sees overlay as new). After 8s idle-hide (`idleHideDelay`), the cycle repeats on next click.

### Proposed fix

`WindowChangeDetector` should filter out windows owned by the cua-driver daemon's own PID.

---

## Bug 3 (Medium): `type_text` targets wrong AX element in modal sheet context

### Problem

With a macOS Open dialog showing a "Go to Folder" sheet, `type_text` inserted text into the sidebar's `AXOutline` instead of the sheet's text field:

```
✅ Inserted 20 char(s) into focused AXOutline "" on pid 89422 via AX.
```

### Root cause

`TypeTextTool` uses `AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue(root, "AXFocusedUIElement")` on the application root. macOS AX focus tracking for sheet hierarchies can lag — the previous focused element (sidebar AXOutline) retains focus status even after the sheet appears.

### Proposed fix

Before writing, validate the focused element's role. If it's `AXOutline`/`AXTable`/`AXList` (non-text containers), return an error suggesting `element_index` targeting instead.

---

## Environment

- cua-driver v0.1.9 (`/Applications/CuaDriver.app`)
- macOS Darwin 25.4.0, display 1440×932 @ 2.0× Retina
- Target app: Tauri 2 desktop app with native Open File dialogs

title: feat(cua-driver-rs): add kill_app tool for force-terminate by pid (closes CUA-541)
body:
## Summary

Adds a new \`kill_app\` MCP tool that force-terminates a process by pid. \`taskkill /F\` on Windows, \`kill -9\` on macOS / Linux. Cross-platform tool surface (registered on all three platforms + the cross-platform stub).

## Why

From today's WINDOWS_CLAUDE_CODE_TEST_PLAN.md Test G live run:

> \"3 × CalculatorApp.exe (pids 12452, 7760, 8572) — Alt+F4 was accepted but the windows do not close; these look like backgrounded UWP instances. cua-driver does not expose a force-kill primitive.\"

cua-driver's only window-close mechanism on Windows is the cooperative path — \`click\` on the X button or a hand-rolled hotkey gesture, which sends \`WM_CLOSE\` via PostMessage. UWP / WinUI3 apps (Calculator, Photos, Settings, Win11 Notepad) treat \`WM_CLOSE\` as \"minimize to suspended state\" rather than exit. Cleanup tests leave orphan processes that survive every polite eviction attempt.

\`kill_app\` is the escalation: skip cooperative close, terminate the process directly.

## What changed

- **Windows** (\`crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs\`):
  \`OpenProcess(PROCESS_TERMINATE | PROCESS_SYNCHRONIZE)\` + \`TerminateProcess(h, 1)\` + \`WaitForSingleObject(h, 2000)\`. The \`PROCESS_SYNCHRONIZE\` right + 2-second wait means the caller's follow-up \`list_apps\` reflects the change immediately. Runs on a \`spawn_blocking\` thread.
- **macOS** (\`crates/platform-macos/src/tools/kill_app.rs\`, new file): \`libc::kill(pid, SIGKILL)\`. Synchronous. Surfaces \`EPERM\` / \`ESRCH\` via \`std::io::Error::last_os_error()\`.
- **Linux** (\`crates/platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs\`): same \`libc::kill(pid, SIGKILL)\`. Adds \`libc = \"0.2\"\` to \`platform-linux/Cargo.toml\` (the crate didn't depend on libc directly before).
- **Stubs** (\`stubs.rs\` in both platform crates): register \`KillAppTool\` so non-target builds get the standard \"not implemented\" error.

Schema: single \`pid: integer\` argument. Bounds-checked at the tool boundary (must be positive, must fit in i32/u32). Marked \`destructive: true\` so MCP clients with permission gating prompt before invoking.

## Test plan

- [x] macOS \`cargo check -p platform-macos\` clean
- [x] Windows: built on the VM (incremental ~23s), reinstalled, daemon picked up the new binary
- [x] \`cua-driver list-tools\` shows \`kill_app: Force-terminate a process by pid\`
- [x] Happy path: 3 cmd.exe processes spawned via \`Start-Process\`, killed via \`cua-driver call kill_app '{\"pid\":<n>}'\` (JSON via stdin so PowerShell doesn't eat quotes) — all 3 terminated cleanly, post-kill \`Get-Process\` confirms gone.
- [x] Error path: \`kill_app\` against a bogus PID (999999) returns actionable message with the real Win32 error code (\`0x80070057 ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER\`).
- [ ] Cross-session: daemon in Session 1+ killing Session-0 processes works (the SSH-test confirmed this; daemon at PID 13088/Session 2 terminated cmd.exe processes at Session 0).

## Notes

The first push hit an \`E0283\` (\`.into()\` ambiguity from a transitive bytes/zune crate impl in the Windows tree). Fixed in the follow-up commit by switching to explicit \`.to_string()\`. macOS / Linux didn't hit it locally but the fix is preemptive for those too.

Closes CUA-541. Three sibling issues from the same WINDOWS_CLAUDE_CODE_TEST_PLAN.md run are filed as:
- CUA-542 (screenshot black on UWP DirectComposition — needs WGC fallback) — \`High\`
- CUA-543 (type_text/hotkey PostMessage doesn't reach XAML targets — needs SendInput / UIA-pattern routing) — \`High\`
- CUA-544 (UIA tree empty after first snapshot on Calculator) — \`Medium\`

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): screenshot of background-collapsed UWP windows (Calculator) returns wrong-size capture — WGC needed
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to PR #1599 which routed XAML/UWP screenshots through screen-region BitBlt instead of PrintWindow. That fix covers the **visible-at-real-size UWP** case (Edge / Photos / Settings / foreground modern Notepad). It does NOT cover the **background-collapsed UWP** case typified by Windows 11 Calculator launched via \`SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE\`.

## Repro

Live on the Windows VM:

\`\`\`powershell
'{\"aumid\":\"Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App\"}' | cua-driver call launch_app
cua-driver call list_windows  # for Calculator's pid
# bounds: { width: 120, height: 30, x: 0, y: 1 }  ← collapsed
\`\`\`

Calculator's top-level HWND persistently reports 120×30 at (0,1) — not its rendered UI dimensions; the real Calculator content lives in a separate compositor-managed CoreWindow that GDI APIs cannot reach.

Workarounds that **don't work**:
- \`SetWindowPos\` + \`ShowWindow(SW_RESTORE)\` + \`SetForegroundWindow\`
- PrintWindow on the top-level HWND → 120×30 PNG of the title bar
- Screen-region BitBlt → same 120×30 region
- Enumerating child HWNDs → no addressable child window contains the real UI

## Cause

Windows 11 UWP/WinUI3 apps render content through DirectComposition / Windows.UI.Composition. The visible UI is a \`GraphicsCaptureItem\` in the compositor's tree, not an HWND in the window manager. GDI APIs only see HWND-backed surfaces.

## Proper fix: Windows.Graphics.Capture (WGC)

\`Windows.Graphics.Capture::GraphicsCaptureItem::CreateForWindow(hwnd)\` works against the composited output regardless of HWND back-buffer. Same API the Windows Snipping Tool uses. Available on Windows 10 1903+.

Implementation outline (~250-300 LOC):
- WinRT API: \`windows::Graphics::Capture\` + \`windows::Graphics::DirectX::Direct3D11\` + \`windows::Win32::Graphics::Direct3D11\`
- Create \`Direct3D11Device\`, build \`GraphicsCaptureItem::CreateForWindow(hwnd)\`, \`Direct3D11CaptureFramePool\`, register frame-arrived callback, grab next frame, copy BGRA bytes
- Threading: WGC frame arrival is async via WinRT \`AsyncOperation\`; bridge to tokio or block-wait

Routing in \`platform-windows/src/capture.rs::screenshot_window_bytes_unsafe\`:
- \`is_xaml_host_hwnd(hwnd)\` → prefer WGC over screen-region
- Fall through to screen-region if WGC init fails (old Windows, no GPU in CI, etc.)
- Legacy Win32 stays on PrintWindow

## Coverage matrix (after WGC ships)

| Case | PrintWindow | screen-region (PR #1599) | WGC (this issue) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Legacy Win32, visible | ✅ | n/a | ✅ |
| Legacy Win32, off-screen | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
| UWP/WinUI3, visible at real size | ❌ (black) | ✅ | ✅ |
| **UWP/WinUI3, background-collapsed (Calculator)** | ❌ wrong size | ❌ wrong size | ✅ |
| UWP/WinUI3, off-screen or minimized | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

## Acceptance

- Screenshot of background-launched Calculator returns its real UI (not 120×30)
- Existing test coverage for legacy Win32 + visible-UWP still passes
- WGC failure path falls back to screen-region / PrintWindow chain

## Context

Spawned from today's WINDOWS_CLAUDE_CODE_TEST_PLAN.md Test C + iteration log in PR #1599. cua-driver-rs v0.2.7+ on the Windows VM.

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): Calculator (and likely other restricted-UIA UWP apps) returns sparse 1-element tree from get_window_state — UIPI ceiling
body:
## Summary

Originally reported in WINDOWS_CLAUDE_CODE_TEST_PLAN.md Test C as \"UIA stopped yielding a tree after the first snapshot\". Investigation on 2026-05-20 shows the real shape is different:

> Calculator's UIA tree is **consistently sparse** (1 element — just the root \`Windows.UI.Core.CoreWindow\`) on every \`get_window_state\` call, regardless of call order, regardless of whether Calculator is foreground or background.

The \"empty after first snapshot\" framing was likely a one-time observation artifact when claude saw a fuller tree once and then saw nothing on the next call (possibly because Calculator's UIA provider populated, then went quiet). Repro on the VM today: never saw a fuller tree.

## Comparison data (live VM, today)

\`cua-driver call get_window_state\` element_count for fresh UWP apps:

| App | element_count | UIA accessibility |
|---|---|---|
| **Modern Notepad** (\`notepad.exe\`) | 30 | full tree with Document, tabs, menus, command bar |
| **Settings** (\`SystemSettings.exe\`) | 75 | full tree |
| **Calculator** (\`CalculatorApp.exe\`) | **1** | only the root CoreWindow |

So this is Calculator-specific (and possibly other restricted UWP apps with similar attribution requirements), not a general daemon bug.

## Likely cause: UIPI / uiAccess gating

Calculator's UWP UIA provider appears to be gated such that only callers with \`uiAccess=\"true\"\` in their manifest (a signed-binary + UAC-elevated invariant) get the full XAML accessibility tree. External UIA clients running at normal Medium integrity see only the bare \`CoreWindow\` root.

Same Win11 UIPI ceiling as the \`SendInput\` → \`ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED\` problem documented in CUA-543. The mitigations are heavy (manifest, Authenticode signing, UAC elevation) and harm install ergonomics.

## What this means for agents

For Calculator specifically: \`click\`, \`type_text\`, and \`hotkey\` all require an element_index in the cache, which requires \`get_window_state\` to populate that cache. With element_count=1, the only element addressable is the CoreWindow root — useless for driving Calculator's buttons.

Workarounds:
- **Vision-mode (pixel coordinates)**: claude can screenshot Calculator (once #1600 / WGC ships) and click button pixel positions directly. No UIA needed.
- **Different calculator**: Win32 calc.exe (if available — Win 11 routes it to UWP) or a third-party calculator app would have a normal accessibility tree.
- **Don't use Calculator as a test target**: pick UWP apps with normal UIA exposure (Settings, Mail, Photos, modern Notepad — all work).

## Acceptance (for closing this issue)

If the project ships \`uiAccess=\"true\"\` for cua-driver via a signed manifest + elevation: Calculator's tree becomes accessible. Otherwise the limit is fundamental and we should:
- Update tool docs to flag Calculator-like apps as vision-mode-only
- WINDOWS_CLAUDE_CODE_TEST_PLAN.md Test C ought to be revised to NOT use Calculator (use Settings or another normally-accessible UWP)

## Context

Spawned from PR #1597 / #1599 iteration on the Windows VM. Diagnostic tool \`debug_window_info\` (shipped in PR #1597) was used for the investigation. cua-driver-rs v0.2.7+.

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): ship with uiAccess="true" manifest + signed binary to unblock UWP automation (SendInput / UIA against Calculator-class apps)
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver-rs` on Windows ships **unsigned**, **un-manifested**, and installs into a **user-writable path** (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\trycua\cua-driver-rs\bin`). It therefore runs at Medium integrity and cannot:

1. `SendInput` against UWP / AppContainer targets — fails with `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (UIPI).
2. Read the full UIA tree of restricted UWP apps — Calculator returns 1 element vs. ~30 for Notepad (#1601).
3. Drive XAML keyboard shortcuts routed through accessibility for those same apps.

The Win32 escape hatch is `uiAccess="true"` in an embedded manifest. This issue scopes what each layer would cost so the maintainer can make a go/no-go call.

Motivating cases: #1600 (background-collapsed Calculator capture) and #1601 (sparse UIA tree).

## 1. Microsoft requirements for `uiAccess="true"` to take effect

All three must hold — failing any one silently downgrades to a normal Medium-integrity launch.

| Requirement | Detail | Microsoft source |
|---|---|---|
| **Embedded manifest** | `<requestedExecutionLevel level="asInvoker" uiAccess="true"/>` inside `<requestedPrivileges>` inside `<trustInfo xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:asm.v3">`. Must be a binary resource, not a side-by-side `.exe.manifest`. | [Application Manifests: `requestedExecutionLevel`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sbscs/application-manifests#requestedexecutionlevel) |
| **Authenticode signed** | Cert must chain to a CA in the machine's Trusted Root store. Ad-hoc / self-signed do not pass AIS at launch. | [UIPI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/user-account-control/how-user-account-control-works#user-interface-privilege-isolation-uipi); [`uiAccess` attribute](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sbscs/application-manifests#uiaccess) |
| **Secure location** | `\Program Files\`, `\Program Files (x86)\`, `\Windows\system32\`. `%LOCALAPPDATA%` / `%USERPROFILE%` / `%TEMP%` are not secure. | [Setting `uiAccess`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthz/setting-the-uiaccess-flag) |
| **(Optional) relaxation** | `HKLM\…\Policies\System\EnableSecureUIAPaths=0` disables the secure-location check. Machine-wide, admin-only, dev-convenience only — not for end-user shipping. | [`EnableSecureUIAPaths` policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/security-policy-settings/user-account-control-only-elevate-uiaccess-applications-that-are-installed-in-secure-locations) |

There is also a `SendInput` runtime check: cross-integrity / AppContainer-`windowInputBlock` targets reject input unless the caller's token carries the `UIAccess` flag, which is set only when the three conditions above hold. ([SendInput input blocking](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-sendinput))

## 2. Current cua-driver-rs state

| Stage | State | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Install path** | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\trycua\cua-driver-rs\bin` (junction chain into `%USERPROFILE%\.cua-driver-rs\packages\…`). Sudo-free. **Not a secure location.** | `libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.ps1:110` |
| **Windows signing in CD** | None. `build-windows` runs `cargo build --release` and zips. No `signtool`, no cert import, no `AzureSignTool`. | `.github/workflows/cd-rust-cua-driver.yml:89-154` |
| **Embedded manifest** | None. No `.manifest` in tree; zero hits for `winres` / `embed-manifest` / `embed_resource`. No `build.rs` on the `platform-windows` or `cua-driver` crates (only `platform-macos` has one). Binary ships with Rust's default manifest (no `trustInfo`). | `find libs/cua-driver-rs -name "*.manifest"` → empty |
| **macOS parallel** | Apple `Developer ID Application` cert via `APPLICATION_CERT_BASE64` / `CERT_PASSWORD` / `DEVELOPER_NAME` / `TEAM_ID` / `APPLE_ID` / `APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD`. **Apple-issued — does NOT chain to any Windows-trusted root, cannot be reused for Authenticode.** | `.github/workflows/cd-rust-cua-driver.yml:183-210` |

## 3. Implementation plan

### 3a. Manifest authoring — `libs/cua-driver-rs/crates/cua-driver/resources/cua-driver.manifest`

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>
<assembly xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:asm.v1" manifestVersion="1.0">
  <trustInfo xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:asm.v3">
    <security>
      <requestedPrivileges>
        <requestedExecutionLevel level="asInvoker" uiAccess="true"/>
      </requestedPrivileges>
    </security>
  </trustInfo>
  <compatibility xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:compatibility.v1">
    <application>
      <supportedOS Id="{8e0f7a12-bfb3-4fe8-b9a5-48fd50a15a9a}"/> <!-- Win 10 -->
      <supportedOS Id="{1f676c76-80e1-4239-95bb-83d0f6d0da78}"/> <!-- Win 11 -->
    </application>
  </compatibility>
</assembly>
```

### 3b. Manifest embedding

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| **`embed-manifest` crate (recommended)** | Pure-Rust build-script; no Windows SDK on runners; one-line `embed_manifest_file(…)`. | Adds a `build.rs` to `cua-driver`. |
| `winres` / `embed-resource` | Mature; can also embed icon + version info. | Pulls `rc.exe`. |
| Post-build `mt.exe` | No Rust dep. | Requires Windows SDK; extra CI step. |

Pick `embed-manifest` — smallest moving part.

### 3c. Code signing

Cua AI **does not** currently have a Windows cert (CD only imports Apple's). Apple certs cannot be reused for Authenticode. Required: a new Windows code-signing cert.

| Cert | Behavior | Cost/yr (estimate, validate with vendor) | Lead time | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **OV** | SmartScreen "unrecognized" until reputation builds. UIPI honored. | ~$200–500 | ~1–5 business days | Since June 2023, all OV+ certs are HSM-only — must use cloud HSM (Azure Key Vault, SSL.com eSigner, DigiCert KeyLocker) or USB token (impractical for CI). |
| **EV** | No SmartScreen warning day 1; instant reputation. UIPI honored. | ~$300–700 | ~1–3 weeks | Same HSM requirement. Strictly better if budget allows. |

**Recommended:** EV cert via Azure Key Vault + [`AzureSignTool`](https://github.com/vcsjones/AzureSignTool) in CD (no PFX on the runner).

**New CI secrets:** `AZURE_KEYVAULT_URI`, `AZURE_KEYVAULT_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_KEYVAULT_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_KEYVAULT_CLIENT_SECRET` (or GitHub→Azure OIDC), `AZURE_KEYVAULT_CERTIFICATE_NAME`.

### 3d. Install path

| Option | Effect | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Force `C:\Program Files\trycua\`** | Secure location everywhere. | Breaks `irm \| iex` no-admin install for everyone. |
| **B. Default keeps `%LOCALAPPDATA%`; opt-in `-AdminMode` drops into `\Program Files\`** | Un-elevated users (the 80%) keep current path; UIPI-bypass users opt in. | Two install modes; doc/branching complexity. |
| **C. Toggle `EnableSecureUIAPaths`** | Single install mode. | Machine-wide HKLM policy change; admin-once; should not be a default. |

**Recommended:** B.

### 3e. CD pipeline changes (`.github/workflows/cd-rust-cua-driver.yml`)

```yaml
# new step in build-windows after cargo build --release:
- name: Sign cua-driver.exe (Authenticode + timestamp)
  env:
    AZURE_KEYVAULT_URI: ${{ secrets.AZURE_KEYVAULT_URI }}
    AZURE_KEYVAULT_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_KEYVAULT_CLIENT_ID }}
    AZURE_KEYVAULT_TENANT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_KEYVAULT_TENANT_ID }}
    AZURE_KEYVAULT_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.AZURE_KEYVAULT_CLIENT_SECRET }}
    AZURE_KEYVAULT_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.AZURE_KEYVAULT_CERTIFICATE_NAME }}
  run: |
    dotnet tool install --global AzureSignTool
    AzureSignTool sign `
      -kvu $env:AZURE_KEYVAULT_URI `
      -kvi $env:AZURE_KEYVAULT_CLIENT_ID `
      -kvt $env:AZURE_KEYVAULT_TENANT_ID `
      -kvs $env:AZURE_KEYVAULT_CLIENT_SECRET `
      -kvc $env:AZURE_KEYVAULT_CERTIFICATE `
      -tr http://timestamp.digicert.com -td sha256 `
      target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/cua-driver.exe
- name: Verify signature
  run: signtool verify /pa /v target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/cua-driver.exe
```

Manifest embedding is compile-time via `build.rs` — no separate CI step.

### 3f. Install ergonomics regression

| | Today | Default (Option B) | `-AdminMode` (Option B) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Install time | ~10s, no admin | Same | ~30s + UAC prompt |
| Locked-down corporate users can install | ~100% | Same | ~50% (admin gate) |
| Calculator-class apps | vision-mode only | Same | full UIA + SendInput |

The `-AdminMode` path is realistically a power-user toggle.

## 4. Cost-benefit summary

| | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Gain** | `SendInput` works against UWP; Calculator-class UIA trees readable (closes #1601); WGC capture (#1600) may benefit from same elevation; XAML hotkey routing feasible. |
| **One-time cost** | ~1 week CI + manifest + install-mode work; cert procurement ~1–3 weeks lead time (validate with vendor); AzureSignTool wiring ~1–2 days. |
| **Recurring cost** | ~$300–700/yr cert (estimate, validate with vendor). |
| **Support-matrix cost** | Two install modes; signed-vs-unsigned-daemon branching in docs; cert renewal calendar. |
| **User-ergonomics cost** | ~50% of corporate users lose no-admin install for the UIPI-bypass mode (acceptable — they keep the default). |

**Alternatives:**

1. **Stay un-elevated**, document Calculator-class apps as vision-mode-only (current state, already captured in #1601). Most UWP apps (Settings, Mail, Photos, modern Notepad) work fine without elevation. **Probably right for v1.x.**
2. **Re-use the Apple Developer ID** — verified **not possible**. Apple-issued certs do not chain to any Microsoft-trusted root.
3. **Free OSS cert via [SignPath.io](https://signpath.io/) Foundation tier** — worth checking eligibility before paying for an EV cert; would zero the recurring cost.

## 5. Acceptance test

On a Win 10/11 VM with signed + manifested + `\Program Files\`-installed daemon, from a normal Medium-integrity PowerShell:

```powershell
'{"aumid":"Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App"}' | cua-driver call launch_app
cua-driver call get_window_state --filter-pid <calc-pid>   # element_count > 1
cua-driver call click --element-index <some-button>        # success
```

Win32-layer asserts:

- `GetTokenInformation(TokenUIAccess)` on the daemon's process token returns `1`.
- `SendInput` against a Calculator-owned thread returns the input count, not `0` + `GetLastError() == ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (5)`.
- `signtool verify /pa cua-driver.exe` reports a valid chain to a trusted root.
- Daemon `.exe` resides under `%ProgramFiles%\trycua\…`.

New integration test under `libs/cua-driver-rs/tests/` asserts the first two via direct Win32 calls so regressions (re-signing with untrusted cert, dropping manifest, moving install path) fail CI.

## Recommendation

Default position: **do nothing for v1.x.** Document Calculator-class restrictions in the WINDOWS skill and #1601. Revisit when a customer pain point shows up that vision-mode cannot cover — at that point this is a 1–2-week implementation project on top of a 1–3-week cert procurement lead.

Closes (conditional on shipping): #1600 (partial — capture), #1601 (full).

title: computer-use: repeated printable keypresses are layout-dependent (Finder path entry breaks under non-Latin layouts)
body:
## Summary

Repeated printable `keypress` input can become layout-dependent instead of text-stable on all backends (macOS, Linux, Windows, Android, VNC).

If the active input source is Russian, Cyrillic, or any other non-Latin layout, an agent that enters a Finder path via repeated printable keypresses can type the wrong characters into `Go to Folder`.

`type_text` is already layout-independent. The bug is that the computer-use stack still allows text-like entry to go through `keypress`.

## Repro

1. Switch macOS input source to Russian.
2. Open Finder.
3. Trigger `Cmd+Shift+G`.
4. Have an agent enter an ASCII path character by character using `keypress` actions (one key per action, no modifiers).
5. The field receives Cyrillic/wrong characters instead of the intended ASCII path.

Example expected path:

```text
/Users/me/tmp
```

Actual result under a Russian layout is layout-mapped text, not the ASCII path.

## Root cause

- The agent/computer-use stack allows free-form text to be expressed as repeated `keypress` actions.
- In `computer_server.main`, the `DirectComputer.keypress()` method (`main.py:1156`) routes single-part keys to `press_key` and multi-part combos to `hotkey`. There is no branch that redirects a single printable no-modifier key to `type_text`.
- `press_key` on every backend sends characters through a physical-key or keycode path that follows the active input source: pynput `keyboard.press/release` on macOS/Linux/Windows, `adb shell input keyevent` on Android, X11 keysym on VNC.
- `type_text` on every backend uses a text-insertion path that does not depend on the active input source: pynput `keyboard.type()` on macOS/Linux/Windows, `adb shell input text` on Android, VNC `type_text()`.
- Tool descriptions and action mapping do not clearly fence `keypress` off from free-form text entry, so the layout-dependent path is easy to hit in practice.

## Proposed fix

Use layout-independent text insertion for text.

- Computer-use / agent side: document and enforce that free-form text, paths, and filenames must use `type` / `type_text`, not repeated printable `keypress`.
- Handler side: when `keypress` resolves to exactly one printable key with no modifiers, route it through text insertion instead of physical-key semantics.

Do not switch the user's system input source as the main fix. That is global state, user-visible, and failure-prone.

## Test plan

- macOS with U.S. layout: a single printable `keypress` action (e.g. `keypress("a")`) inserts the intended character
- macOS with Russian layout: the same `keypress("a")` action inserts `a`, not the layout-mapped Cyrillic character
- Finder `Cmd+Shift+G` then character-by-character path entry via `keypress` works under both U.S. and Russian layouts
- Non-printable keys (`keypress("return")`, arrows, tab, escape) still behave unchanged
- Modifier combos (`hotkey(["cmd","c"])`, `hotkey(["cmd","shift","g"])`) still behave unchanged

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): hotkey accelerators silently no-op on modern XAML/UWP hosts (PostMessage vs CoreInput dispatcher)
body:
## Symptom

When `cua-driver hotkey` is invoked against a modern XAML/UWP host (e.g. modern Notepad, Settings), the keystroke is delivered but the application's accelerator handler never fires. From the user's perspective the call returns success ("✅ Pressed ctrl+s on pid ...") but nothing happens.

Concretely: sending `Ctrl+S` to modern Notepad does not open the Save dialog.

## Reproduction

1. Launch modern Notepad via `cua-driver call launch_app '{"aumid":"Microsoft.WindowsNotepad_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App"}'`
2. `cua-driver call hotkey '{"pid":..., "window_id":..., "key":"ctrl+s"}'` — returns success
3. `list_windows` for that pid still shows 1 window. No dialog. The asterisk-prefixed title (`*untitled - Notepad`) confirms no save flow ran.

## Root cause

`hotkey` posts `WM_KEYDOWN` / `WM_KEYUP` via `PostMessage(target_hwnd, ...)` (`crates/platform-windows/src/input/keyboard.rs::post_key`). Regular Win32 apps consume keystrokes off their message queue, so this works.

Modern Notepad — and other XAML/WinUI 3 hosts — route input through the **CoreInput dispatcher**, which only pulls keystrokes off the **system input queue** (where `SendInput` puts them). Posted-via-`PostMessage` keystrokes are delivered but treated as inert by the dispatcher. No accelerator binding runs.

This is the same architectural mismatch that drove the `type_text` → UIA `ValuePattern.SetValue` rewrite in #1597 — `hotkey` is the deferred half of that fix.

## Suggested fix paths

1. **UIA `InvokePattern` on accelerator command** (mirrors the `type_text` heuristic). Walk the target window's UIA tree for elements with `AcceleratorKey == "Ctrl+S"` (or whatever the requested combo is) and invoke them directly. Works for any XAML target that advertises accelerators in its UIA tree.
2. **`SendInput` fallback for XAML hosts**, with focus-steal trade-off. `is_xaml_host_hwnd` (already in `input/keyboard.rs`) gates the dispatch.
3. **UIA menu-walk for known shortcuts**: for common cases like Save (`Ctrl+S`), Find (`Ctrl+F`), etc., locate the matching menu item by name + Invoke it. More fragile but no focus theft.

Path 1 is the cleanest and matches the type_text approach.

## Workaround

Until fixed, the right way to drive a XAML host's Save flow is to enumerate the UIA tree, find the "Save" menu/button element, and call `click` (which is already UIA-Invoke-based). Document this in the autostart / mcp-tools pages alongside the existing UIA-routing notes.

## Related

- #1597 — `type_text` UIA ValuePattern routing (already merged; same root cause, different action)
- #1604 — cua-driver-uia worker (gives us UIAccess integrity but doesn't help here — issue is dispatch mechanism, not UIPI)

title: fix(get_window_state): 30s timeout + 2000-node cap for heavy webview apps
body:
## Problem

`get_window_state` hangs forever on Arc, Safari with many tabs, and Electron apps because `AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue` blocks indefinitely via XPC when the app's accessibility tree is pathologically large.

## Fix

**Rust (`get_window_state.rs` + `ax/tree.rs`):**
- Wrap `spawn_blocking` AX walk in `tokio::time::timeout(30s)`. Returns a descriptive error suggesting `capture_mode=vision` or a query filter.
- Add `MAX_ELEMENTS=2000` cap to `walk_element`. When hit, the walk stops early and `TreeWalkResult.truncated=true` is set. The partial tree is returned with a warning line appended to `tree_markdown`.

**Swift (`AppState.swift`):**
- Wrap `renderTree` in `withThrowingTaskGroup` with a 30s deadline task. Throws `AppStateError.axWalkTimedOut(pid:)` on expiry.
- Add `maxElements=2000` cap via `visitedCount` parameter. When hit, appends a warning line to the markdown output.
- `renderTree` is now `nonisolated` so it can run on the detached task.

Both implementations mirror each other: 30s timeout + 2000-node cap with a user-visible warning rather than a silent hang.

Fixes #1537. Addresses #1564.

title: fix(computer-server): route printable single-key keypress through type_text
body:
## Summary

`DirectComputer.keypress()` routes single-part keys to `press_key()`, which sends them as physical keycodes. On non-Latin layouts (Russian, etc.) that means `keypress("a")` produces a layout-mapped character instead of `a`. Real scenario: agent types a Finder path char-by-char under a Russian input source and gets Cyrillic.

`type_text()` on every backend already inserts text without depending on the active layout. This PR adds a guard: when `keypress()` resolves to exactly one printable character (no modifiers), it goes through `type_text()` instead. Named keys, modifier combos, and control characters keep their existing paths.

Closes #1605

## Changes

- `computer_server/main.py`: in `DirectComputer.keypress()`, single printable character (`len == 1`, `isprintable()`) now routes to `type_text()` instead of `press_key()`
- New `tests/test_keypress_routing.py`: 22 unit tests covering printable chars → `type_text`, named keys → `press_key`, control chars → `press_key`, combos → `hotkey`, and Unicode modifier aliases (`⌘`, `⌥`) → `press_key`

## Why this works across backends

The guard sits in `DirectComputer`, which delegates to whichever handler `HandlerFactory` returns. On every backend `press_key` uses a keycode/keysym path (pynput on macOS/Linux/Windows, `adb keyevent` on Android, X11 keysym on VNC), while `type_text` uses a text-insertion path (pynput `.type()`, `adb input text`, VNC `type_text`). The fix is backend-agnostic because the invariant holds everywhere.

## Test plan

- [ ] macOS with Russian layout: `keypress("a")` inserts `a`, not Cyrillic
- [ ] Finder `Cmd+Shift+G` + path entry works under Russian layout

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): hotkey PostMessage doesn't set modifier state — universal Win32 silent-no-op for accelerators
body:
## Symptom

`cua-driver call hotkey '{"keys":["ctrl","s"]}'` against most native Win32 apps (LibreOffice, Notepad++, FAR, etc.) returns `✅ Pressed ctrl+s on pid X` but the shortcut never fires. For LibreOffice specifically: Ctrl+A + Ctrl+B + Ctrl+S in sequence insert literal `abs` into the document (treated as text input, not as accelerators).

## Reproduction

```powershell
'{"aumid":"...soffice.bin or Notepad++"}' | cua-driver call launch_app
# launches; resolve pid + window_id
# Then with active window focused:
'{"pid":..., "window_id":..., "keys":["ctrl","s"]}' | cua-driver call hotkey
# returns "✅ Pressed ctrl+s on pid X" — but no Save dialog opens
```

## Root cause

`PostMessage(WM_KEYDOWN, VK_CONTROL)` does NOT update the system-wide modifier state that apps read via `GetKeyState` / `GetAsyncKeyState`. The accelerator dispatcher (`TranslateAccelerator`, called from the target's main message loop) sees plain `a`/`b`/`s` virtual-key presses with no Ctrl held → routes them through the text-input path.

This was a known limitation of the original PostMessage-based hotkey design. We started moving away from it for **XAML/UWP targets** in #1611 (UIA InvokePattern/TogglePattern on the matched element). But native Win32 targets that use `TranslateAccelerator` (which is most of them) still go through the broken PostMessage path.

## Fix path

`SendInput` from the UIAccess'd worker. `SendInput` puts keystrokes onto the **system input queue** — the same queue `GetKeyState` reads — so the Ctrl modifier propagates correctly. Requires:

1. `AttachThreadInput` to the target's UI thread so `SetFocus` works (or use foreground activation)
2. Optional foreground activation via `SetForegroundWindow` (focus-steal trade-off — but the uia worker has UIAccess so this is permitted without the usual restrictions)
3. `SendInput` with the keystroke sequence (KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY where needed, scancodes for reliability)
4. Optional restoration of previous foreground

The uia worker (cua-driver-uia.exe, TokenUIAccess=1) is the right host because UIAccess-marked processes can `SendInput` to elevated targets and can call `SetForegroundWindow` without user-input-driven activation.

## Workaround

For Win32 toolbars with UIA-exposed buttons: use `click` on the matching toolbar element (UIA Invoke path works reliably). Tested with LibreOffice Save SplitButton — UIA Invoke opens the Save As dialog correctly.

For Win32 menu items: walk the UIA tree to find the matching MenuItem by Name, click that.

## Related

- #1597 — `type_text` UIA ValuePattern for XAML targets (similar architectural fix for the typing path)
- #1611 — `hotkey` UIA InvokePattern/TogglePattern for XAML targets

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): launch_app loses launcher-stub pid chain (GIMP, partial LibreOffice)
body:
## Symptom

`launch_app` against apps whose top-level binary is a **launcher stub** that re-execs into another process returns `pid: X, windows: []` and never surfaces a usable pid/window in `list_apps`. Downstream tools (`list_windows`, `get_window_state`, `click`, `type_text`) can't be exercised because they require a valid pid/window_id.

## Reproduction

```powershell
'{"path":"C:\\Users\\...\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\GIMP 3\\bin\\gimp-3.exe"}' | cua-driver call launch_app
# returns pid: 17984, windows: []
# 30s later, list_apps shows pid 17984 -> running: false; no GIMP window anywhere
```

Tested at 2026-05-21 ~00:10 with GIMP 3.2.4 (winget install). Same partial-block applied to LibreOffice's `swriter.exe` → `soffice.bin` handoff: `swriter.exe` exited immediately, the real Writer process was at a different pid that `list_apps` did surface (Writer works because LibreOffice's launcher chain is shorter / faster to register a window).

## Root cause

cua-driver's `list_apps` derives "running" state from visible top-level windows + foreground pid. When the launcher exe spawns a child via `CreateProcess`/`ShellExecute` and exits, the launched pid is no longer the pid that owns the eventual window. cua-driver doesn't track descendant processes.

## Fix paths

1. **Follow descendant processes**: at launch_app time, snapshot pre-launch process list. After launch, diff to find new processes (by parent-process tree or by time). Surface any of those with a window in the result.
2. **Match by exe basename**: when the input path is `gimp-3.exe`, treat any process whose exe basename starts with `gimp` as a candidate.
3. **Return ALL pids in the post-launch process tree**: most reliable; the caller filters.

Path 1 is cleanest. Use `CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS)` + filter by parent-pid chain (`PROCESSENTRY32.th32ParentProcessID`).

## Workaround

For apps with known stable launcher behavior, callers can re-poll `list_apps` after a few seconds and find the real process by name. But that requires the caller to know the launcher pattern — not discoverable from the launch_app result.

## Related

- Found during overnight stress test (2026-05-21 ~00:10)

title: test-fixtures: consolidate canonical Swift + Rust fixtures into shared dir
body:
## Summary

- Move the three canonical Swift HTML test fixtures (`interactive.html`, `form_all_inputs.html`, `test_page.html`) to a new top-level `libs/cua-driver-fixtures/` directory — the single source of truth shared by both `cua-driver` (Swift / macOS) and `cua-driver-rs` (Rust / Windows + Linux + macOS).
- Replace each port's duplicate copy with a relative symlink to the canonical, so every existing test (`os.path.join(_THIS_DIR, "fixtures", "interactive.html")`, `f"{html_server}/test_page.html"`) keeps working unchanged.
- Add `gesture_panels.html` — a 140-line companion fixture using the same ID-convention style as `test_page.html`, covering the four gestures the v2 harness doesn't currently probe: hotkey + modifier-state propagation, pixel-coord pinpoint, drag-and-drop sequence, scroll. Each panel exposes its state via `window.getGesturePanelState()` for `browser_eval` readback.

## Why

Both ports' integration test trees previously carried duplicate copies of the same HTML fixtures — `interactive.html` in two places, `test_page.html` in two places. The duplicate copies are byte-identical today (`diff -q` shows no differences), but with no link between them they would drift the moment one port iterated on its harness.

`gesture_panels.html` exists because the May 2026 Windows VM stress test (Notepad++/VS Code/LibreOffice/FreeCAD/Inkscape/Audacity/Krita) showed four gestures need explicit harness probes that `test_page.html` doesn't cover. Most critical: **modifier-state propagation** — the page-level `#hotkey-status` prints `ctrl=true|false` so SendInput-vs-PostMessage hotkey routing is observable in a single DOM assertion, directly proving #1614's architectural fix.

## What this is NOT

- It's not a refactor of any test code. Every Swift / pytest integration test consumes these files through the same path it always has — only the underlying file is now a symlink.
- It's not a PR for the new `gesture_panels.html` driver (no test invokes it yet — that's a follow-up once the Chromium-on-Windows browser-eval harness is wired up; the file is added now so it lives alongside the canonical fixtures from the start).

## Result
