title: cua-driver-rs Windows: launch_app should auto-inject anti-throttling flags for hidden Chromium browsers
body:
## Summary

`launch_app` on Windows uses `SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE` so launched apps don't steal focus. For Chromium-based browsers (Edge / Chrome / Brave / Vivaldi / Opera) this triggers occlusion-based renderer throttling, which suspends the renderer process — UIA tree shows no page DOM and `PrintWindow` returns a blank body.

## Repro

```powershell
cua-driver call launch_app '{"path":"msedge","additional_arguments":["file:///C:/some/page.html"]}'
cua-driver call get_window_state '{"pid":<pid>}'
# UIA tree: only Edge chrome (~22 elements: address bar, tabs, buttons).
# Zero page DOM elements.
cua-driver call screenshot '{}'
# Body returns pure white regardless of CSS background.
```

## Expected

Page DOM exposed via UIA; screenshot shows the rendered page.

## Root cause

When a Chromium window is launched non-foreground, Chromium's `CalculateNativeWinOcclusion` marks it occluded and pauses the renderer + accessibility tree. This holds for the entire tab lifetime, not just while occluded.

## Fix

When `launch_app` resolves `path` or `name` to a Chromium-based browser AND the launch will be hidden (which is always, today), auto-prepend these flags to `additional_arguments`:

```
--disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion
--disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows
--disable-renderer-backgrounding
```

These defeat occlusion-based throttling without affecting normal interactive use.

Browser-name match list (resolve via `path.lower()` after extracting the executable basename, also resolve App Paths registry shortcut names):
- `msedge`, `chrome`, `brave`, `opera`, `vivaldi`, `chromium`, `arc` (Chromium-based)
- Skip Firefox / firefox-esr (Gecko, no occlusion throttling)

## Verification

I tested with this flag set against the canonical Swift `test_page.html` on a Windows VM via cua-driver-rs over MCP stdio. All 6 harness goals (click counter, type_text, checkbox, dropdown, link, canvas) passed via UIA read-back. Without the flags: zero page DOM elements visible. With the flags: 33 elements including the full WebArea.

For Chromium-on-Windows DOM verification to work via UIA at all, the caller currently also needs `--force-renderer-accessibility` — that one is page-level not driver-level (it's a Chromium choice not to expose a11y until an AT client probes), so it belongs in the test harness, not in `launch_app`. The three throttling flags above are different — they correct for an interaction between cua-driver-rs's hidden-launch design and Chromium's occlusion logic.

## Related

- #1614 — SendInput hotkey (different but related: also discovered while stress-testing Windows browsers)
- #1593 — cua-driver-uia worker (related: SendInput hotkey requires it; PostMessage-only paths in this issue don't)

title: cua-driver-rs Windows: click(x,y) silently rerouted to UIA Invoke when an actionable element is at that point
body:
## Summary

`click(x,y)` with literal pixel coordinates is documented to post `WM_LBUTTONDOWN` / `WM_LBUTTONUP` to the topmost descendant under those coordinates. In practice, when UIA hit-tests an Invokable element at that point, the path silently switches to `IUIAutomationInvokePattern::Invoke` instead — which fires the element's default action at its *center*, ignoring the requested coords.

## Repro

`test_page.html` (the canonical Swift harness, now shared at `libs/cua-driver-fixtures/test_page.html`) has a 300×150 `<canvas id="mycanvas">` whose `mousedown` handler draws a red dot at the click position and updates `#canvas-status` with the coords.

```
cua-driver call click '{"pid":<edge-pid>,"x":110,"y":677}'
```

Where `(110, 677)` is window-local coords inside the canvas, ~30px from the top-left corner.

Tool response: `"✅ Performed UIA Invoke at (110,677)"` — note "UIA Invoke", not "Posted click".

`#canvas-status` updates to `canvas: clicked at (152,77)` — the canvas's geometric *center*, not the requested (110, 677). The canvas `mousedown` handler did fire, but with synthesized coords from UIA's default-action invocation, not the literal coords I asked for.

## Expected

Tool response: `"✅ Posted click to pid <pid>"` with the literal coords. `#canvas-status` should read `canvas: clicked at (<computed-from-window-110,677>,<...>)`.

## Why this matters

This silently breaks any pixel-precision use case: drawing apps, image maps, custom canvases, paint surfaces, 3D viewports. Callers can't trust `click(x,y)` to land at the pixel they asked for whenever UIA happens to expose the parent element as Invokable.

It also confuses the UX: the existence of the `x,y` overload implies pixel precision; the silent UIA reroute means there's no escape hatch when UIA *also* sees the element.

## Root cause hypothesis

`crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs::ClickTool` probably calls `try_invoke_in_window_at_point` (or the equivalent) as a pre-check, and if it returns an Invokable element, takes the Invoke path. For element-index callers this is correct; for `x,y` callers it isn't.

## Fix

The `x,y` code path should bypass the UIA Invoke pre-check entirely. Always post `WM_LBUTTONDOWN` / `WM_LBUTTONUP` to the topmost descendant at the requested coords via `WindowFromPoint` + window-local conversion.

If there's a reason to keep UIA Invoke as a fallback for element-index callers, it should be conditional on the click being routed via `element_index`, not via raw `x,y`.

## Related

- #1620 — GTK-on-Windows UIA black hole (different mechanism, but a sibling case of "pixel-coord is the only viable click path on some surfaces")

title: cua-driver-rs Windows: PostMessage(WM_LBUTTONDOWN/UP) to Chromium HWND doesn't fire DOM input — coord clicks on Edge/Chrome need SendInput
body:
## Summary

`click(x, y)` against Chromium-based browsers (Edge, Chrome, etc.) returns the success string `"✅ Posted click to pid <pid>"`, but the Chromium DOM input pipeline never sees the click — `onclick` handlers don't fire, `mousedown` event listeners don't trigger, and DOM state mutations don't happen.

This breaks coordinate-addressed clicks on **any** element inside Chromium content (buttons, links, canvases, custom widgets) — not just canvas-like surfaces.

## Repro

Discovered while verifying the fix for #1621 against `libs/cua-driver-fixtures/test_page.html` loaded in Edge.

```
# Daemon must be in user's interactive session (Session 2 on Windows) with
# Edge launched using the four flags from #1620.

# Element-index click on "Click Me" button via UIA Invoke — WORKS:
cua-driver call click '{"pid":<edge-pid>,"element_index":16}'
# → counter increments from 0 to 1 ✅

# Coordinate click on the SAME button at its center — FAILS:
cua-driver call click '{"pid":<edge-pid>,"x":126,"y":252}'
# → tool response: "✅ Posted click to pid <pid>"
# → counter STAYS at 0 — onclick never fired ❌
```

Same result for canvas (`#mycanvas`) and any other DOM target.

## Why it was hidden before #1621

The previous version of `try_invoke_in_window_at_point` accepted any UIA element with `InvokePattern` at the click point. Chromium's accessibility tree exposes many elements (buttons, links, even canvases) as Invokable, so the x,y click silently rerouted through UIA Invoke — which fires the element's default action regardless of coords. From the caller's POV the click "worked" (for buttons), but pixel precision was lost (for canvases). #1621 fixed the canvas misrouting and surfaced this underlying delivery gap.

## Likely root cause

Chromium's input thread architecture doesn't process posted WM_LBUTTONDOWN/UP on the top-level frame HWND (or even on `Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND`). Chromium installs its own input message filter that requires `SendInput`-routed events through the system input queue, not `PostMessage` to the message pump. The same architecture is documented in the Chromium source: `content/browser/renderer_host/input/input_router_impl.cc` filters synthetic events by `SendInput`-style queue origin.

This matches the symptoms: UIA Invoke (which calls into Chromium's a11y bridge directly) works; PostMessage to either the top-level HWND or `Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND` does not.

## Fix paths

1. **SendInput via cua-driver-uia worker.** For Chromium targets, route coordinate clicks through the UIAccess-elevated `cua-driver-uia.exe` (#1593) which can `SetForegroundWindow` Edge + `SendInput` to land synthetic mouse events on the system input queue. This is the only path that survives Chromium's input filter.

2. **CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol).** When Edge is launched with `--remote-debugging-port`, the driver could connect to the DevTools websocket and call `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`. This delivers DOM-level clicks with pixel precision, no system focus required. Requires the test harness to pass `--remote-debugging-port`; can't be the default path since most users won't.

3. **Stay on UIA Invoke** for the cases that work, document pixel precision as unsupported on Chromium for coord clicks without `--remote-debugging-port`. Pragmatic but lossy.

## Recommended

Path 1 — SendInput via the cua-driver-uia worker is the architecturally consistent answer:
- We already have the worker (#1593, manifested + signed)
- The worker handles modifier-state hotkey (#1614/#1618), which has the same Chromium issue
- Routing Chromium x,y clicks through the worker is a natural extension of "the worker is where input that needs system-queue origin goes"

The dispatch logic in `crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs::ClickTool` should:

```rust
// Pseudocode
if target_is_chromium(hwnd) {
    return route_via_uia_worker(pid, x, y, button, count);
}
// existing UIA Invoke / PostMessage logic
```

Where `target_is_chromium` checks the top-level window's class name (`Chrome_WidgetWin_1`, `MozillaWindowClass`, etc. — Chromium and friends use a stable set).

## Related

- #1621 — control-type whitelist for x,y → UIA Invoke (made this gap visible)
- #1620 — Chromium anti-throttling flags
- #1614, #1618 — SendInput-routed hotkey (sibling architectural fix; same Chromium quirk)
- #1593 — cua-driver-uia worker (where the SendInput path lives)

title: cua-driver Windows install.ps1: PowerShell 5.1 parse errors at lines 946+
body:
## Summary

`libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.ps1` fails to parse under stock Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the version that ships with Windows 10 / Windows Server 2019 / Windows 11). Multiple `Write-Host` lines in the post-install hints region trigger parser errors:

```
At C:\...\install-cua-driver.ps1:946 char:83
+ ... st "  Use in the current session:  `$env:Path += `";$VisibleBinDir`""
+                                                                       ~~~
Unexpected token '`""' in expression or statement.
```

```
At C:\...\install-cua-driver.ps1:962 char:52
+         Write-Host "  Run now without re-logging:  & `"$installedBina ...
+                                                    ~
The ampersand (&) character is not allowed.
```

Same errors at lines 963, 964, 977, 979, 980, 981, 982, 990. Affects the `-AutoStart` path and the manual-autostart hint block. Net effect: a stock Windows host's `iwr install.ps1 | iex` does nothing — nothing installs.

## Repro

```powershell
iwr "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.ps1" | iex
# Parse fails at line 946; nothing installs.
```

## Workaround

Manual install from the release zip:

```powershell
$url = "https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/download/cua-driver-rs-v0.2.9/cua-driver-rs-0.2.9-windows-x86_64-binary.zip"
iwr $url -OutFile $env:TEMP\cua.zip
Expand-Archive $env:TEMP\cua.zip "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\trycua\cua-driver-rs\bin"
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('Path', "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\trycua\cua-driver-rs\bin;" + [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','User'), 'User')
```

## Fix paths

1. Use single-quoted strings for the hint lines, or `+` string concatenation for the bits that need `$installedBinary` interpolation.
2. Or use a here-string with a single-quote opener (`@'…'@`) for the autostart hint block — keeps `&` and `$` literal across the whole block.
3. Or drop the `&` and write literal commands.

## Repro environment

- Windows Server 2025 (Azure VM)
- Stock PowerShell 5.1 (no PS 7+)

Reported during v0.2.9 install verification on the Windows VM after the #1620 / #1621 / #1623 fixes landed.

title: fix(cua-driver): install.ps1 PowerShell 5.1 parse compatibility (#1626)
body:
## Summary

`iwr install.ps1 | iex` failed silently on stock Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the version that ships with Windows 10 / Server 2019 / Server 2025). PS 7+ (`pwsh`) parses fine; PS 5.1's tokenizer chokes on three patterns in the post-install hint block. Net effect: every Windows user on the default PS gets nothing installed when running the README's documented one-liner.

## Root causes

1. **Nested backtick-escaped double-quotes** (L946): `"  Use in the current session:  \`$env:Path += \`";$VisibleBinDir\`""` — PS 5.1 mis-terminates the string at the first `\`"`.
2. **Call operator `&` inside double-quoted strings with `\`"$var\`"`** (L962-964, 969): `"... & \`"$installedBinary\`" autostart kick"` — PS 5.1 treats `&` as the call operator even inside a literal string.
3. **Em-dash `—` inside a double-quoted Write-Host string** (L934): the multi-byte UTF-8 character makes PS 5.1's tokenizer mis-report "string is missing the terminator" several lines later.

## Fix

Reword the post-install hints to reference `cua-driver` by name (which the User PATH update adds anyway) instead of `& "<full-path>"`. The binary path still appears verbatim on a separate `Binary at: <path>` line. The `$autostartHint` here-string is unrolled into individual `Write-Host` calls — same visual output, no here-string body containing the problem characters. The em-dash in the User PATH success line becomes `--`.

Em-dashes inside `#` comments are left as-is; they don't affect PS 5.1's parser in comment context.

## Verification

```
PS> $PSVersionTable.PSVersion
5.1.26100
PS> $src = Get-Content -Raw install.ps1
PS> $t = $null; $e = $null
PS> [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseInput($src,[ref]$t,[ref]$e) | Out-Null
PS> $e.Count
0
PS> [scriptblock]::Create($src)    # what `iex` does internally — used to fail
[scriptblock]
```

End-to-end run via the README one-liner now:

- downloads windows-x86_64 binary from GitHub Releases ✅
- extracts to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\trycua\cua-driver-rs\bin` ✅
- creates the two NTFS directory junctions ✅
- adds bin dir to User PATH ✅
- prints the hint block cleanly ✅
- `cua-driver --version` resolves and reports `cua-driver 0.2.8` ✅

## Behavioral change

Post-install hints now show `cua-driver autostart kick` (relying on the just-added PATH entry resolving the command) instead of `& "C:\...\cua-driver.exe" autostart kick`. For the current PowerShell session the user still needs to open a new shell or reload the User PATH for `cua-driver` to resolve. The full binary path is still printed on a separate `Binary at: <path>` line for the explicit-invoke case.

Closes #1626.

## Test plan

- [x] Parser API (`[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseInput`) returns 0 errors on PS 5.1.26100
- [x] `[scriptblock]::Create($src)` succeeds (this is what `iex` does internally)
- [x] End-to-end install via `iwr | iex` on a fresh Windows Server 2025 VM with PS 5.1
- [ ] Test the `-AutoStart` path on the same VM
- [ ] Verify PS 7+ (`pwsh`) still parses + runs (not regressed)

title: fix(cua-driver): install.ps1 OSArchitecture lookup under StrictMode Latest
body:
## Summary

`irm install.ps1 | iex` fails immediately on a fresh user account with:

```
iex : The property 'OSArchitecture' cannot be found on this object. Verify that the property exists.
```

Source: `Get-TargetTriple`'s `[System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation]::OSArchitecture` call. Under `Set-StrictMode -Version Latest` (install.ps1:78), PS 5.1 reports the static property access as missing-property in certain session contexts — specifically a freshly-created admin user with no profile, no prior loaded modules. The script works fine under the RID-500 built-in Administrator on the same VM, which is why this went undetected through v0.2.9.

## Fix

Use `$env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE` as the primary architecture source — always set on Windows, never trips StrictMode, no .NET version dependency. `RuntimeInformation.OSArchitecture` is kept as a try/catch fallback for edge configurations where `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE` is unset.

| Source | Value | Triple |
|---|---|---|
| `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE` | `AMD64` | `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` |
| `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE` | `ARM64` | `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc` |
| `RuntimeInformation` fallback | `X64` | `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` |
| `RuntimeInformation` fallback | `Arm64` | `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc` |

## Repro

Provision a fresh non-RID-500 admin user on Windows 11 24H2:
```powershell
net user testuser P@ssw0rd! /add /Y
net localgroup Administrators testuser /add
```
Log in as `testuser`, open non-elevated PowerShell, run:
```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.ps1 | iex
```
Before this fix: hard fail after the "install dir" log line.
After this fix: install completes through to `cua-driver-rs 0.2.9 installed.`

## Verification

- [x] `install.ps1` parses cleanly on PS 5.1.26100.8457 (3,169 tokens, 0 errors)

title: fix(cua-driver): uninstall.ps1 halts when scheduled task already gone
body:
## Summary

Under `\$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'` (set at uninstall.ps1:57), PowerShell 5.1 treats native-command stderr as a terminating error. `2>\$null` masks the display but the error record still trips Stop and halts the script. Net effect: when the \`cua-driver-serve\` Scheduled Task is already gone (e.g. installer's autostart step failed earlier), \`schtasks /Query\` writes "task not found" to stderr, the script terminates, and phases 2-5 (kill daemon, remove junctions, remove package home) all skip.

## Fix

Locally lower \`\$ErrorActionPreference\` to \`Continue\` around both \`schtasks\` invocations (Query and Delete), restore via \`finally\`. Missing-task detection still uses \`\$LASTEXITCODE\` — same control flow.

## Repro

```powershell
# As cuademo (a standard admin user, NOT RID-500):
irm install.ps1 | iex                     # install OK
cua-driver autostart enable               # access-denied — task NOT registered
irm uninstall.ps1 | iex                   # ❌ halts at schtasks /Query
```

After this patch the uninstall completes cleanly through all 5 phases.

## Related

- Surfaced during the cuademo fresh-install dogfood that followed #1630 / #1631 / #1632.
- Sibling install.ps1 hardening: #1628 (PS 5.1 parse), #1631 (OSArchitecture / StrictMode).

title: cua-driver-rs CLI: launch_app rejects 'aumid' field — works via MCP, fails via 'cua-driver call'
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver call launch_app '{"aumid":"..."}'` fails with `Provide either bundle_id or name to identify the app to launch.`, even though the schema and code accept `aumid` as a valid target. The same call via the MCP tool surface (Claude Code, etc.) works.

## Repro

On Windows, v0.2.12, cuademo (non-RID-500 admin) PowerShell:

```powershell
cua-driver call launch_app '{"aumid":"Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App"}'
# cua-driver.exe : Provide either bundle_id or name to identify the app to launch.
```

Via MCP tool (works):
```
mcp__cua-driver__launch_app({aumid: "Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App"})
# → returns pid, windows[], etc.
```

## Hypothesis

The CLI's JSON-args deserialization path (`cua-driver call <tool> <json>`) drops or renames the `aumid` field before it reaches `LaunchAppTool::run`. The target resolution chain (`launch_path > path > aumid > name > bundle_id`) then finds no target and emits the Swift-compat error.

Possible causes:

- The CLI's arg-passing layer uses a different `serde` shape than the MCP layer (e.g. `serde(rename = "aumid")` not applied on the CLI path).
- `cua-driver call` consumes JSON args via a wrapper that re-serializes through a schema that lacks `aumid`.
- The CLI's `validate_args` step rejects unknown fields and silently drops `aumid` if the schema declaration is incomplete somewhere.

## Workarounds

- Use MCP path (Claude Code, opencode, etc.) — works.
- Use `path` field with the full AUMID:
  ```powershell
  cua-driver call launch_app '{"path":"shell:appsFolder\\Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App"}'
  ```
- Use `bundle_id` if the AUMID contains `!`:
  ```powershell
  cua-driver call launch_app '{"bundle_id":"Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App"}'
  ```

## Fix direction

Audit the `cua-driver call <tool>` JSON-args plumbing and confirm that all schema fields (`launch_path`, `path`, `aumid`, `name`, `bundle_id`, `urls`, `additional_arguments`, ...) round-trip identically to the MCP path. Add a regression test that calls `cua-driver call launch_app` with each field shape against a known-running app.

## Surfaced

During the cuademo fresh-install dogfood (v0.2.12) when probing whether a Medium-IL daemon can drive Calculator. The MCP path was unavailable (session-scoped named pipe — Claude Code's MCP server in fbonacci's Session 0 saw fbonacci's High-IL daemon, not cuademo's Medium-IL one), so we tried the CLI path and hit this gap.

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): list_apps misses UWP apps for non-RID-500 admin users
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver call list_apps` on Windows enumerates desktop apps and Start Menu shortcuts but omits installed UWP / AppContainer apps (Calculator, Photos, modern Settings, Microsoft Store apps, etc.) for non-RID-500 admin users.

On the **same machine**, the RID-500 built-in Administrator account (`fbonacci`) DOES see Calculator etc. in `list_apps` output. The non-RID-500 admin (`cuademo`) doesn't.

## Repro

Windows 11 24H2, cua-driver-rs v0.2.12, daemon at Medium IL via the RunLevel=Highest autostart task (filtered token wins because cuademo is non-RID-500 — see #1602 context):

```powershell
PS> Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.WindowsCalculator | Select-Object Name,PackageFullName
Name                          PackageFullName
----                          ---------------
Microsoft.WindowsCalculator   Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_11.x.x.x_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe
# → installed for cuademo

PS> cua-driver call list_apps | ConvertFrom-Json | Where-Object { $_.name -match "Calc" }
# → empty
```

Comparison from fbonacci (RID 500, High IL daemon) on the same VM during earlier tests:
```
"bundle_id": "Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe",
"name": "Windows Calculator",
"kind": "uwp",
"launch_path": "shell:appsFolder\\Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App"
```

## Hypothesis

`shell:AppsFolder` enumeration (the source for UWP apps in list_apps) is filtered by the calling process's token IL or capability set. Medium-IL processes may not have access to enumerate all installed UWP packages — only those the user has explicitly invoked or where the package metadata permits Medium-IL enumeration.

Alternative: the enumeration is done via `IShellItem::BindToHandler(BHID_EnumItems)` on `shell:AppsFolder` and that itself may require higher privilege to surface ALL installed UWP apps.

This is the same family of restriction as the Calculator-UIA-tree truncation (#1602) — UWP / AppContainer surfaces are gated by token integrity in places we don't always expect.

## Workaround

Use the `path` field with the full AUMID directly (skips enumeration):
```powershell
cua-driver call launch_app '{"path":"shell:appsFolder\\Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App"}'
```

`Get-AppxPackage` from PowerShell does enumerate UWP apps from a Medium-IL admin shell, so the data is reachable via the AppX management surface even if `shell:AppsFolder` filters us out.

## Fix direction

1. Confirm via Process Monitor whether the `shell:AppsFolder` enumeration call returns truncated results from a Medium-IL caller — capture the syscall trace from both `fbonacci` and `cuademo` daemons doing the same enumeration.
2. If Medium-IL is the variable: add a fallback enumeration via the AppX management API (`Get-AppxPackage` equivalent — `PackageManager::FindPackagesForUserWithPackageTypes`) which works from Medium IL.
3. Merge the two enumerations in list_apps so UWP coverage is consistent across token IL.

## Related

- #1602 (UWP automation / EV cert + UIAccess)
- #1601 (Calculator returns 1 element)
- The above CLI `aumid` field bug — together they make UWP-from-cuademo difficult to dogfood from the CLI

## Surfaced

During the v0.2.12 cuademo dogfood when probing whether Medium-IL daemons can drive UWP at all. Confirmed Calculator is installed (`Get-AppxPackage`) but absent from `list_apps`, and `ApplicationFrameHost.exe` is only running when a UWP app is open (so we can't even use that pid as a probe target without first opening a UWP via a non-cua-driver mechanism).

title: cua-driver-rs CLI: 'call <tool>' silently falls back to stdin when positional JSON fails to parse — masks PS 5.1 argv quote-stripping
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver call <tool> <json>` uses `serde_json::from_str(json).ok()` on the positional arg, and if that returns None **silently falls back to reading JSON from stdin**. When stdin is empty (the common case), the tool receives `json_args = None`, and the tool's own required-field validator emits a misleading error like `"Missing required integer field pid."`.

The actual problem is upstream: PowerShell 5.1's native-command argv parsing strips quotes around field names in multi-field JSON, so the arg cua-driver receives is malformed JSON. The CLI never tells the user this.

## Repro

Windows PowerShell 5.1 (Windows 11 24H2):

```powershell
PS> cua-driver call get_window_state '{"pid":9912,"window_id":197488}'
cua-driver.exe : Missing required integer field pid.
```

The same JSON in a single-field arg works:
```powershell
PS> cua-driver call list_windows '{"pid":9912}'
# returns windows list
```

The difference is the **comma**: PS5.1's argv parser handles single-field JSON OK but mangles multi-field JSON. The CLI silently absorbs the parse failure instead of surfacing it.

## Root cause (`crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs:209-211`)

```rust
Some("call") => {
    let tool = pos.next().unwrap_or("").to_string();
    let json_args = pos.next()
        .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(s).ok())   // ← .ok() swallows the parse error
        .or_else(|| read_stdin_json());
    Command::Call { tool, json_args, screenshot_out_file }
}
```

## Fix direction

When the positional JSON arg is present but doesn't parse, emit a clear actionable error before falling back to stdin. Two options:

1. Emit a clear error directly:
   ```
   error: positional arg "{...}" is not valid JSON. Falling back to stdin (which appears empty).
   hint: PowerShell 5.1 may be stripping quotes around field names. Try piping the JSON via stdin:
     echo '{"pid":9912,"window_id":197488}' | cua-driver call get_window_state
   ```

2. Differentiate "no positional arg given" vs "positional arg given but malformed":
   ```rust
   let json_args = match pos.next() {
       Some(s) => match serde_json::from_str(s) {
           Ok(v) => Some(v),
           Err(e) => {
               eprintln!("error: positional JSON arg did not parse: {e}");
               eprintln!("hint: try piping the JSON via stdin to avoid PowerShell argv quirks:");
               eprintln!("  '{{...}}' | cua-driver call <tool>");
               std::process::exit(2);
           }
       },
       None => read_stdin_json(),
   };
   ```

## Workaround

Pipe the JSON via stdin (works around the PS argv quote-stripping):
```powershell
'{"pid":9912,"window_id":197488}' | cua-driver call get_window_state
```

## Surfaced

During the cuademo (non-RID-500 admin) v0.2.12 fresh-install dogfood, attempting to verify the Medium-IL UWP UIA tree size on Calculator. Took multiple iterations of the probe script to realize the CLI was masking a real argv quoting issue.

## Related

- #1635 — `cua-driver call launch_app` rejects `aumid` field via CLI (different root cause, similar surface — both make UWP automation hard from non-MCP code paths)
- #1636 — `list_apps` misses UWP apps for non-RID-500 admins

title: cua-driver-rs autostart docs vs reality: RunLevel=Highest doesn't actually elevate non-RID-500 admin daemons on AtLogon trigger
body:
## Summary

PR #1630 switched the autostart Scheduled Task to `RunLevel=Highest` + `LogonType=Interactive`, on the assumption that this would give the daemon at High IL after the AtLogon trigger fires. The autostart.rs doc comment claims:

> RunLevel=Highest (since 2026-05-21): the daemon is registered to run at the user's elevated/admin token rather than the filtered standard-user token. This is what lets cua-driver drive UWP / AppContainer apps

In practice, on non-RID-500 admin accounts (the typical Windows user — any admin user except the built-in Administrator), the daemon still runs at **Medium IL** after the AtLogon trigger. UAC's Admin Approval Mode unconditionally filters the token regardless of the principal's RunLevel.

## Repro

```powershell
# As a typical Windows admin user (member of BUILTIN\Administrators, NOT RID 500):
irm install.ps1 | iex
cua-driver autostart enable     # → UAC prompt, registers task at RunLevel=Highest
# Log out and back in (so the AtLogon trigger fires from Task Scheduler, not user-initiated)
cua-driver call check_permissions
# → {"elevated":false, ...}
```

Confirmed on Windows 11 24H2 with `cuademo` (UAC-split-token admin, SID ending in -1000). Same task definition on `fbonacci` (RID 500, no UAC split-token) gives `elevated:true` — the difference is the user account type, not the task definition.

## Why it doesn't work

- `LogonType=Interactive` makes the task run in the user's interactive session token.
- For non-RID-500 admins, the interactive session token at logon time is the *filtered* (Medium IL) token. Windows hands out the filtered token by default; the user's full token is only available via UAC elevation.
- `RunLevel=Highest` is a hint, but it doesn't bypass UAC's token filtering for AtLogon-triggered Interactive tasks.
- Various Task Scheduler combinations (`ProcessTokenSidType=Unrestricted` etc.) either don't apply to Interactive LogonType or are rejected with "unexpected node" by the task XML schema.

The only ways to get a true High-IL Interactive daemon for non-RID-500 admins:
1. **EV-cert + UIAccess** on `cua-driver-uia.exe` (#1602) — proper long-term answer
2. Built-in Administrator (RID 500) account — special case, no token filtering by default
3. Globally disable UAC (`EnableLUA=0`) — heavy hammer, security trade-off, requires reboot
4. `LogonType=S4U` — gives full token but task lands in Session 0 (no interactive desktop, breaks UWP activation)

## What to fix

Two things, separately:

### (a) Honest doc comment

Update `autostart.rs::REGISTER_PS` doc comment to reflect reality:

> RunLevel=Highest: requested for the principal, but Windows UAC unconditionally filters interactive logon tokens for non-RID-500 admin accounts. On those accounts the daemon still starts at Medium IL — which is fine for Win32 + Chromium automation, but truncates UWP / AppContainer UIA trees (Calculator returns ~1 element vs ~30+). RunLevel=Highest is the cheapest path that lifts THIS for the RID 500 built-in Administrator; full UWP coverage for typical admin users still requires the EV-cert UIAccess worker (#1602).

### (b) check_permissions / doctor output

`cua-driver doctor` and the post-install hint block should warn when:
- The autostart task is registered at `RunLevel=Highest`, AND
- The daemon's actual IL is Medium (`elevated:false`)

That's a strong signal the user is on a non-RID-500 account and our autostart workaround isn't doing what they think. Print a clear "you'll see truncated UIA trees for Calculator-class UWP apps; see #1602" warning so users aren't confused later when the bug bites.

## Related

- #1602 — UIAccess + EV cert (the real fix)
- #1601 — Calculator returns 1 element
- #1630 — the PR that introduced the RunLevel=Highest path with the misleading promise

## Surfaced

cuademo v0.2.12 dogfood. The whole autostart-RunLevel=Highest design rested on an assumption that turned out to only hold for RID 500.

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): list_windows under ApplicationFrameHost pid returns unrelated windows (AgentCursorOverlay, ISE, Program Manager)
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver call list_windows '{"pid":<ApplicationFrameHost-pid>}'` returns a mix of windows: the legitimately-hosted UWP windows (Calculator), plus unrelated windows from other processes — `TropeCUA.AgentCursorOverlay.default`, `Windows PowerShell ISE`, `Program Manager`, `Windows PowerShell`, etc.

The pid filter appears to be loose — it's returning windows that aren't actually owned by ApplicationFrameHost.exe.

## Repro

Windows 11 24H2, cua-driver-rs v0.2.12, daemon at any IL:

```powershell
PS> Start-Process calc   # spawn a UWP via ApplicationFrameHost
PS> $afh = (Get-Process ApplicationFrameHost).Id
PS> cua-driver call list_windows "{`"pid`":$afh}" | ConvertFrom-Json | Select -ExpandProperty windows | Format-Table title

title
-----
TropeCUA.AgentCursorOverlay.default
Calculator
Windows PowerShell ISE
Calculator
Windows PowerShell
Select Administrator: C:\Users\cuademo\.cua-driver-rs\packages\releases\0.2.12-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\cua-...
Program Manager
```

`Get-Process ApplicationFrameHost | Get-WindowEnumeration` (or PowerShell's `Get-Process | ForEach { ... GetMainWindowTitle }`) on the same pid returns only the actual UWP windows hosted by ApplicationFrameHost (Calculator + any other open UWP apps). So this looks like a list_windows bug, not a Windows-shell display quirk.

## Hypothesis

`list_windows` may be using `EnumWindows` (system-wide window enumeration) and post-filtering by `GetWindowThreadProcessId == pid` — but the filter is either off-by-one or doing partial matching. Or the pid is being interpreted as a session id / something else.

Alternative: list_windows may be returning ALL top-level windows in the user's session when pid filter doesn't apply (e.g. the user-supplied pid doesn't match any known process — but ApplicationFrameHost IS a known process).

## What to inspect

`crates/platform-windows/src/win32/windows.rs` (or wherever list_windows is implemented). Specifically:
- Does the pid filter use `==` or `<=`?
- Is there a fallback to "list all windows" when the pid doesn't match?
- Is the comparison done after extracting `GetWindowThreadProcessId` correctly?

## Why this matters

Affects every workflow that uses `list_windows` to disambiguate a UWP app's windows from co-hosted windows in the same ApplicationFrameHost. A user-facing automation flow trying to "find Calculator's window" gets back a list including the user's PowerShell window — needs to know to filter further.

## Surfaced

cuademo v0.2.12 dogfood, while probing Calculator's UIA tree. The probe script picked the first window with title matching "Calculator" — happened to work, but the list also contained `TropeCUA.AgentCursorOverlay.default` (a cua-driver-internal window!) and the user's PowerShell windows, which is wrong.

title: cua-driver-rs check_permissions: reports 'elevated:false' on a daemon at actual High IL (0x3000)
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver call check_permissions` returns `{"elevated":false,...}` on a daemon that is actually running at High IL (token integrity RID `0x3000`), verified via direct Win32 `OpenProcessToken` + `GetTokenInformation(TokenIntegrityLevel)`. The check is reporting against the wrong condition — probably `IsInRole(Administrator)` on a token whose Administrators SID is enabled but the role check still returns false in this scenario.

This is consequential: the `elevated` field is used in our autostart setup docs as the "did the High-IL workaround actually work?" signal. A misleading `elevated:false` would convince users (and CI) that RunLevel=Highest didn't work even when it did.

## Repro

Windows 11 24H2, cua-driver-rs v0.2.12, daemon registered via `cua-driver autostart enable` with `RunLevel=Highest`, launched via AtLogon trigger:

```powershell
# Direct Win32 read of the daemon's token IL:
$cd = (Get-Process cua-driver).Id
# Using the inline TokenIL helper from the earlier matrix tests:
[TokenIL]::GetIntegrity($cd)
# → 12288 (0x3000) — HIGH IL ✓

# But check_permissions says otherwise:
cua-driver call check_permissions
# → {"elevated":false,"post_message":true,"uia":true}

# And UWP automation actually works at High IL:
Start-Process calc; Start-Sleep 4
$framePid = (Get-Process ApplicationFrameHost).Id
'{"pid":' + $framePid + ',"window_id":<wid>}' | cua-driver call get_window_state
# → element_count: 41 (full UIA tree of Calculator — same as RID-500 admin would see)
```

`elevated:false` + `element_count:41` is internally inconsistent — if the daemon really wasn't elevated, it would NOT be able to read 41 elements from an AppContainer'd Calculator (the historic #1601/#1602 gap).

## Hypothesis

The Rust implementation of `check_permissions` likely calls something like:

```rust
WindowsPrincipal::IsInRole(Administrator)
// or equivalent: check whether BUILTIN\Administrators is in the current process token
// with SE_GROUP_ENABLED.
```

For a UAC-filtered admin token (filtered at logon), `IsInRole` returns false because the Administrators SID is present but marked `SE_GROUP_USE_FOR_DENY_ONLY`.

But on this VM, the daemon at IL=0x3000 was spawned by Task Scheduler via the AtLogon trigger of a `RunLevel=Highest` task. That code path produces a token with Administrators SID **enabled** AND IL High — the user's full token. IsInRole *should* return true here.

Possibly the check is happening BEFORE the daemon process inherits the full token, or `IsInRole` is being called against a different (impersonation?) token than the one the process actually runs under.

The honest check is to query the token's mandatory IL via `GetTokenInformation(TokenIntegrityLevel)` and return `elevated = (rid >= 0x3000)`, instead of relying on a role-membership heuristic.

## Fix direction

Replace the IsInRole-style check in check_permissions with a direct token IL query:

```rust
fn is_high_il() -> bool {
    use windows::Win32::Security::{GetTokenInformation, TokenIntegrityLevel, ...};
    // OpenProcessToken on GetCurrentProcess
    // GetTokenInformation(token, TokenIntegrityLevel, ...)
    // Read the last sub-authority of the integrity SID
    // Return true iff RID >= 0x3000
}
```

Same algorithm we used in the inline `TokenIL` helper in serve.rs / the dogfood probe scripts.

## Why we noticed

cuademo's v0.2.12 fresh-install dogfood: every diagnostic in the troubleshooting flow was hinging on `elevated:true/false` from check_permissions to confirm the autostart-elevation workaround landed. Got `elevated:false` after a full sign-out/sign-in cycle with the task at Highest, and spent 30+ minutes pursuing the wrong root cause (assuming RunLevel=Highest didn't elevate non-RID-500 admins). Eventually verified the daemon was actually at High IL via direct Win32 token read, exposing that check_permissions was lying.

## Related

- #1602 — UWP automation / EV cert + UIAccess (this bug muddies the symptom diagnosis for #1602)
- #1638 — RunLevel=Highest doc/reality gap (this bug is what made the gap LOOK real)
- #1601 — Calculator returns 1 element (also potentially confused by this reporting bug)

A fix here might let us close or significantly downgrade #1602 / #1638 — turns out cuademo IS getting High IL via the autostart-elevation path, and Calculator DOES drive cleanly from there. The remaining gap may purely be about UAC-prompt UX, not about token IL.

title: fix(cua-driver-rs): CLI 'call' surfaces JSON parse errors with PS5.1 stdin-pipe hint (#1637, closes #1635)
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver call <tool> <json>` used `.and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(s).ok()).or_else(stdin)` which silently swallowed parse errors and fell back to stdin. On PowerShell 5.1, native-command argv parsing mangles multi-field JSON (strips quotes around field names) — the CLI never told the user. The tool's own required-field validator then emitted a misleading "missing field X" error.

## Fix

Differentiate "no positional arg" (legit stdin fallback) from "positional arg given but didn't parse" (emit clear error + stdin-pipe hint + exit 2). Applied to both `cua-driver call <tool>` and the implicit `cua-driver <tool>` paths.

Sample output after fix:

```
error: positional JSON arg to 'cua-driver call' did not parse: ...
       received: {pid:9912,window_id:197488}

hint: PowerShell 5.1 strips quotes around JSON field names in
      multi-field args. Pipe the JSON via stdin instead:
        '{"pid":1234,"window_id":5678}' | cua-driver call get_window_state

      Or use PowerShell 7+ (pwsh) which preserves the quotes.
```

## Also closes #1635

The launch_app error "Provide either bundle_id or name" was misleading — Windows resolver accepts `aumid`, `path`, `launch_path`, `urls` too. The Swift-original message predated those additions. Now reads: "Provide one of: bundle_id, name, aumid, path, launch_path, or urls".

Note: the actual root cause of #1635 (cuademo's `cua-driver call launch_app '{"aumid":"..."}'` failing) is the PS argv quote-stripping fixed above. The error-message tweak just prevents future confusion when someone hits the error for unrelated reasons.

Closes #1637, closes #1635.

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): autostart task's daemon spawns a visible console window at logon
body:
## Summary

The \`cua-driver-serve\` Scheduled Task (registered by \`cua-driver autostart enable\` / \`install.ps1 -AutoStart\`) spawns the daemon with a default Windows CUI console window visible on the user's desktop at every interactive logon. The window stays open for the lifetime of the daemon — a constant eyesore that clutters the desktop after every sign-in.

Reported by cuademo dogfood after sign-out + sign-in on v0.2.13.

## Repro

1. \`irm install.ps1 | iex\`
2. \`cua-driver autostart enable\` (accept UAC prompt)
3. Sign out and back in
4. Daemon launches via AtLogon trigger → console window appears on desktop with title "Administrator: C:\\Users\\<user>\\.cua-driver-rs\\packages\\releases\\<v>-...\\cua-driver.exe" displaying "cua-driver daemon listening on \\\\.\\pipe\\cua-driver"

## Why

Our autostart task action is:
\`\`\`
\$action = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute \$env:CUA_DRIVER_AS_EXE -Argument 'serve' ...
\`\`\`

\`cua-driver.exe\` is a console-subsystem (CUI) executable. When Task Scheduler launches it without a parent console, Windows allocates a new console window and attaches the process — which makes the window visible.

## Fix direction (pick one)

### Option 1: subsystem flag

Mark \`cua-driver.exe\` as a windows-subsystem (GUI) binary when serving as a daemon — no console allocated at startup. Trade-off: stdio output disappears when the user invokes \`cua-driver serve\` from PowerShell directly. Would need to split into two binaries (\`cua-driver.exe\` CUI + \`cua-driver-daemon.exe\` GUI) or a \`#![windows_subsystem = "windows"]\` conditional. **Heavy lift, breaks the "one binary" UX.**

### Option 2: wrap in hidden powershell via task action (recommended)

Change autostart.rs's task action to:
\`\`\`
\$action = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute "powershell.exe" \\
    -Argument "-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -NonInteractive -Command \\"Start-Process -FilePath '\$env:CUA_DRIVER_AS_EXE' -ArgumentList 'serve' -WindowStyle Hidden\\"" \\
    -WorkingDirectory \$env:USERPROFILE
\`\`\`

PowerShell launches hidden, then uses \`Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden\` to start cua-driver detached. Result: no visible window. Trade-off: an extra powershell.exe in the process tree at launch time (exits after spawning the child).

### Option 3: FreeConsole at startup

In \`serve.rs\` Windows-only init: call \`GetConsoleWindow()\` + \`GetWindowThreadProcessId\`; if the console is owned by this process (vs inherited from a parent cmd/PowerShell), call \`FreeConsole()\` to detach. Trade-off: the window FLASHES briefly during process startup (kernel creates console before main() runs) — not a perfect hide.

### Option 4: hide window after startup

\`GetConsoleWindow()\` + \`ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_HIDE)\` if owned by this process. Same flash trade-off as #3 but doesn't break stdio.

**Recommended: Option 2.** Cleanest user experience (no window at all, no flash), no code changes to cua-driver itself, contained to autostart.rs's task action. Document the powershell wrapper in the function's doc comment so the rationale is preserved.

## Surfaced

cuademo (non-RID-500 admin) dogfood on Windows 11 24H2, cua-driver-rs v0.2.13. The visible window was noticed immediately on the desktop after sign-in cycle, with the title "Administrator: C:\\Users\\cuademo\\.cua-driver-rs\\packages\\releases\\0.2.13-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\\cua-driver.exe".

title: cua-driver-rs check_permissions still misreports IL — Rust impl disagrees with equivalent C# Win32 read (#1640 followup)
body:
## Summary

PR #1641 (#1640 fix) replaced \`GetTokenInformation(TokenElevation)\` with \`GetTokenInformation(TokenIntegrityLevel)\` to honestly report the daemon's integrity level. The new code STILL misreports — on a cuademo daemon that the kernel says is at High IL (RID 0x3000), \`check_permissions\` returns Medium IL (RID 0x2000).

This is the SAME class of bug as #1640 but with a different root cause. The Rust impl using \`OpenProcessToken(GetCurrentProcess(), ...)\` disagrees with equivalent C# code reading the same process's token externally via \`OpenProcess(pid) → OpenProcessToken(...)\`.

## Repro

cuademo (non-RID-500 admin) on Windows 11 24H2, cua-driver-rs v0.2.13, fresh sign-in (so daemon was spawned by Task Scheduler's AtLogon trigger with RunLevel=Highest):

```
PS> cua-driver call check_permissions
{
  "elevated": false,
  "integrity_level": "Medium",
  "integrity_level_rid": 8192,    # 0x2000 — WRONG
  ...
}
```

Equivalent C# from PowerShell (TokenIL.GetIntegrity using OpenProcess + OpenProcessToken):
```
pid=11356  IL=High (RID=12288)    # 0x3000 — CORRECT
```

Same process. Same primary token. Different read results.

## Hypotheses

1. **Named-pipe impersonation leak**: cua-driver's pipe handler may impersonate the client token (cuademo's Medium IL shell) and not revert before check_permissions runs. \`OpenProcessToken(GetCurrentProcess(), TOKEN_QUERY, ...)\` should return the PRIMARY token regardless of impersonation, but if the windows-rs crate's binding is using something like \`OpenThreadToken\` under the hood (or applying TOKEN_QUERY_SOURCE flags that change behavior), it might return the impersonation token instead.

2. **windows-rs TOKEN_MANDATORY_LABEL struct layout mismatch**: unlikely (0x2000 is too specific to be misaligned-pointer garbage) but worth checking.

3. **Pseudo-handle quirk**: \`GetCurrentProcess()\` returns the pseudo-handle \`HANDLE(-1)\`. Maybe \`OpenProcessToken\` on the pseudo-handle behaves differently than on a real handle from \`OpenProcess(GetCurrentProcessId())\`.

## Fix direction (suggested order)

1. **Change \`OpenProcessToken(GetCurrentProcess(), ...)\` to \`OpenProcessToken(OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, GetCurrentProcessId()), ...)\`** — mirrors the working C# code path that returns the right answer. If this fixes it, hypothesis 3 was right.

2. **Add \`RevertToSelf()\` at start of check_permissions** — ensures the calling thread isn't impersonating anything before the query. If (1) doesn't fix it but this does, hypothesis 1 was right and we have a broader impersonation-leak issue across other tools.

3. **Read TokenLinkedToken too** — for diagnostic purposes, dump both primary token IL and linked token IL. Helps understand the token layout for Task-Scheduler-spawned processes.

## Why this matters

The honest \`elevated\` field is the user-facing diagnostic for "did my autostart-elevation strategy work?". A misreporting check_permissions sent the cuademo dogfood down a 90-minute rabbit hole (#1640's filing). Even after that fix, the report is still wrong — and once again it's making us doubt whether \`RunLevel=Highest\` works. It does. The reporter doesn't.

## Surfaced

cuademo dogfood, v0.2.13 fresh install on Windows 11 24H2, autostart task registered + AtLogon-triggered. Direct Win32 read confirms daemon at IL=0x3000; cua-driver call check_permissions returns IL=0x2000.

title: install.ps1: cua-driver not resolvable in the SAME shell after irm | iex — /Users/francesco/cuaath needs in-process update
body:
## Summary

After \`irm install.ps1 | iex\` succeeds in PowerShell, \`cua-driver --version\` fails with "not recognized" in the SAME shell. The installer registers the bin dir on the User PATH (registry), but PowerShell's \`\$env:Path\` was cached at process start — the registry update doesn't propagate to the running shell.

The install message acknowledges this:
> cua-driver will resolve in any NEW PowerShell window.
> In THIS shell, invoke via the full Binary path printed below.

But that's a usability papercut: the user just ran the install one-liner, sees "0.2.16 installed", and the natural next command (\`cua-driver --version\`) fails. They have to open a new tab or remember to copy the full binary path.

## Repro

```powershell
PS> irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.ps1 | iex
...
cua-driver-rs 0.2.16 installed.
Added C:\Users\cuademo\AppData\Local\Programs\Cua\cua-driver\bin to your User PATH.
  cua-driver will resolve in any NEW PowerShell window.

PS> cua-driver --version
cua-driver : The term 'cua-driver' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, ...
```

## Fix

\`install.ps1\` runs inside the user's current shell via \`iex\` — it CAN write to that shell's \`\$env:Path\`. After updating the persistent User PATH, also prepend the bin dir to the current process's \`\$env:Path\` if not already there. Then update the post-install hint to say "available immediately in this shell" instead of "in any NEW PowerShell window".

Sketch:

```powershell
# After the User PATH update:
if ($env:Path -notlike "*$VisibleBinDir*") {
    $env:Path = "$VisibleBinDir;$env:Path"
}
```

That's a 4-line patch in install.ps1's Add-Bin-To-PATH function. Plus the hint-message update.

## Why this matters

The "fresh install" flow is the most visible UX path for cua-driver-rs. A user hitting "command not found" right after a successful install reads as broken. The fix is trivial and removes the confusion entirely.

## Surfaced

cuademo v0.2.16 fresh-install dogfood:
```
==> Added C:\Users\cuademo\AppData\Local\Programs\Cua\cua-driver\bin to your User PATH.
... cua-driver-rs 0.2.16 installed.

PS> cua-driver --version
cua-driver : The term 'cua-driver' is not recognized ...
```

The user explicitly noted "the cua-driver alias only works on new tabs".

title: fix(cua-driver)(#1651): install.ps1 updates current shell's PATH for immediate cua-driver resolution

title: fix(autostart): hide console window at logon via PowerShell wrapper
body:
## Problem

The `cua-driver-serve` Scheduled Task launches a visible console window at every interactive logon (issue #1645). `cua-driver.exe` is a CUI binary — without a parent console, Task Scheduler allocates one and it stays on the desktop for the daemon lifetime.

## Fix

Implement **Option 2** from the issue: wrap the task action in a hidden PowerShell launcher.

**Before:**
```
Action: cua-driver.exe serve
```

**After:**
```
Action: powershell.exe -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -NonInteractive
        -Command "Start-Process -FilePath <exe>
                  -ArgumentList 'serve' -WindowStyle Hidden
                  -WorkingDirectory <home>"
```

`Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden` spawns the daemon fully detached. The `powershell.exe` wrapper exits immediately, leaving only `cua-driver.exe` in the process tree. No visible window, no flash.

Fixes #1645

Dev-script polish so the local-build install loop matches what end users experience via \`install.ps1\`.

title: agent-cursor overlay should default to disabled at daemon startup (opt-in via set_agent_cursor_enabled)
body:
## Summary

The agent-cursor overlay window (\`Cua.AgentCursorOverlay.default\` per PR #1656; was \`TropeCUA.AgentCursorOverlay\`) is created at \`cua-driver serve\` startup with \`WS_VISIBLE\` set. It's a transparent click-through layered window that visualizes where the agent is moving / clicking, similar to the macOS cua-driver agent cursor.

The window is harmless in practice (transparent, no focus theft, not in taskbar) but it IS top-level + \`WS_VISIBLE\` per Win32. This means:

1. \`EnumWindows\` enumeration tools (Spy++, Process Explorer, our own \`list_windows\`) show it as a visible window owned by the daemon.
2. It registers as a top-level window from the moment \`cua-driver serve\` starts — even if the user has no agent / no automation in flight. They opted into auto-starting the daemon at logon (Scheduled Task) but didn't explicitly opt into "show a cursor overlay."
3. Some screen-recording / accessibility tooling treats every WS_VISIBLE top-level window as worth iterating, slightly inflating the "windows on screen" count.

## Proposal

Make the overlay **default to disabled** when \`cua-driver serve\` starts. The overlay only gets enabled when:

- The MCP client calls \`set_agent_cursor_enabled\` with \`enabled=true\`, OR
- The user passes \`cua-driver serve --enable-cursor-overlay\` (CLI flag for users who DO want the overlay visible by default)

The overlay window is then created lazily on first \`set_agent_cursor_enabled\` call, OR the window is created hidden (\`!WS_VISIBLE\`) at startup and only shown on enable.

## Why this is consistent with the rest of cua-driver

- \`cua-driver serve\` is supposed to be a quiet background daemon. The autostart \`cua-driver-serve\` Scheduled Task (#1630/#1654) goes out of its way to spawn the daemon without a visible console window. Spawning a separate visible overlay window from the same daemon contradicts that intent.
- The MCP tool surface already has explicit toggles (\`set_agent_cursor_enabled\`, \`set_agent_cursor_motion\`). The current default ("enabled") makes those tools feel like the wrong direction — you'd expect \`enabled\` to be off until requested.
- The overlay is most useful when a human is WATCHING the agent work. For headless / unattended automation scenarios (CI, server-side agent runs), it's just dead pixels in the desktop window list.

## Implementation sketch

\`crates/platform-windows/src/overlay.rs\`:

1. Create the window with \`WS_POPUP\` only (no \`WS_VISIBLE\`) at startup. Window exists but is hidden.
2. \`set_agent_cursor_enabled(enabled=true)\` calls \`ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_SHOWNA)\`. \`enabled=false\` calls \`ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_HIDE)\`.
3. CLI flag \`cua-driver serve --enable-cursor-overlay\` defaults the enabled state to true so users who want the current behavior can opt in.
4. \`crates/cua-driver/src/serve.rs\`: thread the flag through the cursor init call.

Mirror changes on Linux (\`platform-linux/src/overlay.rs\`) — create with \`override_redirect = true\` + \`map_window\` deferred until enable.

## Backward compat

Behavior change for users who relied on the overlay being visible-by-default. Those users get a one-line migration: \`cua-driver serve --enable-cursor-overlay\` or call \`set_agent_cursor_enabled\` from their agent. Worth a CHANGELOG note + post-install hint mention.

## Surfaced

During the cuademo dogfood — \`EnumWindows\` on the daemon's pid returned a visible \`Cua.AgentCursorOverlay.default\` window even though no agent was driving the daemon. User flagged it as unexpected: "I asked for a hidden daemon, why is there a visible overlay window?"

Related to (but separate from) #1645 which was about the daemon's console window specifically.

title: docs(install.ps1): remove false claim that UWP needs the elevated autostart task
body:
## Summary

install.ps1's post-install hint was telling users:

> Without auto-start, the daemon runs at the user's default token IL.
> That's fine for Win32 + Chromium apps. UWP / AppContainer apps
> (Calculator, modern Settings, Photos) need the elevated autostart task.

The "**UWP needs the elevated autostart task**" claim is wrong. Empirical verification during 2026-05-22 Windows dogfood arc:

| Account | IL | Calculator UIA \`element_count\` |
|---|---|---|
| fbonacci (RID 500) at High IL via RunLevel=Highest task | High | **41** |
| cuademo (regular admin, UAC-split) running cua-driver directly from her PowerShell | **Medium** | **41** |

So UWP / AppContainer UIA works at Medium IL too. The IL gating turned out to be a methodological artifact — earlier 0-element results came from running tests in non-interactive SSH / psexec contexts, which can't drive UIA cross-AppContainer correctly **regardless of IL**. Live RDP sessions just work at any IL level.

Replacing the hint with the honest reason RunLevel=Highest is useful: elevated operations like registry / services / ACL writes the daemon may need. UWP is not the differentiator.

## Follow-ups
- #1602 (EV cert + UIAccess for UWP) will be closed — premise was wrong
- #1638 (RunLevel=Highest doesn't elevate) will be closed — both premises wrong
- #1657 (overlay default disabled) will be closed — overlay is intentional UX

title: fix(computer-server): route single printable keypress through type_text
body:
## Problem

`keypress()` with a single printable character (e.g. `'a'`, `'/'`) was routed through `press_key()`, which uses pynput `keyboard.press/release` — a physical-key path that follows the active input source. Under a Russian, CJK, or any non-Latin layout this inserts the layout-mapped character instead of the intended ASCII one, breaking Finder path entry and any agent workflow that types text character-by-character.

## Fix

Detect single printable characters via `unicodedata.category` and route them through `type_text()` instead. `type_text()` uses pynput `keyboard.type()` which inserts the literal Unicode codepoint regardless of the active input source.

**Detection rule:** `len(key) == 1 and category not in (Cc, Cs, Cn)`

| Input | Before | After |
|-------|--------|-------|
| `'a'`, `'/'`, `'0'`, `' '` | `press_key` (layout-dependent) | `type_text` (layout-independent) |
| `'return'`, `'tab'`, `'escape'` | `press_key` | `press_key` (unchanged) |
| `['cmd', 'shift', 'g']` | `hotkey` | `hotkey` (unchanged) |

## Tests

10 unit tests in `test_keypress_layout.py` — all passing.

Fixes #1605

title: fix(cua-driver-rs): 3 cli.rs bugs — BOM-in-stdin, daemon image merge, --socket plumbing
body:
## Summary

Three small fixes to `cua-driver call` discovered during overnight dogfooding on the Windows VM (cua-driver-rs v0.2.18). All are real bugs with concrete repros + tests; none changes documented behavior — they fix paths that *should* have worked but didn't.

### 1. UTF-8 BOM in stdin payloads silently rejected (`5f033aed`)

PowerShell 5.1's `Set-Content -Encoding utf8` writes a 3-byte BOM (\`EF BB BF\`) at file start. When that file is piped into \`cua-driver call <tool>\`, the cli's \`read_stdin_json\` failed to parse and the tool returned the misleading error \"Missing required integer field pid\" (because every field looked missing).

Fix: strip the BOM in \`read_stdin_json\` before serde_json::from_str. Two unit tests guard the behavior (BOM present + BOM absent).

**Repro before fix:**
\`\`\`powershell
Set-Content -Path .\\req.json -Value '{\"pid\":99999}' -Encoding utf8   # writes BOM
Get-Content .\\req.json -Raw | cua-driver call list_windows
# → \"Missing required integer field pid.\"
\`\`\`

### 2. Daemon-forwarded screenshot dropped the image bytes (`cf8f3ca9`)

\`cua-driver call screenshot\` over a daemon socket returned \`{\"format\": \"png\", \"width\": ..., \"height\": ...}\` and silently discarded the \`screenshot_png_b64\` field. The in-process path was correct; only the daemon-forwarding branch in \`run_call\` was missing the image merge into structuredContent.

Fix: in the daemon-forwarding branch, walk the response \`content\` array, capture any \`type: image\` item, and merge it into \`structuredContent\` as \`screenshot_png_b64\` + \`screenshot_mime_type\` — same shape as the in-process path produces.

### 3. \`--socket\` flag wasn't wired for \`Command::Call\` (`d375e053`)

The cli-reference docs document \`--socket\` for \`cua-driver call\`, but \`Command::Call\` didn't actually accept it. Added the \`socket\` field to \`Command::Call\` (parsed in both call sites), added a \`socket_override\` param to \`run_call\`, and added an integration regression test (\`test_call_screenshot_via_daemon_emits_b64\`).

The new test is \`@unittest.skipIf(sys.platform == \"win32\")\` because the subprocess-spawned daemon on Windows CI runs in Session 0 (no graphics → BitBlt returns \`0x80070006\`). It exercises the regression on macOS + Linux runners.

## Diff

- \`crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs\` — BOM strip + image merge + \`socket_override\` param
- \`crates/cua-driver/src/main.rs\` — \`Command::Call\` socket field plumbed
- \`tests/integration/test_cli.py\` — \`test_call_screenshot_via_daemon_emits_b64\`

~140 LOC across 3 files. All three commits independently revertable.

## Docs

No docs change needed — \`cli-reference.mdx\` already documents \`--socket\` for \`call\` (the docs were aspirational; this PR aligns implementation with documentation). \`mcp-tools.mdx\` is auto-generated from Swift sources and these are internal cli plumbing fixes that don't change Swift's tool surface.

## Test plan

- [x] \`python3 -m unittest test_cli\` → 17/17 passing on macOS
- [x] Verified live on Windows VM (cuademo Session 9) — see [`OVERNIGHT_HANDOFF_CHECKS.md`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/tree/overnight/cursor-overlay-shared-util) section 2
- [ ] CI green

title: feat(cua-driver-rs): screenshot defaults — jpeg @ 85 + max_image_dimension 1568
body:
## Summary

Two behavior changes to the \`screenshot\` tool on all 3 Rust platforms, motivated by the Windows VM dogfood overnight finding that screenshots were coming back at **~10.5 MB**:

| Setting | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| \`max_image_dimension\` default | \`0\` (no cap) | **\`1568\`** | Swift parity (\`CuaDriverConfig.defaultMaxImageDimension\` is 1568). The 0 default was a Rust-only regression. |
| \`screenshot\` tool \`format\` default | \`png\` | **\`jpeg\`** | Agents want compact images for vision-context. Schema still accepts both; PNG is opt-in via \`{\"format\":\"png\"}\`. **Diverges from Swift** (Swift still \`png\`). |
| \`screenshot\` tool \`quality\` default | \`95\` (macos+windows) / \`85\` (linux) | **\`85\`** everywhere | Sweet spot for screen content; q=95 was actually larger than PNG for solid-color UI. Linux already at 85; macOS Claude-Code-compat tool also 85. |

## Measured impact (macOS, 3840×2160 → 1568×882)

| Config | Decoded bytes |
|---|---|
| **before tonight** (PNG, no cap) | 4,866,498 |
| jpeg @ 85, no cap | 825,429 (5.9×) |
| jpeg @ 85, cap 1568 | **167,895** (**29×**) |

Same query on Windows VM: ~10.5 MB → **85 KB** (125× reduction).

## Files

- \`crates/platform-{windows,linux,macos}/src/tools/{impl_,screenshot}.rs\` — defaults + tool descriptions
- \`crates/platform-{windows,linux,macos}/src/tools/{impl_,mod}.rs\` — \`DriverConfig::default().max_image_dimension\`
- \`tests/integration/test_cursor_visibility.py\` — pass explicit \`format=png\` so the per-pixel cursor-colour decode keeps working
- \`crates/cua-driver/tests/mcp_protocol_test.rs\` — outdated docstring
- \`PARITY.md\` — moves \"quality 95\" out of Fixed and adds two Intentional Rust-only rows; new Fixed row for max_image_dimension

## Compat

The CLI's \`screenshot_png_b64\` structuredContent key keeps its name — it's a cross-implementation contract (Swift \`AppState.swift:97\`, get_window_state, both SKILL.md files, all integration tests). The companion \`screenshot_mime_type\` field reports the actual MIME (\`image/jpeg\` for the new default).

Users with a persisted \`~/Library/Application Support/cua-driver/config.json\` that explicitly sets \`max_image_dimension\` (even to 0 for \"no cap\") keep their value — the config loader only falls back to the default when the field is absent. Fresh installs get 1568.

## Docs

- \`mcp-tools.mdx\` is auto-generated from Swift sources, which still default to PNG — **not regenerated in this PR**. The docs will become accurate when Swift adopts the same defaults (tracked as a follow-up parity question).
- \`PARITY.md\` updated this PR.

title: feat(cua-driver-rs): single shared post-install-hints.txt for all 4 Rust installers
body:
## Summary

The 4 cua-driver-rs installer scripts each inlined their own post-install hint block — with predictable drift:

| Installer | Skill hint | MCP hint | Try-it | Docs link |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `_install-rust.sh` (canonical Unix Rust path) | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `install.ps1` (canonical Windows Rust) | ❌ | ❌ | partial | ✅ |
| `install-local.sh` (Rust dev Unix) | ❌ | ❌ | partial | ❌ |
| `install-local.ps1` (Rust dev Windows) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

Same hint text would need to land in 4 files in 2 shells. Adding a new MCP client or renaming a CLI flag meant grepping 4 files.

## The fix

**Single text file** `libs/cua-driver/scripts/post-install-hints.txt` with `{{BINARY}}` placeholder. Each installer renders it with shell-native substitution:

| Installer | How it renders |
|---|---|
| `_install-rust.sh` | `curl` from raw.githubusercontent.com + `sed` |
| `install.ps1` | `Invoke-WebRequest` + PS `-replace` |
| `install-local.sh` | direct disk read from `../cua-driver/scripts/` + `sed` |
| `install-local.ps1` | direct disk read + `-replace` |

Each has a **one-line essentials fallback** if the .txt is unreachable (network failure on remote installs, missing file on local) so users always get enough to recover.

## What stays inline per installer

OS-specific bits — 4–6 lines each, per-shell natural, each script targets one OS anyway:
- macOS TCC reminder (`open -n -g -a CuaDriver --args serve`)
- Windows Scheduled-Task autostart
- Linux systemd autostart reference

## Why not a CLI subcommand

An earlier draft of this work added `cua-driver post-install` to the Rust binary and had all 4 installers delegate via `& $installedBinary post-install`. **Reverted** — the chicken-and-egg risk (failed binary install ⇒ no hints either) made the .txt approach safer. The .txt has no runtime dependency; even a totally broken binary install still prints hints.

## Files

- **New**: `libs/cua-driver/scripts/post-install-hints.txt` — the shared text (~50 lines)
- **Edited**: `libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh`, `install.ps1`, `libs/cua-driver-rs/scripts/install-local.sh`, `install-local.ps1` — each replaces inline hints with `.txt` render + keeps install-specific lines (Installed banner, PATH handling, BETA warning, OS-specific autostart)
- **Edited**: `libs/cua-driver-rs/PARITY.md` — new "Installer post-install hints" section documenting the design

Net diff: +194 / −50 LOC across 6 files. Going forward, hint changes happen in **one** place.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash libs/cua-driver-rs/scripts/install-local.sh` on macOS — prints the unified block with `{{BINARY}}` correctly substituted + macOS TCC + LaunchAgent hint
- [ ] `.\install-local.ps1` on Windows VM
- [ ] `irm https://.../install.ps1 | iex` end-to-end (canonical Windows installer, remote fetch path)
- [ ] CI green

title: feat(cua-driver-rs): agent-guidance refactor + uninstall converge + warnings cleanup
body:
## Summary

Four logically-grouped commits, bundled per request (single PR for easier deploy). All originated from a fresh-install dogfood on the cuademo VM — the dogfood surfaced real bugs and a research-backed restructuring opportunity.

### 1. `fix(cua-driver-rs)(uninstall): converge uninstall.{ps1,sh} + UAC self-elevation` (`fca003ec`)

`uninstall.ps1` now self-elevates via UAC when it detects an `-AutoStart` install (the `cua-driver-serve` task at `RunLevel=Highest` plus the High-IL daemon it spawns can't be torn down from a non-elevated same-user shell — silent `Access Denied` on `schtasks /Delete` and `Stop-Process` left dangling state otherwise).

`uninstall.sh` inlines what `_uninstall-rust.sh` used to do — single canonical script per shell, mirroring `uninstall.ps1`'s shape. `_uninstall-rust.sh` deleted; CI workflow + docs updated to match.

### 2. `fix(cua-driver-rs)(install-local.ps1): UTF-8 read for post-install-hints` (`7bc1cf0b`)

PR #1664's rendered `Next steps:` block came out with mojibake on Windows: `•` → `â€¢`, `—` → `â€"`. Cause: `Get-Content -Raw` defaults to Windows-1252 on PS 5.1 when the source file has no BOM. Surgical fix at the one Windows reader (`[System.IO.File]::ReadAllText(..., UTF8)`); the other 3 installers were unaffected so `post-install-hints.txt` stays BOM-free.

### 3. `chore(cua-driver-rs): clean up 30 build warnings in -p cua-driver path` (`5986430b`)

`cargo build --release -p cua-driver` was emitting 28 + 3 warnings before; zero after. Mechanical: dead imports/mut/writes, `#[allow(dead_code)]` on cross-platform stubs, `let _ =` on Win32 teardown calls, module-scope `#![allow(non_upper_case_globals)]` for external `UIA_*ControlTypeId` constants.

### 4. `feat(cua-driver-rs): agent-guidance refactor — Skills / MCP-instructions / per-tool` (`7ab537c1`)

Informed by a survey of how OSS computer-use tools (Playwright MCP, browser-use, Goose, Open Interpreter, Anthropic computer-use cookbook) push usage guidance to LLM agents, cross-checked against the MCP spec + Claude Skills convention:

- **SKILL.md: 911 → 493 lines** (Anthropic's documented limit is 500). Extracted macOS-specific content (no-foreground contract, AppleScript prohibitions, AXMenuBar navigation, SkyLight click dispatch, Apple-Events JS bridge) into a new `MACOS.md` mirroring the existing `WINDOWS.md` / `LINUX.md` / `WEB_APPS.md` companion files.
- **`AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS` (MCP `instructions` field)**: converted from `const &str` to `fn -> String` templated per-host via `cfg!(target_os = ...)`. macOS clients see "AX", Windows "UIA", Linux "AT-SPI" — Goose's `ComputerController` pattern. Added a closing line pointing skill-aware harnesses at `SKILL.md` + the per-OS companion (free description-match hint for Claude Code / Codex / OpenClaw / OpenCode; ignored by Hermes / Cursor / generic MCP clients).
- **Thicker per-tool descriptions** on `click` + `screenshot` (all 3 platforms): "prefer element_index over pixel coords" editorial on `click`, `max_image_dimension=1568` default + pointer to `get_window_state` on `screenshot`. Per-call gating rather than per-session — Anthropic computer-use cookbook shape.

## Out of scope (flagged here for follow-up)

- **Sibling Swift skill at `libs/cua-driver/Skills/cua-driver/SKILL.md`** is 887 lines — also over Anthropic's 500-line ceiling. Same refactor pattern applies (extract macOS-specific content into a companion file); not done in this PR because it's the Swift driver's skill, not the Rust port.
- **Pre-existing daemon hot loop on this Windows VM**: idle daemon CPU is ~95% (HEAD has the same behaviour — bisected by stashing this PR's changes, rebuilding HEAD, observing the same CPU burn). Likely the cursor-overlay thread's `SetTimer(hwnd, 1, 8, None)` running at 125 Hz unconditionally. Worth gating to "spin only when the overlay is actually visible/active" in a separate PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --release -p cua-driver` clean (zero warnings)
- [x] `install-local.ps1` runs end-to-end on a freshly-wiped Windows VM
- [x] Rendered `Next steps:` block shows proper `•` bullets and `—` em-dashes
- [x] `uninstall.ps1` self-elevates correctly after an `-AutoStart` install (UAC prompt, fully removes daemon + task + `~\.cua-driver\` + skill junctions)
- [ ] `uninstall.sh` smoke on macOS + Linux (needs reviewer host to verify — no Mac/Linux VM available this session)
- [ ] Screenshot defaults end-to-end (`jpeg @ 85`, `≤1568px`) — verified via dump-docs schema; runtime call hangs in Claude Code subprocess context (pre-existing daemon hot loop, see "Out of scope"), needs interactive RDP retest
- [ ] Cross-check the rendered MCP `instructions` field from an MCP client (handshake response shows OS-templated content + skill pointer)

title: feat(cua-driver-rs): unify browser_eval + page into one cross-platform tool
body:
## Summary

Six logical commits. Drops the duplicate `browser_eval` tool, promotes `page` to cross-platform via a new `PageBackend` trait, ships Windows (UIA) + Linux (AT-SPI) backends. macOS keeps its Apple Events / Electron-CDP / AX-WebView routing — strict refactor for callers.

Informed by a 3-agent research spike + an empirical Windows-Edge test battery (see follow-up below).

### Why drop `browser_eval`

| | macOS | Windows | Linux | Swift driver |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `browser_eval` (pre-PR) | ✅ registered (redundant alongside `page`) | ✅ registered (sole option) | ✅ registered (sole option) | **never existed** |
| `page` (pre-PR) | ✅ registered (4 actions, 4 backends) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ canonical |

`browser_eval` only ever existed in the Rust port — it was CDP-only, single-action (`Runtime.evaluate`), and on macOS shipped alongside the strictly-more-capable `page`. This PR removes the duplicate, brings Windows + Linux up to `page`'s 3-action surface, and re-syncs Rust ↔ Swift parity.

### What each platform now does for `page`

| Action | macOS | Windows | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| `get_text` | Apple Events → `document.body.innerText` (BrowserJs); CDP for Electron; AX walk for WKWebView | **UIA `TextPattern.DocumentRange.GetText(-1)` on the web Document element** — no `--remote-debugging-port` needed | AT-SPI text walk |
| `query_dom` | Apple Events `querySelectorAll` JS | **UIA `FindAll(TreeScope_Subtree, …)` with CSS→ControlType mapping** (`a[href]`→Hyperlink, `button`→Button, `input`→Edit, `h1`-`h6`→Heading, `li`→ListItem, `img`→Image, `[role=*]`→ControlType). `#id`/`.class`/`[role=*]` post-filter via `AutomationId`. `[data-*]` errors with a pointer at `execute_javascript`. | AT-SPI role-based query |
| `execute_javascript` | Apple Events JS; Electron→CDP | **CDP via the new shared `mcp_server::cdp` helper**, discovers port via `$CUA_DRIVER_CDP_PORT` env var. Returns an actionable error when not set. | CDP via the same shared helper |
| `enable_javascript_apple_events` | full impl | "not supported on this platform" via the trait's default impl | same |

The Windows UIA path is research-validated: same pattern NVDA, pywinauto, and AccessKit-consumers all use. Chrome 138+ (June 2025) exposes native UIA on by default; before that it was IA2→UIA proxy — both work.

### Architecture

- **`crates/mcp-server/src/page.rs`** (new, 240 lines) — `PageBackend` trait + cross-platform `PageTool`. Tool name, schema, and action dispatch live here; each platform supplies a backend.
- **`crates/mcp-server/src/cdp.rs`** (new, extracted from `browser_eval.rs`) — shared raw-TCP CDP `Runtime.evaluate` helper. Reused by Windows + Linux JS-exec paths.
- **`crates/mcp-server/src/browser_eval.rs`** — **deleted**.
- **`crates/platform-macos/src/tools/page.rs`** — rewritten as `MacOsPageBackend` impl, all 4 actions preserved.
- **`crates/platform-windows/src/tools/page.rs`** (new, 449 lines) — `WindowsPageBackend` with UIA + shared CDP.
- **`crates/platform-linux/src/tools/page.rs`** (new, 159 lines) — `LinuxPageBackend` with AT-SPI + shared CDP.
- Each platform's tool-registration entry point constructs and registers its `PageTool` with the right backend.

## Verification

- `cargo build --release -p cua-driver` on `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` → **0 warnings, 0 errors**
- `cargo test --release -p cua-driver --test mcp_protocol_test` → **28/28 passed**
- `cargo test --release -p platform-windows` → **16/16 passed**
- macOS + Linux compile-checks deferred to reviewer host (no Mac/Linux VM this session). The modules are `cfg`-gated cleanly; behaviour-equivalent to the previous macOS-only `page` tool plus new platform impls.

## Explicit follow-ups (deliberately deferred)

1. **CDP-port discovery on Windows + Linux currently reads `$CUA_DRIVER_CDP_PORT`.** Richer discovery (parsing `--remote-debugging-port` from the live browser's command line — `NtQueryInformationProcess` / PEB read on Windows, `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` on Linux) is a clean follow-up. Today's error message points users at the env var.
2. **🎯 UIA-JS-exec primary path on Windows.** A separate empirical Edge test battery this session confirmed that **UIA `ValuePattern::SetValue` on the address-bar Edit element with `javascript:try{document.title=…}` then InvokePattern Enter** executes arbitrary JS in the existing tab's existing DOM context — no `--remote-debugging-port`, no extension, no driver. Chromium's omnibox `javascript:` paste-strip is gated on user-input tracking and UIA writes route through `EditModel::SetUserText()` without setting the flag. **This will land in a follow-up PR** that upgrades `execute_javascript` on Windows from CDP-required to UIA-primary + CDP-fallback. Tracked separately so this PR's review surface stays focused on the unification.
3. **`#id` selector** uses `AutomationId` on Windows — works for Chromium's common case but isn't universally guaranteed. Full IA2 `attributes`-string parse (via `LegacyIAccessiblePattern.GetIAccessible()` → `QI(IAccessible2)`) is a richer follow-up.
4. **`[role=*]` ARIA mapping** is the common subset (button, link, textbox, heading, image, listitem). Extending to the full ARIA taxonomy is mechanical.
5. **macOS `BrowserJs::CdpClient` is its own internal CDP client**, predating the new shared `mcp_server::cdp` helper. Could be deduped — small win, not load-bearing.
6. **Linux page backend isn't runtime-tested.** No Linux VM available this session. Builds clean; assumes AT-SPI roles match the implementer's mapping table. Small risk of role-name skew across desktops/distros.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --release -p cua-driver` clean on Windows
- [x] `cargo test --release -p cua-driver --test mcp_protocol_test` green (28/28)
