title: Fix cross-platform CUA driver GUI verification
body:
## Summary

This PR hardens the CUA driver GUI verification path across Windows, macOS, and Linux. It fixes cases where platform GUI tests skipped the real assertion path, could not address native controls exposed by app frameworks, relied on stale accessibility-tree assumptions, or depended on downloaded fixture apps that drifted away from repo-owned harnesses.

The latest Windows pass also addresses partner-reported 0.7.1 findings around background keyboard false-success reporting, Chrome/background click refusal diagnostics, packaged Notepad launch verification, and the RDP-backed runner needed for real cursor/focus assertions.

## What This Fixes

### Windows interactive desktop detection and RDP guard runner

- Keeps Windows Session 0 as a clear non-interactive runner signal for SSH and service-launched processes.
- Replaces the named `OpenWindowStationW("WinSta0")` probe with the process's attached window station, active input desktop, thread desktop, and foreground HWND diagnostics.
- Distinguishes a locked/non-Default desktop from an unlocked idle `Default` desktop that simply has no foreground window yet.
- Lets GUI tests seed the foreground with `focus-monitor-win` when the desktop is otherwise valid.
- Adds `CUA_REQUIRE_GUI=1` so dedicated GUI runners fail closed instead of skip-passing when the desktop is unsuitable.
- Updates Windows `doctor` output with the same desktop-state summary.

### Windows guard UX and launch behavior

- Reorders guard tests so the target harness launches first, then `focus-monitor-win` becomes the measured foreground sentinel.
- Adds stronger cleanup for leftover focus monitor, Electron harness, and driver processes.
- Makes the cursor pixel assertion deterministic by using an explicit cursor id and motion settings.
- Updates the repo-local Electron harness to show main and child windows inactive, allowing launch/background assertions without stealing focus.
- Adds a shared web child-window control so background click can assert a real window-open side effect.
- Verifies `launch_app({"name":"Notepad","start_minimized":true})` resolves packaged Notepad through its AUMID and returns usable pid/window metadata on the Azure Windows RDP VM.

### Windows W1/W8 reporting hardening

- Changes background `type_text` on the unreadable PostMessage path from a checked success to “sent, not verified” with structured `verified:false`, `verify:"unreadable"`, and foreground escalation guidance.
- Changes background `press_key` PostMessage success to the same unverified reporting shape, so callers no longer see a confirmed keypress when the driver cannot prove it landed.
- Preserves coordinate-injection failure causes for click, double-click, and right-click instead of collapsing them into a generic class-level `background_unavailable` message.
- Adds structured refusal codes for `background_occluded`, `background_uipi_blocked`, and generic `background_unavailable`.
- Adds unit/guard coverage for these reporting contracts.

### Windows WPF and WinUI3 harness coverage

- Updates UIA walking so enabled actionable elements can be indexed even when the framework reports them as offscreen.
- Adds a narrow fallback for WPF menu items that are visible and enabled but do not expose the expected cached action pattern.
- Restores the WPF scroll test to the background `WM_VSCROLL` path and narrows the silent-drop guard so scroll messages are not rejected with pointer click/move cases.
- Uses explicit foreground delivery where WPF text input requires it.
- Reorders the WinUI3 fixture so radio, flyout, popup, and related controls are discoverable before the long scroll region dominates the UIA walk.

### Shared Electron and Tauri harnesses

- Removes the old macOS pytest Electron fixture that downloaded a prebuilt `.app` release zip.
- Adds a repo-local Tauri harness under `libs/cua-driver/tests/fixtures/apps/cross-platform/tauri` that embeds the shared web DOM.
- Adds the Windows Tauri ICO asset required by `tauri-build` so the harness builds on both macOS and Windows.
- Builds Electron and Tauri from repo-local source and stages deterministic `harness-electron` / `harness-tauri` outputs for macOS, Linux, and Windows.
- Updates Windows guard/modality tests and sandbox staging to use the repo-local harness executables instead of downloaded desktop-test-app binaries.
- Removes the tracked downloaded Tauri macOS binary from the Python fixture assets.

### macOS harness and capture verification

- Updates macOS GUI harness tests to use the daemon proxy path where needed.
- Covers the capture and desktop-scope paths that require local GUI permissions and daemon-backed execution.
- Includes build/runtime adjustments for the Swift-linked driver pieces so local test and install flows can find the required runtime consistently.

### Linux harness and accessibility behavior

- Updates Linux GUI verification around AT-SPI, capture, input, overlay, and Wayland/X11 support paths exercised by the ignored GUI suites.
- Fixes the GTK popover test assumption: GTK/AT-SPI can expose the popover content in the tree before it is shown, so the test now asserts an explicit `popover_open=False` to `popover_open=True` state transition.
- Keeps the headless GUI test flow compatible with Xvfb, DBus, AT-SPI, and a lightweight window manager.

### Test organization and contributor docs

- Removes the legacy Python e2e suite so Rust integration tests are the source of truth for driver behavioral coverage.
- Rehomes repo-local fixture apps and build helpers from `libs/cua-driver/test-harness` to `libs/cua-driver/tests/fixtures`, giving Rust harness tests one neutral fixture root.
- Keeps generated staged apps under ignored `libs/cua-driver/rust/test-apps` and keeps Electron/Tauri build products out of the PR.
- Moves the legacy Windows Sandbox runner out of `libs/cua-driver/rust/sandbox` into `libs/cua-driver/tests/runners/windows-sandbox` and marks it as a non-canonical smoke runner.
- Adds a canonical Rust-only Windows runner at `libs/cua-driver/tests/runners/windows/run-all.ps1` for repo-local fixture suites; optional external-app suites are excluded.
- Ports TextEdit launch-focus coverage into ignored Rust macOS coverage in `modality_launch_focus_macos_test.rs`, and marks LibreOffice as optional explicit-run coverage.
- Adds focused contributor READMEs for the Rust workspace, Rust test matrix, scripts, and fixture app/build folders.
- Adds a small Fumadocs contributor page at `reference/cua-driver/development` that points to repo-local READMEs instead of duplicating implementation detail.
- Removes an uncertain checked-in macOS smoke result file and stale download-era ignore/docs entries.

### Testkit and verification workflow

- Adds small testkit helpers for reading structured tool responses and tree text in the platform harnesses.
- Makes guard-style tests report why they skipped when the runner is not interactive instead of failing with ambiguous platform API errors.
- Adds `libs/cua-driver/scripts/sync-vm-worktree.sh`, a generic helper for syncing the host checkout to verification machines and pulling artifacts back while keeping source commits host-owned.
- Makes touched Windows PowerShell scripts parse cleanly under Windows PowerShell 5.1, which can read UTF-8-without-BOM files as ANSI.

## Validation

- Local host checks passed:
  - `node --check libs/cua-driver/tests/fixtures/apps/cross-platform/electron/main.js`
  - `cargo test --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml -p cua-driver --test modality_launch_focus_macos_test --no-run`
  - `cargo check --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml -p cua-driver --test guard_ux_test`
  - `cargo test --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml -p platform-windows input::delivery::tests::background_unavailable_with_cause_preserves_actuator_failure --no-run`
- Azure Windows VM compile passed: `cargo check -p platform-windows -p cua-driver --tests`.
- Azure Windows VM focused W8 unit passed: `cargo test -p platform-windows input::delivery::tests::background_unavailable_with_cause_preserves_actuator_failure -- --nocapture`.
- Azure Windows VM RDP/scheduled-task GUI run with `CUA_REQUIRE_GUI=1` passed: `cargo test -p cua-driver --test guard_ux_test -- --nocapture --test-threads=1`, 6/6 passed.
- Azure Windows VM packaged Notepad launch check passed via `cua-driver call launch_app`, returning the Notepad AUMID, pid, inactive state, and visible window metadata.
- Azure Windows VM PowerShell 5.1 parser check passed for the touched harness/sandbox scripts, including the moved `tests/runners/windows-sandbox` scripts and `tests/runners/windows/run-all.ps1`.
- Azure Windows VM full harness build passed and staged WPF, WinUI3, WebView2, Electron, and Tauri executables from repo-local sources.
- Azure Windows VM Rust no-run checks passed: `cargo test -p cua-driver --test guard_ux_test --no-run` and `cargo test -p cua-driver --test modality_input_e2e_test --no-run`.
- Windows WPF ignored harness suite passed, 18/18.
- Windows WinUI3 ignored harness suite passed, 7/7.
- Windows SSH/default pass: `cargo test -p cua-driver -p platform-windows -- --nocapture` passed; GUI-only assertions skip explicitly when run outside an interactive desktop.
- Linux default pass: `cargo test -p cua-driver -p platform-linux -- --nocapture` passed.
- Linux ignored GUI suites passed under Xvfb/DBus/AT-SPI for GTK3, capture mode, and desktop scope.
- macOS default and ignored GUI harness passes were verified locally with the daemon proxy path.
- Shared Electron/Tauri harness checks: `bash -n` for build scripts, `git diff --check`, staged-output ignore checks, and targeted sensitive/stale-reference scans passed.
- macOS aggregate harness build passed and staged AppKit, SwiftUI, WKWebView, `CuaTestHarness.Electron.app`, and `CuaTestHarness.Tauri.app` from repo-local sources.
- Tauri harness build passed directly and the staged app plist reports `CuaTestHarness.Tauri`, `com.trycua.harness.tauri`, and executable `CuaTestHarness.Tauri`.

## Latest Cross-Platform Behavioral Matrix

The Rust-owned `cross_platform_behavior_test` now exercises the same classes of
background/foreground, AX, and pixel workflows through repo-local Electron and
Tauri fixtures. Every action is checked against a fresh application-state
oracle; a successful driver response without a state change is a failure.

Latest validation after the driver fixes:

- Linux Electron under Xvfb, xfwm4, DBus, and AT-SPI: **5/5 passed**.
- Windows Electron + Tauri in the active RDP user session: **5/5 passed**.
- Windows guard UX in the active RDP user session: **6/6 passed**.
- Windows background modifier hotkeys: both fixture families now return honest structured refusal rather than a false success.
- macOS Electron + Tauri: AX calculator, background pixel calculator, keyboard, and child-window + foreground drag rows pass; the nested scroll row remains a strict known capability gap.

The underlying fixes include Linux AT-SPI element focus and directional scroll actions, Windows UIA element focus, focused-child key retargeting for WebView2/Tauri, UIA `ScrollPattern` delivery, and stricter Windows background hotkey capability reporting. The private machine journal is intentionally excluded from this PR.

## Notes

- The Windows GUI guard path now has a verified RDP/scheduled-task runner with a real foreground desktop; SSH/service runs still self-skip GUI-only assertions by design.
- Background keyboard delivery on partner GH-hosted Windows still needs environment comparison if their fixture continues to see dropped input. This PR prevents false confirmed success and gives structured escalation, but does not claim every GH-hosted keyboard target now accepts background PostMessage input.
- Background Chrome click refusals now preserve the concrete actuator cause. Restoring any 0.6.8-era apparent no-foreground Chrome click behavior under fully occluded GH-hosted conditions remains separate follow-up work.
- macOS background Chromium pixel click and foreground drag are now fixed in this branch using focus-without-raise plus an explicit active HID gesture. Nested non-focusable web scrolling remains separate follow-up work.
- This PR intentionally omits local verification journals and machine-specific details.

## Verification Update

- macOS local daemon, after `install-local.sh`: Electron and Tauri background pixel calculator **2/2 passed**.
- macOS local daemon, after `install-local.sh`: Electron and Tauri foreground drag/drop **2/2 passed**.
- macOS full Rust matrix: AX, pixel, keyboard, and drag rows pass for both fixtures; editor/save passes, while the nested `overflow:auto` scroll oracle remains at `scroll_offset=0`. A follow-up explicit foreground global-HID wheel experiment also remained unchanged, so this is documented as a renderer/scroll-surface capability gap rather than an assertion relaxation.
- The private cross-platform fix journal is maintained locally and is intentionally not staged or published.

## Verification Update: Linux AT-SPI and Background Keyboard

- Linux WebKitGTK AT-SPI traversal now preserves raw `(bus name, object path)` references for WebProcess descendants, while ordinary unique-name references retain the `atspi` P2P connection path used by Electron/Chromium.
- Linux default Rust matrix under Xvfb, xfwm4, DBus, and AT-SPI: **5/5 passed** with external application-state oracles.
- Linux unit suites: `cua-driver` **67/67** and `platform-linux` **48/48** passed; active protocol/schema checks also passed.
- Linux Chromium/Electron background hotkey behavior is now an explicit structured `background_unavailable` refusal when no EIS backend is available. The X11 probe showed that claiming success for an unfocused renderer was a silent no-op; foreground is the explicit escalation.
- Linux Tauri/WebKitGTK tree readiness is fixed and exposes the full web tree, but the optional strict Tauri input lane remains failing under headless Xvfb (0/5 external input-oracle rows). It is still opt-in via `CUA_INCLUDE_TAURI_LINUX=1` until a principled WebKitGTK input route is implemented.
- The VM sync helper now preserves platform-specific VM-built `rust/test-apps` artifacts during host-to-VM `rsync --delete` syncs.
- macOS was rebuilt with `install-local.sh`; TCC grants remained intact. The known nested web `overflow:auto` scroll gap remains strict and unchanged.
- The Linux interactive CI workflow now installs the Tauri/WebKitGTK build prerequisites required for the repo-local harness; the replacement workflow passed its build and Xvfb/AT-SPI modality job.## CI Architecture Foundation (2026-07-10)

- Adds OS-scoped Rust unit workflows: Linux runs the Linux platform set; Windows runs the Windows platform/UIA set. Shared Rust/testkit and fixture changes trigger both appropriate lanes.
- Adds test-only `CUA_TEST_DRIVER_BIN`, `CUA_TEST_APPS_ROOT`, and `CUA_TEST_WORKSPACE_ROOT` overrides so immutable or remote build outputs can be tested without changing the shipped driver.
- Adds strict fixture preflight for the canonical Rust matrix, preventing missing apps from becoming silent skips in CI or VM runs.

- Adds contributor-facing CI/Nix/test layout documentation and keeps the private machine journal out of the PR.

Validation for this slice: full default macOS `cua-driver` tests passed (69 unit tests plus non-ignored integration tests), `cua-driver-core` and testkit tests passed (including the new relocation override test), and the shared cross-platform matrix compiled with `--no-run`. title: Support OpenAI GPT-5.5 built-in computer tool (`computer_call.actions[]`)
body:
Hi Cua team,

I’m evaluating Cua as the execution/runtime layer for a Linux computer-use demo, and I’d like to clarify the roadmap for OpenAI’s newer built-in computer tool flow.

From the public docs/blog posts and the current agent loop, it looks like Cua already covers two OpenAI-style paths:

1. The older preview path:
   - model: `gpt-5.5`
   - tool: `computer_use_preview`
   - `computer_call.action` with a single action
   - `computer_call_output` for screenshots

2. The newer-model function-call harness path, for example GPT-5.4 support:
   - Responses API
   - a custom `computer` function tool schema
   - model output handled as `function_call`

OpenAI’s current GA computer-use docs now describe a different built-in tool flow:

```json
{
  "model": "gpt-5.5",
  "tools": [{ "type": "computer" }]
}
```

The response uses `computer_call`, with batched `actions[]`, rather than the old single `action` shape.

Do you have plans to support this GPT-5.5 built-in computer tool flow directly in `cua-agent`? In particular:

- selecting the OpenAI loop for `gpt-5.5` / `openai/gpt-5.5`
- sending `tools: [{ "type": "computer" }]` instead of the old `computer_use_preview` schema or a custom function tool
- handling `computer_call.actions[]`
- emitting the correct screenshot output shape expected by the new GA flow

This would make it much easier to use Cua with OpenAI-compatible Responses gateways that already support `gpt-5.5` and the new built-in computer tool, without relying on the deprecated preview protocol or a custom function-call harness.

Thanks!

title: test(cua-driver): converge Rust desktop E2E contracts
body:
## Why

The desktop suites mixed unit checks, shell-generated summaries, one-off guards, and GUI behavior tests. Missing cells could disappear, setup failures could produce reduced green runs, and a successful tool response could be mistaken for input delivery.

This PR makes the Rust harnesses the source of truth for desktop behavior. Repo-local applications expose observable state, and every action must prove either its external effect or an exact structured refusal. Background actions also prove that they did not steal focus, raise the target, move the real cursor, or leak input.

## Canonical test model

- Unit and protocol tests stay desktop-independent and video-free.
- Electron and Tauri share one 36-cell catalog per app. macOS also runs a native WKWebView host.
- Native harness owners use the same typed result and evidence contract.
- AX/PX targeting and foreground/background delivery are dimensions of each action.
- Focus, z-order, cursor, leaked-input, capture, and desktop-scope checks attach to the actions that need them.
- Contributors run `all`; CI partitions shared, native, and capture work only as internal jobs.

Each result records platform, display server, harness, action, targeting, delivery, scope, backend route, expected and observed behavior, independent oracles, duration, and evidence. The reporter rejects missing, duplicate, undeclared, contradictory, or evidence-less rows.

## Driver and harness fixes

### Evidence and reporting

- Added source, fixture, accessibility, capture, GUI-session, and playable-video preflights.
- Resolves one immutable source SHA per workflow and records it in every summary and environment record.
- Added a physically foreground, fully occluding sentinel for background actions.
- Requires an allowed structured refusal plus clean desktop-side-effect observations.
- Records a full-desktop MP4 for each canonical cell and before/after evidence for targeted actions.
- Added a compact coverage grid and artifact-linked row for each cell.
- Isolated process-global recording hook phases so parallel unit tests cannot consume another test's before/after capture.

### Linux

- Replaced X11 false-success paths with foreground XTest delivery, semantic background delivery where proven, and exact refusals elsewhere.
- Added generic `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` discovery, native wlroots capture and recording, stable window identity, compositor-aware geometry, and strict session preflights.
- Added GNOME WinRects geometry and activation plus persistent portal/libei input with revocable grants.
- Preserves 64-bit Wayland identities, resolves connection-local toplevel IDs by stable process and title data, and reconstructs renderer origins for targeted PX input.
- Packages `libxkbcommon`, portal/libei support, the nested compositor, and source-owned Rust tests through Nix.
- Restored the optional `cua-compositor` as a separate experimental environment with a versioned acknowledged protocol, PID targeting, exact resource errors, focus and z-order observation, scene geometry queries, direct pointer and keyboard routes, and typed evidence.
- Makes nested pointer hit-testing target-subtree-local so an occluding sentinel cannot intercept a background action. Renderer child surfaces reuse their bound pointer resource or fall back to the owning root.
- Keeps standard Wayland and the private nested route separate in result metadata and public documentation.

### Windows

- Restored occluded Electron AX/PX single-left clicks through the proven background-safe `PostMessage` route.
- Proved occluded Electron child-window delivery; unsupported Chromium gestures retain exact refusals.
- Corrected foreground PX activation and renderer keyboard targeting.
- Added canonical WPF and WebView2 PX background-left-click rows with fixture-owned state and desktop-side-effect oracles.
- Added WPF background combo selection and an exact WPF background-drag refusal.
- Made `start_minimized` fail closed before spawning when Windows cannot guarantee no activation.
- Reports minimized windows truthfully, filters them from `on_screen_only`, and restores them through the existing `bring_to_front` tool.

### macOS

- Restored PX background left-click delivery through AX hit-testing for Electron, Tauri, and AppKit without focus changes.
- Fixed the first-character loss in foreground PX typing.
- Converts silent background scroll and drag no-effects into exact `background_unavailable` refusals.
- Added the native WKWebView host to the complete shared catalog.
- Added AppKit scroll, right/double click, slider drag, and background-drag contracts.
- Added SwiftUI background AX click/value rows and foreground popover state verification.
- Fixed desktop-scope HID delivery, fixture stability, per-connection daemon sessions, and structured refusal propagation.
- Preserves the installed app's TCC identity during local installation.

## Cleanup

- Removed the synthetic calculator fixture and duplicate calculator tests.
- Removed old guard, modality, delivery, and legacy shared owners after mapping useful assertions into typed action rows.
- Removed shell and PowerShell behavioral inference from Cargo output.
- Keeps software-dependent checks such as LibreOffice outside canonical `all`.
- Added `libs/cua-driver/docs/action-support.md`, an evidence journal, and the public [Platform Support](https://cua.ai/docs/reference/cua-driver/platform-support) reference.\n- Split the validation model into [How Cua Driver Is Validated](https://cua.ai/docs/concepts/how-cua-driver-is-validated), covering source-built harnesses, independent oracles, retained evidence, and maintainer-triggered release validation.\n- Added a cross-OS [Platform Roadmap](https://cua.ai/docs/reference/cua-driver/platform-roadmap) that separates evidence gaps, engineering work, experimental environments, and hard OS boundaries without promising dates.

## Validation

- **Linux X11:** [run 29194456173](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29194456173) passed all **108** declared outcomes: **71 delivered, 37 exact refusals, 0 failures, 0 skips**.
- **Linux Sway native and capture:** [run 29195551765](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29195551765) passed native GTK **31/31** and capture/scope **5/5**, with playable per-cell video.
- **Linux Sway shared:** [run 29199656600](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29199656600) passed **29/36** Electron rows, up from 23/36. [Focused run 29200827296](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29200827296) then passed all **9/9 Electron PX-background** rows at the replacement source. The same 9 Tauri rows remained environment-limited by the hosted DRM/EGL setup.
- **Nested compositor:** [run 29197643541](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29197643541) passed native GTK **31/31**; [run 29197887387](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29197887387) passed capture/scope **5/5** with exact `LinuxCuaCompositorInject` metadata. Full shared run [29199596935](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29199596935) passed **26/36** Electron rows before focused repairs. [Run 29200462634](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29200462634) then passed **7/9** occluded PX-background rows. Dedicated scroll run [29200854535](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29200854535) remained red, so the environment stays experimental.
- **GNOME:** a representative GNOME 46 session passed **31** native GTK rows, **3** capture contracts, and **2** desktop-scope contracts.
- **KDE:** Plasma 6 reached session startup, GTK AT-SPI discovery, generic discovery, and portal-interface preflight. No KDE behavioral matrix is accepted.
- **Packaging and unit gates:** [Nix source run 29200852035](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29200852035) passed at `a78f525a`. Linux unit, distribution, docs, script, Windows compile, and the local 35-test testkit suite are green.
- **Windows:** [run 29166454913](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29166454913) passed all **113** typed rows: **92 delivered, 21 exact refusals, 0 failures, 0 skips**.
- **macOS:** the complete local matrix passed all **130** declared rows: **124 delivered, 6 exact refusals, 0 failures, 0 skips**.

## Remaining explicit gaps

- Standard Wayland cannot route arbitrary raw focus-bound pointer or keyboard input to an occluded, unfocused surface. Unsupported paths return exact structured refusals.
- Sway Electron still lacks foreground AX right click, foreground AX double click, and foreground AX/PX hotkey delivery.
- Hosted Sway cannot expose a representative Tauri/WebKitGTK renderer accessibility tree without DRM/EGL. The native frame can exist while the renderer tree is absent.
- The nested `cua-compositor` remains experimental. Renderer left/double click, one AX right-click timeout, and renderer scroll are not stable across focused runs. Unicode text and a canonical parallel-drag row remain unproven.
- KDE lacks a target-addressable KWin activation adapter and an accepted behavioral matrix.
- GNOME and KDE portal-backed MP4 parity, representative shared renderer runs, and real-Xorg MPX/uinput evidence remain open.
- SwiftUI transient-panel AX enumeration, Windows elevated-integrity refusal coverage, and several native control combinations remain unproven.

title: fix(cua-driver): target page JavaScript exactly
body:
## Summary

- allow `page.execute_javascript` to accept explicit `cdp_port` and `target_url_contains`
- require an explicit target hint to match exactly one CDP page
- reject invalid CDP ports instead of truncating them

## Why

Multi-window Electron processes expose multiple page targets on one CDP port. `execute_javascript` previously discarded the caller's resolved page identity and selected the first page target. An explicit URL hint also fell back to the first page when no target matched, so a successful RPC could execute against the wrong renderer.

The lower-level CDP session code already supported selecting a target by URL. This change threads that identity through the `page` tool and makes explicit hints fail closed when absent or ambiguous.

## Validation on latest upstream main

Rebased without conflict onto `trycua/cua@8c921b2b3bf13494724ead4f0a814d80c56a7e8b`.

```text
cargo test -p cua-driver-core page::tests
  3 passed

cargo test -p platform-macos browser::cdp_client::tests
  6 passed

cargo test -p cua-driver-core cdp::tests
  2 passed

cargo check -p cua-driver --release
  passed

cargo check -p platform-windows --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu
  passed

cargo check -p platform-linux  # Debian bookworm / Rust 1.92
  passed
```

The targeted-page commit is `68a42c06bf3fdfa429d65e9c011efa13c2414548`; review feedback is addressed by `5c2b402d`, which reuses the existing CDP session cache, and `0e9a8294`, which prevents replay after a script has been sent. `35fa5658` completes explicit targeted routing on Windows and Linux. `git range-diff` reports it equivalent to the originally tested patch commit `adef3e87405986cc82df52ae59aef4c32e08a082`.

## Real multi-window downstream validation

Maka uses cua-driver as the sole page executor. Its real-machine harness runs two independent Electron `BrowserWindow` pages on one CDP port and passes the exact port + unique URL hint through cua-driver for pointer actions, element inspection, `Input.insertText`, and post-action readback.

Final batch `semantic-targeting-v5`:

- 10/10 complete runs passed
- 39/39 checks passed in every run
- two-window click/type routing and text isolation passed in every run
- zero fallback, wrong-target, no-op, or duplicate-effect cases
- frontmost application and real pointer remained unchanged

Per-action results:

| Action | Pass | Route | p50 / p90 / max |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| left click | 10/10 | targeted `page.execute_javascript` | 84 / 87 / 102 ms |
| checkbox click | 10/10 | targeted `page.execute_javascript` | 70 / 77 / 77 ms |
| range drag | 10/10 | targeted `page.execute_javascript` | 96 / 102 / 127 ms |
| right click | 10/10 | targeted `page.execute_javascript` | 74 / 80 / 85 ms |
| double click | 10/10 | targeted `page.execute_javascript` | 74 / 78 / 98 ms |

The downstream repo also passed its full typecheck, build, tests, bundle provenance gate, and final 39/39 real-machine E2E after integrating the patched driver.

## Compatibility

- Repeated targeted evaluations reuse the existing per-port CDP session cache, avoiding repeated Chrome remote-debugging confirmation prompts.
- Retry is limited to retarget failures before `Runtime.evaluate`; a sent script is never replayed after timeout or disconnect.
- Windows and Linux consume explicit `cdp_port` and unique URL hints through the shared CDP helper; calls without explicit targeting retain the existing backend behavior.
- Backends that do not implement targeted execution fail closed only when the caller supplies an explicit target.
- `insert_text` and `type_keystrokes` now share the checked CDP port parser, eliminating the previous `u16` truncation behavior.

title: Lume logs successful VM stops as CancellationError and rewrites config locks
body:
## Problem

A normal requested stop of a blocking `lume run` process is reported as an error by the run process:

```text
ERROR: Failed in VM.run error=The operation couldn’t be completed. (Swift.CancellationError error 1.)
```

`lume stop` succeeds, but then performs aggressive lock cleanup that removes and restores `config.json`. The blocking `lume run` process exits with status 1.

This appeared repeatedly during the Lume 0.3.13 release E2E in both unattended setup and ordinary run/stop checks.

## Expected behavior

- An intentional stop should be logged as a normal lifecycle event, not an error.
- The corresponding blocking `lume run` process should exit successfully when the VM was intentionally stopped.
- Aggressive config backup/restore should run only when ordinary lock release actually fails.

## Why it matters

The current output looks like VM or config corruption even when the requested operation succeeded, and exit status 1 complicates automation around `lume run`.

## Reproduction

```bash
lume run --no-display macos-tahoe
# In another shell:
lume stop macos-tahoe
```

Observed with Lume 0.3.13 on macOS Tahoe host and guest.

title: cua-driver: coordinate clicks fail on scaled/HiDPI ultrawide display (Chrome web content), element-index clicks work fine
body:
# cua-driver Bug Report: Coordinate clicks fail on HiDPI/scaled ultrawide display (Chrome web content)

## Environment
- **cua-driver version:** 0.7.1
- **OS:** macOS 26.5.1 (Build 25F80), arm64 (Apple M4 Max)
- **Display:** Ultrawide via SwitchResX4 — physical resolution 7680x2160, scaled "UI Looks like" 3840x1080 @ 120Hz
- **Target app:** Google Chrome (150.0.7871.102)
- **Hermes Agent build:** current session, 2026-07-11

## Summary
`computer_use(action='click', coordinate=[x,y])` reports success ("✅ Posted click to pid NNNN (background CGEvent; not driver-verified — confirm via screenshot)") but the click does **not** land on Chrome web page content. No navigation, no element focus, no visual state change occurs. This reproduces consistently across:
- Native Chrome omnibox/address bar (partial — some interactions work, most don't)
- Web page links and buttons (fully broken — 100% reproduction rate)
- Google search results page
- Amazon.com pages
- The Claude OS dashboard page (localhost:8081)

## What DOES work
- `action='key'` with keyboard shortcuts (cmd+t, cmd+l, cmd+2, cmd+w, etc.) — reaches Chrome reliably, confirmed via visible tab switches
- `action='click'` when using **element index** (`element=N` from a same-turn `capture(mode='som')` call) — uses AXPress instead of a raw CGEvent, and this reliably navigates/activates
- `action='type'` — text is inserted (driver reports "Inserted N char(s) into AXTextField"), but this appears to use AX text-insertion APIs, not synthetic keystrokes, so a trailing `\n` inserts a literal newline character instead of submitting the field (Enter must be sent separately as `action='key', keys='return'`, and even that is unreliable when text was inserted via `type` rather than typed via real key events)

## What DOESN'T work
- `action='click'` with raw `coordinate=[x,y]` on any web page content area — click is "posted" (background CGEvent) but never registered by the page/renderer
- `action='key', keys='return'` submitting the omnibox after `action='type'` into it — inconsistent, frequently no-ops even when the address bar visibly contains the correct URL

## Suspected root cause
The screenshot/AX-tree coordinate space does not match the real click-injection coordinate space under this scaled-resolution ultrawide setup (7680x2160 physical, 3840x1080 logical via SwitchResX). CGEvent-based synthetic clicks are likely being posted at coordinates that don't correspond to where Chrome's renderer expects them, while AXPress-based clicks (using the accessibility API's semantic element, not raw pixels) bypass the coordinate math entirely and work correctly.

## Reproduction steps
1. Set up a Mac with SwitchResX-scaled resolution (any ratio where "UI Looks like" != actual panel resolution)
2. Open Chrome, navigate to any page with links
3. Call `computer_use(action='capture', mode='som', app='Google Chrome')` to get a screenshot + element list
4. Call `computer_use(action='click', app='Google Chrome', coordinate=[x,y])` targeting a visible link's on-screen position (from the screenshot)
5. Observe: driver reports success, but no navigation/state change occurs
6. Contrast: call `computer_use(action='click', app='Google Chrome', element=N)` for the same link using its element index from the same capture — this works

## Workaround in use
Always click by `element=N` (from a fresh, same-turn `capture(mode='som')`) rather than by `coordinate=[x,y]` when driving Chrome on this machine. Element tokens go stale quickly (single-use in practice), so this requires a capture → click → capture cycle per interaction, which is much slower than coordinate clicking would be if it worked.

## Suggested fix directions
1. Verify CGEvent coordinate transform accounts for the actual scale factor when a non-native resolution is set via SwitchResX or similar tools (not just Retina 2x, but arbitrary custom scale factors)
2. Consider auto-detecting coordinate-space mismatches (e.g., a "verify" pass — post the click, then check if the AX tree changed as expected — and warn/fall back to AXPress if not)
3. Make `action='type'` optionally use real keyboard-event injection (CGEventKeyboardSetUnicodeString or per-character key events) as an option, so trailing `\n` / Enter behaves like a genuine keystroke and reliably submits forms/omniboxes

title: cua-driver: for web pages, escalate to the page tool (JS) instead of foreground when a background action isn't possible
body:
## Summary
For web-rendered targets (browsers, Electron), when a background input action can't be delivered — e.g. a background `type_text`/`click` gets dropped by the renderer — the driver currently escalates via `escalation.recommended: "foreground"`. Foregrounding steals the user's focus, which breaks the core no-foreground contract the driver exists to protect.

## Proposal
For web pages specifically, the escalation should be to use the **`page` tool with JavaScript** (`execute_javascript` / `insert_text` / `type_keystrokes`) to perform the action against the DOM directly. That keeps the action fully backgrounded — no focus steal.

## Motivation / real example
Creating an Azure resource group in Chrome via cua-driver: the resource-group-name `<input>` dropped a background `type_text` (Chrome web content) and `escalation.recommended` was `foreground`. Foreground delivery worked but briefly stole focus. A `page`/JS escalation would have kept it backgrounded.

Today the `page` escalation (`escalation.recommended == "page"`) only fires for racy contenteditable rich-text editors. This asks to extend "prefer page/JS over foreground" to web-page actions generally, whenever the background rung fails.

title: docs(cua-driver): converge validation guidance and cleanup (conv2 7/7)
body:
## Summary

Final replacement PR from the #2161 second-wave convergence landing.

- documents the two-layer Rust test model: deterministic unit/protocol tests and real-application Harness E2E
- publishes current Windows, macOS, Linux X11, Sway, GNOME, KDE, and nested-compositor support boundaries using the Diataxis split between explanation, reference, and contributor guidance
- records the accepted exact-source baselines: Windows 114/114, macOS 133/133, Linux X11 108/108, and Linux Sway 108/108
- documents AX/PX targeting, foreground/background delivery, exact refusals, cross-cutting desktop oracles, typed row evidence, and per-cell MP4/trajectory ownership
- wires Windows, logged-in macOS, Linux X11, and Linux Sway validation into the cua-driver release reminder
- removes obsolete Python/shell/GIF fixture suites and historical plans after their useful contracts were mapped to typed Rust owners
- refreshes generated Lume references from current 0.3.15 source after the post-rebase generator gate found the 0.3.14 pages stale

This PR preserves the existing user-authored documentation edits that accumulated on the convergence branch; it does not quarantine or discard them. It is rebased onto merged #2184 and contains only the final docs/release-wiring/cleanup slice plus the explicit Lume generator adaptation.

## Important contracts documented

- A successful tool response does not prove delivery; fixture or desktop state must change.
- Background rows attach focus, z-order, cursor, and leaked-input oracles where applicable.
- Unsupported routes pass only when the exact declared structured refusal and side-effect contract are observed.
- Canonical contributors run one selector-free `all` command per OS; shared/native/capture fan-out is internal CI plumbing.
- Calculator and TextEdit are supporting typed checks in the canonical logged-in macOS lane. LibreOffice remains optional.

title: Add global agent guidance to prefer cua-driver for GUI and browser automation
body:
## Problem

Agents that have multiple browser/computer-use paths available can select a generic browser controller or shell workaround even when `cua-driver` is installed. This loses `cua-driver`'s background-operation, no-focus-steal, accessibility-first, and action-verification guarantees.

A local workaround was added to the user's global Codex guidance at:

```
/Users/administrator/.codex/AGENTS.md
```

The preference should be available as a supported, reusable configuration rather than a one-machine edit.

## Proposed guidance

Add or install global agent guidance equivalent to:

```md
## Computer and Browser Use

- Prefer the `cua-driver` skill and `cua-driver` CLI for computer-use and browser-use tasks that require operating a graphical interface.
- Follow the skill's snapshot-before-action and snapshot-after-action verification loop for every GUI action.
- Prefer accessibility element actions first and use pixel actions only when the accessibility path is unavailable or demonstrably ineffective.
- Continue to prefer purpose-built APIs or CLIs for semantic, non-GUI operations when they fully cover the requested task.
```

This should apply to both native applications and browser GUIs while preserving purpose-built APIs/CLIs as the preferred path for operations that do not need UI control.

## Possible implementation

- Have `cua-driver skills install` optionally install or merge this guidance into the agent's global instructions.
- Alternatively, ship a documented global `AGENTS.md` snippet/template for Codex, Claude Code, OpenClaw, and other supported clients.
- Make the merge idempotent and avoid overwriting unrelated user guidance.
- Keep explicit user-selected tools and higher-priority host instructions authoritative.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Installing/configuring `cua-driver` provides a supported way to make it the default GUI/browser automation path globally.
- [ ] Guidance covers native apps and browser GUIs.
- [ ] Guidance requires a fresh snapshot before each action and verification snapshot afterward.
- [ ] Guidance prefers accessibility actions before pixel dispatch.
- [ ] Semantic non-GUI work still prefers purpose-built APIs/CLIs.
- [ ] Re-running installation does not duplicate or replace unrelated global instructions.
- [ ] Documentation explains where the guidance is installed and how to opt out or remove it.

## Motivation

This came up during a GCP billing-console workflow: the agent initially selected a generic browser path, while the desired behavior was to use `cua-driver` for the authenticated browser UI and retain CLI/API tools only for operations they fully support.

title: [cua-driver][page] Make authenticated default-profile Chrome a first-class, user-approved flow
body:
## Problem

Automating a repetitive workflow in an authenticated Chrome SPA exposed a gap between accessibility-only browser control and DOM/JavaScript control in `cua-driver 0.7.1` on macOS.

The existing, logged-in Chrome instance used its default profile. In that configuration:

- `page.get_text` and `page.query_dom` could fall back to the accessibility tree.
- `page.execute_javascript` reported that no CDP port was available.
- Launching Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port` is not viable for its default data directory.
- Chrome's `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` toggle can expose the real profile, but it requires explicit user approval and the caller must know and pass the port.
- Without DOM execution or a current-tab navigation primitive, the agent had to edit the omnibox, press Return, wait for the SPA, and perform several AX actions for every item.
- AX `set_value` changed the visible value of a React autocomplete but did not dispatch the input events needed to populate results; real keystrokes worked.
- During navigation, a few snapshots returned a successful payload without an `elements` array, forcing callers to defensively normalize transient states.

This is not a request to bypass Chrome's security confirmation. The user should remain responsible for granting remote-debugging access.

## Proposed direction

1. Add a `page.capabilities` or `page.prepare` action for an existing browser window. It should report the available read, DOM, JavaScript, navigation, and input backends and return a structured `user_action_required` result when Chrome approval is needed.
2. After approval, discover the browser-level CDP listener owned by the target PID even when the classic `/json` discovery endpoint is unavailable. Reuse the existing `CdpSessionCache` so one approved connection supports repeated tab attachments without repeated prompts.
3. Add `page.navigate` for navigating an existing authenticated tab in place, with `target_url_contains` or an explicit target identifier. On macOS, an Apple Events URL setter could be a useful fallback when CDP is unavailable.
4. Add a DOM-aware `page.fill` action, or an option that dispatches the expected `input` and `change` events for SPA controls. Keep `type_keystrokes` as the durable fallback.
5. Make transient snapshots return `elements: []` plus a structured loading/error state, rather than omitting `elements`.

## Security constraints

- Never enable or approve remote debugging automatically.
- Keep the listener loopback-only and bind the cached session to the requested browser process.
- Require an unambiguous target match before navigation or JavaScript execution.
- Do not log cookies, storage, page contents, tokens, or session identifiers.

## Acceptance criteria

- An agent can start from an already-running, logged-in default-profile Chrome window without relaunching into a separate profile.
- The tool clearly explains the one user approval required and resumes after it is granted.
- `execute_javascript`, `navigate`, and DOM-aware filling reuse one cached connection across repeated operations.
- A browser-level WebSocket endpoint works when `/json` returns no usable page discovery.
- Tests cover same-tab navigation, React-style input events, ambiguous target selection, user-denied approval, and transient navigation snapshots.

title: test(cua-driver): harden background E2E oracles
body:
## Summary

This PR strengthens the Rust desktop E2E contract and fixes the product defects that the new oracles exposed.

### Driver fixes

- Windows UIA actions now scroll fully clipped controls into view before acting and keep the UIA off-screen state in sync.
- Windows background `type_text` through `ValuePattern` now appends to the control's existing value instead of replacing it.
- macOS keyboard delivery clears inherited modifier flags before posting text and key events, preventing stale modifiers from changing later input.

### E2E signal

- Background delivery requires the target to be fully covered, with stable focus, z-order, foreground input, and cursor position where the platform exposes it.
- The foreground sentinel records focus, visibility, keyboard, pointer, wheel, and heartbeat events.
- Preflight deliberately leaks input and raises the target to prove that the guards can detect both failures before product rows run.
- Shared Electron, Tauri, and WKWebView catalogs now contain 40 typed cells per harness, including AX/PX, foreground/background, exact type-then-Return workflows, editor save, and scroll state.
- Fixture state checks use exact journaled outcomes instead of trusting a successful driver response.
- Canonical runs reject zero-cell filters, unexpected skips, under-sized catalogs, ambiguous window identity, and orphaned videos.
- Sway observation resolves the intended container, handles nested fullscreen ancestors, and refuses ambiguous PID-only matches.
- Preflight owns fixture child cleanup even when activation fails.
- Contributor docs describe the matrix, evidence contract, reports, and canonical commands.

## Why

A successful driver response does not prove that the target application received an action. Background delivery also needs evidence that the target was covered and that the user's foreground remained unchanged. These changes make those claims explicit and machine-checked, then fix the driver behavior that failed the stronger checks.

## Validation

Exact final head: `64e824490b6a796102a46fcece518a9d6c32c145`

- [Windows complete matrix](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29257963004): native WPF/WinUI3/WebView2, capture/desktop scope, shared Electron/Tauri, and combined summary all passed.
- [Wayland shared matrix](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29257961614): Sway shared matrix and typed summary passed.
- [Linux X11 complete matrix](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29254936043): capture 5/5, native 31/31, and shared 80/80 passed at `268a6ab1`. Later commits only change preflight identity and cleanup logic for Windows/Sway.
- macOS local canonical matrix: 138 deliveries and 6 expected refusals passed. One AppKit background AX click was interrupted by physical cursor movement; the strict cursor guard caught it. The same row then passed in isolation on final head with fixture-state, focus, z-order, cursor, and no-leaked-input evidence. Final-head daemon, AX, screenshot, canary, and video preflight also passed.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-testkit --lib`: 40 passed.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib`: 121 passed.
- Changed Rust files pass `rustfmt --check`; the branch passes `git diff --check`.

## Scope

This PR changes the Rust driver, repo-owned fixtures, E2E testkit, canonical runners, and contributor documentation. It does not import an external Python harness or add model-driven tests.

## Known limitations

- Standard Wayland does not expose the physical pointer position, so Wayland rows cannot claim the cursor-preservation oracle.
- Installed LibreOffice coverage remains an optional external-app suite outside the canonical run-all command.
- Expected background refusals remain visible as typed matrix outcomes; they are capability limits, not claimed deliveries.

title: cua-driver/Linux: expose canonical app identity in list_windows
body:
## Problem

On Linux, `list_windows` and `list_apps` can describe the same running application with different identities:

- X11 `list_windows.app_name` comes from `WM_CLASS`.
- Native Wayland uses the compositor `app_id` or an AT-SPI application name.
- `list_apps` resolves `/proc` processes against XDG desktop entries and can return a canonical display name and desktop-file ID.

For example, a FreeCAD window may have `app_name="Qt6Application"`, while the positive-PID `list_apps` record reports `name="FreeCAD"` and `bundle_id="org.freecad.FreeCAD"`. Consumers that accept an app name or bundle ID must call both tools and join the records by PID before they can target the window.

This surfaced while reviewing [NousResearch/hermes-agent#63725](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/63725). The adapter implements the PID join itself as a compatibility fallback.

## Current implementation

- X11 derives `app_name` from `WM_CLASS`: [`platform-linux/src/x11/mod.rs`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3cadb5f82e7d2ed071a2082764276ec872a52135/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/x11/mod.rs#L43-L81)
- Linux `list_apps` separately resolves process executables to XDG identities: [`platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3cadb5f82e7d2ed071a2082764276ec872a52135/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs#L192-L312)
- `list_windows` serializes only the platform-derived `app_name`: [`platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3cadb5f82e7d2ed071a2082764276ec872a52135/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs#L429-L451)

## Proposed contract

Make each positive-PID Linux window record carry enough additive app identity metadata for a caller to match a display name, stable XDG desktop-file ID, or platform-native identifier without reconstructing the relationship itself.

Possible fields:

- `app_id` or `bundle_id`: stable XDG desktop-file/compositor identifier when known
- `app_aliases`: canonical display name, process name, raw `WM_CLASS`, and Wayland `app_id`
- `platform_metadata.wm_class`: raw X11 instance/class values for diagnostics

Keep the existing `app_name` behavior backward compatible unless we make an intentional versioned contract change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Extract the existing process-to-XDG resolver so `list_apps` and `list_windows` share it.
- [ ] Enrich positive-PID X11 window records with the matching XDG identity when unambiguous.
- [ ] Preserve Wayland `app_id` and add canonical aliases when a reliable PID/XDG match exists.
- [ ] Never join installed-only `pid=0` records to windows.
- [ ] Preserve raw `WM_CLASS`/compositor identity for debugging and backward compatibility.
- [ ] Add a unit fixture for `WM_CLASS=Qt6Application`, PID `7675`, and XDG identity `FreeCAD/org.freecad.FreeCAD`.
- [ ] Add a real Linux MCP integration row asserting that `list_apps` and `list_windows` expose a common usable identity for the same positive PID.
- [ ] Cover an X11 native harness and a Wayland-capable harness; keep FreeCAD/LibreOffice as optional real-app coverage.
- [ ] Document behavior when Wayland does not expose a PID or desktop-entry matching is ambiguous.

## Notes

Localized display names should be aliases rather than replacements for stable identifiers. Wrapper processes and applications whose top-level window belongs to a child PID also need explicit treatment.

title: cua-driver: define and test list_windows z_index semantics
body:
## Problem

`list_windows.z_index` is easy for integrations to misinterpret:

- The cross-platform convention is **higher means closer to the front**.
- X11 receives `_NET_CLIENT_LIST_STACKING` in bottom-to-top order and assigns increasing indices.
- macOS and Windows normalize their native front-to-back enumeration to the same higher-is-frontmost convention.
- Native Wayland providers may return `z_index: null` because the compositor does not expose stacking order.

The convention is present in some implementation comments and platform-specific descriptions, but it is not stated consistently in the shared tool contract. Consumers can therefore sort in the wrong direction or fail when Wayland returns `null`. This surfaced while reviewing [NousResearch/hermes-agent#63725](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/63725), which currently sorts ascending and treats the first record as frontmost.

## Current implementation

- macOS documents higher as frontmost and reverses CGWindowList order: [`platform-macos/src/tools/list_windows.rs`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3cadb5f82e7d2ed071a2082764276ec872a52135/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/list_windows.rs#L12-L18), [`platform-macos/src/windows.rs`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3cadb5f82e7d2ed071a2082764276ec872a52135/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/windows.rs#L165-L180)
- Windows reverses `EnumWindows` order to the same convention: [`platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3cadb5f82e7d2ed071a2082764276ec872a52135/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs#L704-L727)
- X11 assigns increasing indices to `_NET_CLIENT_LIST_STACKING`: [`platform-linux/src/x11/mod.rs`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3cadb5f82e7d2ed071a2082764276ec872a52135/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/x11/mod.rs#L39-L81)
- Native Wayland records may use `None`: [`platform-linux/src/wayland/mod.rs`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3cadb5f82e7d2ed071a2082764276ec872a52135/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/mod.rs#L620-L636)

## Proposed contract

Define `z_index` once in the shared `list_windows` schema and documentation:

- integer: higher values are closer to the front
- `null`: stacking order is unavailable and callers must not infer one

Do not invent `0` for providers that cannot observe stacking order. If a provider can identify only the active window, consider an additive `is_frontmost` field rather than fabricating a complete order.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add the same `z_index` description and nullability to every platform's `list_windows` schema.
- [ ] Document the convention in the CUA Driver reference and skill.
- [ ] Add contract tests proving that macOS, Windows, and X11 normalize to higher-is-frontmost.
- [ ] Add a Wayland contract test proving that unavailable order is serialized as `null` and remains consumable.
- [ ] Add a cross-platform consumer example that selects `max(z_index)` only from non-null values and uses an explicit fallback otherwise.
- [ ] Audit `launch_app.windows` and other window-record surfaces for the same semantics.

title: cua-driver: reject ambiguous PID-only action targets instead of choosing a window
body:
## Problem

Window-scoped actions may receive a `pid` without a `window_id`. When that process owns more than one top-level window, the resolver can select the first matching window. That makes a syntactically valid call capable of typing, pressing a key, clicking, or scrolling in the wrong document or dialog.

Callers should preserve and pass `(pid, window_id)`, but the driver should also fail closed when PID-only targeting is ambiguous.

This surfaced during an integration review where `type_text`, `press_key`, and `hotkey` retained only the PID while capture and pointer actions retained the exact window identity.

## Proposed contract

- A `pid` with exactly one eligible top-level window remains valid for backward compatibility.
- A `pid` with no eligible windows returns the existing not-found result.
- A `pid` with more than one eligible window and no `window_id` returns a structured `ambiguous_window_target` refusal before any input is sent.
- An explicit `(pid, window_id)` always resolves exactly or fails.
- The refusal includes enough candidate metadata for the caller to recover by listing windows and selecting one.

## Scope

Audit every window-scoped action resolver, including:

- `type_text`, `press_key`, and `hotkey`
- click, right click, double click, scroll, and drag variants
- capture and focus helpers that accept PID-only targeting

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add a shared resolver outcome for zero, one, and multiple eligible windows.
- [ ] Return a structured ambiguity refusal without changing focus, z-order, cursor, or application state.
- [ ] Add same-PID/two-window contract tests on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- [ ] Add a harness E2E row proving an explicit `window_id` reaches the intended sibling window.
- [ ] Document when PID-only targeting is accepted and when callers must provide `window_id`.

title: cua-driver/Windows: background Chrome click can miss or blur the foreground sentinel
body:
## Problem

On a hosted Windows Server 2025 interactive desktop, a real Chrome target does not produce a deterministic safe result for background coordinate clicks on current `main` (`3cadb5f82e7d2ed071a2082764276ec872a52135`).

Observed outcomes across repeated runs include:

- a background scene click reaching the target once;
- point and scene clicks missing the target;
- the foreground sentinel recording a blur during the action.

The last outcome is the most serious: a background request must either deliver without disturbing the foreground desktop or return a structured refusal before acting.

Our canonical Windows matrix proves the stricter target-state, focus, z-order, cursor, and leaked-input oracles on repo-built Electron, Tauri, WPF, WinUI 3, and WebView2 fixtures. It does not currently prove the same route against standalone Chrome, so the surface-specific regression can escape that matrix.

## Reproduction shape

1. Launch Chrome with a deterministic page that journals button state.
2. Fully occlude Chrome with a foreground sentinel that records focus, keyboard, pointer, and wheel events.
3. Call `click` with Chrome's `pid`, `window_id`, window-local `x/y`, and `delivery_mode:"background"`.
4. Assert target state and all foreground side-effect oracles.
5. Repeat with fresh processes and both point- and scene-addressed routes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The same action deterministically delivers under full occlusion or returns one exact structured refusal.
- [ ] A background result never blurs or lowers the foreground sentinel.
- [ ] Run at least three fresh-process seeds on `windows-latest` and an interactive Windows VM.
- [ ] Add an optional real-Chrome compatibility row that uses the same typed report and independent oracles as the canonical Rust catalog.
- [ ] Keep the repo-built shared harness as the canonical contract; use the Chrome row to detect materially different renderer/window-class behavior.
- [ ] Retain per-cell video, target journal, focus journal, and driver trajectory for failures.

## Related

- #2176 tracks page/JS escalation when native background delivery is unavailable on web surfaces.
- #2193 introduced the current strict background E2E oracles and canonical Windows matrix.

title: cua-driver/macOS: foreground Chrome drag starts but does not move or drop
body:
## Problem

Against a real Chrome page on current `main` (`3cadb5f82e7d2ed071a2082764276ec872a52135`), macOS foreground drag starts but does not produce motion/drop state. Both window-local and scene-addressed attempts record `drag_started=yes` while the drop zone remains `none`.

The repo-built shared harness proves drag behavior on representative renderer hosts, but standalone Chrome remains a materially different surface and currently has no retained compatibility row.

## Reproduction shape

1. Launch Chrome with a page that journals pointer down, movement, and drop-zone state.
2. Bring the target to the foreground.
3. Call foreground drag using window-local start/end coordinates.
4. Repeat through scene addressing.
5. Assert application-owned movement and drop state rather than the driver return value.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Determine whether the failure is event construction, movement interpolation, coordinate conversion, timing, or Chrome-specific acceptance.
- [ ] Foreground drag produces both motion and the expected drop state for window and scene routes, or returns an honest target-specific refusal before pointer down.
- [ ] Add an optional real-Chrome compatibility row using the canonical typed report and per-cell video.
- [ ] Verify the fix in a logged-in macOS session with Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions.
- [ ] Confirm AppKit, SwiftUI, Electron, Tauri, and WKWebView drag rows do not regress.

title: cua-driver 0.7.1 Linux/X11: cua-overlay-x11 thread burns ~50% CPU at idle (same as #1808, Linux not fixed by #1865/#1933)
body:
### Bug: cua-driver 0.7.1 Linux/X11 — cua-overlay-x11 thread burns ~50% CPU at idle

**Related:** #1808 (closed — same class of bug, fixed in #1865 for macOS and #1933 for Windows in v0.5.19)
**Platform:** Linux X11 (Ubuntu 25.10, kernel 6.17.0-40-generic)
**Binary:** cua-driver 0.7.1 (`/home/philip/.local/bin/cua-driver` symlink to `~/.cua-driver/packages/releases/0.7.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/cua-driver`)
**Launched as:** Hermes MCP server (`command: /home/philip/.local/bin/cua-driver`, `args: ['mcp']`)

### Symptoms

When cua-driver is started as a long-running MCP server (stdio mode), it pegs a single CPU core at ~45-50% continuously, even when no MCP client is sending requests. The burn starts at MCP startup and continues for the full lifetime of the process.

### Root cause (best read)

A single TID, comm `cua-overlay-x11`, is responsible. It runs in a tight userspace loop on `hrtimer_nanosleep` with no syscalls in between — `cat /proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/wchan` returns `-` (i.e. running in userspace, not blocked on a syscall or futex). The thread does not back off when the agent cursor is disabled via the `set_agent_cursor_enabled(false)` MCP tool — the loop is independent of the on/off state.

### Workaround (currently used)

Pass `--no-overlay` to the daemon. Confirmed by reading the upstream issue thread that this fully eliminates the burn on macOS/Windows. Linux is the missing platform.

This is identical in shape to the macOS render loop fixed in #1865 (introduced `needs_frame_tick()` event-driven pattern, switched from unconditional 60Hz/125Hz tick to ACTIVE→IDLE cadence) and the Windows overlay fix in #1933. The Linux overlay should apply the same `needs_frame_tick()` gating in the X11 overlay render loop.

### Verification available

I can attach:
- `ps -L -p <pid> -o tid,pcpu,stat,wchan,comm` output showing the hot thread
- `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/stack` output (empty due to perf_event_paranoid=4 on this system)
- The `cu-driver --no-overlay mcp` workaround in production at my MCP config

### Suggested fix

Port the event-driven render pattern from #1865/#1933 to `crates/platform-linux/src/overlay.rs` (or whatever the Linux overlay module is named). The `needs_frame_tick()` gate should be true only when:
- a cursor has an in-flight glide path
- a spring-settle animation is active
- a click pulse is mid-fade
- an idle-fade hasn't completed

Otherwise the thread should park on a `Condvar` or `eventfd` and wake on `wake_overlay()` calls from `send_command` / `remove_cursor` / session-end events.

### Environment

```
$ uname -a
Linux philip-NucBox-EVO-X1 6.17.0-40-generic #40-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC ...
$ /home/philip/.local/bin/cua-driver --version
cua-driver 0.7.1
$ echo $XDG_SESSION_TYPE
x11
```

Happy to test a PR.

title: docs: restore OpenClaw guide and remove obsolete routing

## What changed

- add a task-focused guide for running OpenClaw in a local Lume macOS VM

title: Standardize foreground delivery as action-scoped activation with guaranteed restoration
body:
## Problem

The documented cross-platform contract for `delivery_mode:"foreground"` is:

1. capture the current foreground window,
2. activate the target,
3. perform one complete action,
4. restore the previous foreground,
5. return.

`bring_to_front` is the separate persistent-activation operation.

An audit of current `main` at `3cadb5f82e7d2ed071a2082764276ec872a52135` found that the implementation does not consistently uphold that contract.

## Current behavior

### Windows

- Keyboard and text foreground paths perform a real foreground swap and restore synchronously after short settling delays.
- Normal pixel `click` uses the active SendInput path, but restoration is delegated to an asynchronous polling task, so the tool may return before focus is restored.
- Indexed clicks, `double_click`, and `right_click` use the non-activating SendInput helper in several foreground branches. That helper temporarily raises the target with `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE`; it does not guarantee that the target becomes the OS foreground window.
- Foreground `drag` similarly uses a non-activating/topmost pointer path.
- Foreground `scroll` moves the real cursor over the target and sends a wheel event without activating the target.
- Pointer restoration reuses `restore_foreground_polling_best_effort`, a launch-oriented asynchronous helper with input-idle waiting and a polling window.

The result is that `foreground` can mean either real activation or temporary z-order/cursor routing depending on the action.

### macOS

Most actions follow front -> act -> restore correctly, but activation lasts for the complete action rather than a fixed instant:

- native menu key paths can complete in under 1 ms,
- click and scroll paths can remain fronted for tens to roughly 150 ms,
- text entry includes a 200 ms focus settle plus typing time,
- drag remains foreground for the full gesture plus its post-action settle.

If the private fronting SPI is unavailable, some paths run the action without activation and report the fallback instead of failing the foreground request.

### Linux X11

X11 generally follows activate -> settle -> act -> EWMH restore. Activation includes an 80 ms pre-action settle and lasts for the whole action. Restoration remains best-effort and is not asserted by the E2E suite.

### Linux Wayland

Native Wayland foreground routes activate the target and inject input, but do not capture or restore the previously active toplevel. This affects click, scroll, drag, type_text, press_key, and hotkey. Where compositor state is insufficient to restore safely, the limitation is not reflected in the common API contract.

## Test gap

Canonical foreground E2E cases currently declare only the `FixtureState` oracle. They prove that the action landed, but do not prove:

- that the requested target actually became foreground,
- that activation lasted only for the action,
- that the previous foreground was restored before the tool returned.

Background rows have focus, z-order, cursor, and leaked-input oracles, but there is no corresponding foreground-lifecycle oracle.

## Proposed contract

Define `delivery_mode:"foreground"` as **action-scoped activation**:

> Activate the selected target for one complete action and restore the previously active window before returning.

Keep `bring_to_front` as persistent activation.

“Action-scoped” is preferable to “instant”: a drag or delayed typing operation must remain active for the whole gesture.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All foreground action families use a shared scoped-activation abstraction on each OS.
- [ ] The prior foreground is restored synchronously before the tool response is returned.
- [ ] Windows click, double-click, right-click, drag, scroll, type, key, and hotkey either perform real activation or return an honest structured capability error.
- [ ] Wayland restores the previous target on compositors where active-toplevel state and activation are available.
- [ ] Wayland returns a structured limitation where safe restoration cannot be implemented; it must not silently claim the common contract.
- [ ] macOS reports a structured foreground failure when activation was explicitly requested but unavailable, rather than silently degrading to background delivery.
- [ ] X11 restoration verifies both active-window and input-focus postconditions within a bounded deadline.
- [ ] Add a cross-platform foreground-lifecycle E2E oracle that proves target activation, action delivery, and restoration of the original foreground.
- [ ] Add representative foreground lifecycle rows for pointer, keyboard, scroll, and drag actions on Windows, macOS, X11, and supported Wayland compositor lanes.
- [ ] Update docs to describe foreground delivery as action-scoped and document compositor-specific limitations.

## Relevant code

- Windows delivery contract: `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/input/delivery.rs`
- Windows keyboard swap: `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/input/keyboard.rs`
- Windows pointer helpers: `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/input/mouse.rs`
- Windows async restoration: `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs`
- macOS scoped activation: `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/input/skylight.rs`
- Linux X11 scoped activation: `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/input/mod.rs`
- Linux Wayland activation: `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/mod.rs`
- E2E case/oracle definitions: `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-testkit/src/e2e.rs`

title: feat(cua-driver): add stable AX node identity tokens
body:
> **Status: tracking draft.** This PR grew to 19 files / +1274 −766, which is well outside what is reviewable as a single change in this repo (recent merged PRs sit around ~111 lines). It is being split into focused PRs; this one stays open only to track that split. Please review the individual PRs below instead.

## Split status

| Part | PR | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Full 32-bit snapshot generation (token collision fix) | #2608 | open, independent |
| `set_value` AXValue read-back with `verified` / `changed` | #2621 | open, independent |

Both are single-file, independent of each other, and independent of the token work below.

## Re-scoped after review of upstream `main`

Two items I originally listed for extraction turned out not to be upstream defects at all, and I'm not proposing them as standalone fixes:

**`token_for` returning `Option` instead of panicking.** Upstream's `token_for` is a pure formatting helper — it does not consult the registry and cannot panic. The `.expect("token requested for an unregistered snapshot element")` I was pointing at was introduced by this PR's own registry rework, not by upstream. It is an internal correctness issue of the mechanism proposed here, not a bug to fix in `main`.

**Element-action TOCTOU.** The race you identified in review —

> If another session re-snapshots the same window between validation and cache lookup, that index can refer to a different AX node

— applies to the token-resolution path this PR adds. Upstream `ax/cache.rs` has only `update(pid, window_id, nodes)`; there is no generation tracking and no `resolve_token`, so there is nothing in `main` to harden independently. This belongs with whatever token design lands, not before it.

I'd rather say this explicitly than ship two PRs that claim to fix upstream bugs which aren't there.

## Deliberately dropped from the split

Three parts of this PR should not land in their current form:

**Opaque UUID tokens.** Replacing the token body with a UUID v4 conflicts with the format goals already documented in `element_token.rs` ("8-16 char budget", "debug-grep-able without a side-table"), and at least one user in #2207 types tokens by hand on the command line. Replay resistance across daemon restarts is better served by a per-process nonce that keeps the readable shape, e.g. `s{nonce}-{generation}:{index}`.

**`allow_pixel_fallback(via_token) = !via_token`.** This couples addressing to dispatch strategy, which are orthogonal. cua-driver's architecture is AX-first with a pixel ladder; a token should make "which element" more precise, not change "how it is delivered". The requirement it encoded ("never fall back to pixels") belongs in the downstream client, which can already enforce it by rejecting `structuredContent.path != "ax"`. If a driver-side switch is still wanted it should be an explicit opt-in parameter that leaves current behaviour unchanged by default, proposed separately.

**`node_identity`.** The value stored was `element_ptr as u64` — the same pointer the cache already holds. A fresh AX walk yields a new `AXUIElementRef`, so it cannot survive a re-snapshot and does not deliver what the PR title claimed. A real stable identity needs `CFEqual` / `AXIdentifier` (both already used in `ax/tree.rs`), and that deserves its own change with its own justification.

## What remains for the token mechanism itself

The remaining pieces (opaque-capability tokens, generation binding, typed rejection codes) change a public contract, so per `rfcs/README.md` they should go through an RFC issue rather than arriving as a PR. I'll open one rather than re-pushing this branch.

## Original description

<details>
<summary>Expand</summary>

Hardens the existing cua-driver `element_token` protocol on macOS without introducing a second token abstraction: keeps the cross-platform `TokenRegistry` as the single token source, widens the generation, attaches macOS AX node identity to the snapshot entry, binds token use to PID / window / generation / index / node identity, returns typed fail-closed error codes, retains the validated AX node for `click` and `set_value`, and performs `set_value` write/read-back on that same node reporting idempotent writes as `changed:false`.

</details>

title: Add consent-aware telemetry for Cua Driver and Lume

## Summary

- Add default-on, consent-aware telemetry to Cua Driver and Lume with persistent disable controls and explicit reset and purge behavior.
- Send a content-free schema v2 envelope to PostHog EU with person profiles and GeoIP enrichment disabled.
- Record bounded CLI, MCP session, MCP tool outcome, install, release, and Lume usage events.

A normal uninstall preserves the pseudonymous installation ID and saved preference so returning installations remain measurable. Disabling telemetry stops all telemetry requests. title: Windows: D3D screenshot returns 0x0, coordinates offset by -32000 with multiple IDD virtual displays
body:
## Description

On Windows 10 with multiple Indirect Display Driver (IDD) virtual monitors present, `cua-driver` captures return zero-size screenshots (width=0, height=0) and all element coordinates are offset by -32000, making coordinate-based clicking and screenshot feedback unusable.

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 10 Pro, build 19042.630 (x86_64)
- **cua-driver**: 0.7.1 (installed via pip)
- **Python**: 3.11.15
- **Hermes Agent**: running via API server (not CLI)

## Display Adapters (wmic output)

| Adapter | Driver Version |
|---------|---------------|
| Intel(R) UHD Graphics 630 | 27.20.100.8783 (real GPU) |
| Virtual Display Device | 1.0.0.9 (Huawei IDD) |
| OrayIddDriver Device | 17.50.19.949 (Sunlogin) |

## Expected Behavior

- capture(mode='som') or capture(mode='vision') should return a screenshot with valid dimensions matching the user's actual display resolution.
- Element coordinates should be in screen-space (e.g., x=0..1919, y=0..1079).

## Actual Behavior

- All captures return width=0, height=0, empty image data.
- All element coordinates are approximately -32000 (UIAutomation constant for off-screen elements).
- AX tree itself is correctly populated (elements are findable by accessibility).
- UIA Invoke, set_value, and key operations work correctly (they don't rely on coordinates).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a Windows 10 system with at least one IDD virtual display driver (Huawei Virtual Display Device, Sunlogin/OrayIddDriver, or similar).
2. Run cua-driver mcp and connect via MCP client.
3. Call capture(mode='som') or capture(mode='vision').
4. Observe width=0, height=0 in the response and all element coordinates at -32000.

## Root Cause Analysis

The system has 3 display adapters. The D3D/WGC (Windows Graphics Capture) API in cua-driver appears to be enumerating the virtual display adapter(s) instead of the real physical display, returning zero-area capture targets. The IDD virtual monitors present themselves as full display devices to the OS but have no real screen backing them, hence 0-size captures.

UIAutomation reports elements as 'off-screen' (-32000 coordinates) because the windows are placed on the virtual desktop that spans multiple 'monitors', and the primary real monitor's coordinate space isnt being mapped correctly.

## Workaround

For now, operations that don't require pixel coordinates work:
- set_value (UIA ValuePattern) for text input into form fields
- key for keyboard shortcuts
- UIA Invoke for buttons via element index
- focus_app to activate windows

Coordinate-based operations (click by [x,y], drag, scroll) and screenshot-based workflows are broken.

## Suggested Fix

When enumerating display adapters for D3D/WGC capture, cua-driver should either:
1. Skip IDD virtual display adapters (filter by driver name or device class).
2. Or pick the adapter that actually has a non-zero resolution as the capture target.
3. Or allow the user to specify which display/adapter to capture via configuration.

Additionally, when UIAutomation returns -32000 coordinates, cua-driver could attempt to calculate the actual screen position by accounting for the virtual desktop offset.
