## Expected

The root package declares the same canonical repository as its native packages, and release reruns can repair an older tagged source manifest before packing.

## Acceptance criteria

- The checked-in TypeScript package declares canonical Git repository metadata.
- The publisher sets/verifies that metadata while packaging an existing tag so 0.11.0 can be recovered without moving the immutable tag.
- Packed root metadata is tested before publish.

title: Cua Driver SDK CD can pass before the npm package is publicly readable
body:
## Summary

The Cua Driver SDK package workflow can finish successfully even when the newly published root npm package is not yet readable by an unauthenticated consumer.

## Reproduction

Release workflow: https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/29923263392

The `Publish @trycua/cua-driver` step reported `+ @trycua/cua-driver@0.11.0`, public access, and a signed provenance statement. After the workflow completed successfully, both of these consumer checks returned HTTP 404:

```sh
npm view @trycua/cua-driver@0.11.0 version
curl -i 'https://registry.npmjs.org/@trycua%2fcua-driver'
```

The six native platform packages were publicly readable, so the failure was isolated to the newly created root package.

## Expected

The workflow should not report successful npm delivery until an unauthenticated registry request can resolve the exact root package version and a clean install/import smoke test passes.

## Suggested fix

Add a bounded post-publish poll against the unauthenticated public registry, followed by a clean temporary-project `npm install @trycua/cua-driver@$VERSION` and root import. Keep the poll tolerant of ordinary registry propagation, but fail with the exact consumer response after the timeout.

No credentials, local paths, or package contents should be logged.

title: fix(cua-driver): don't report direct capture ready before Tahoe consent
body:
## Summary

On a fresh macOS Tahoe VM, `check_permissions` reported direct capture as fully ready, but the first video recording still raised Tahoe's one-time direct-capture consent dialog.

The tested source already contains the permission-consent fix from #2407 that closed #2296, so this appears to be a remaining gap in the readiness probe rather than pre-fix behavior.

## Environment

- Cua Driver: `0.10.0`
- Source SHA: `d5a5e33d6d0b5dc4998c4985bc0704d6df2b0a1d`
- macOS: `26.5.2 (25F84)`
- Architecture: arm64
- Install: `libs/cua-driver/scripts/install-local.sh --release --autostart`
- Responsible app identity: `com.trycua.driver.local`

## Reproduction

1. Install Cua Driver in a fresh macOS VM.
2. Grant Accessibility and Screen Recording to the installed app identity.
3. Run the prompt-capable live probe:

```sh
cua-driver-local call check_permissions '{"prompt":true}'
```

It reports:

```json
{
  "accessibility": true,
  "screen_recording": true,
  "screen_recording_capturable": true,
  "direct_capture_status": "ready"
}
```

4. Start the first video recording:

```sh
cua-driver-local call start_recording '{"output_dir":"/tmp/cua-recording","record_video":true}'
```

The call reports `video_active: true`, but macOS then presents the one-time dialog:

> “CuaDriverLocal” is requesting to bypass the system private window picker and directly access your screen and audio.

5. Click **Allow** through the interactive desktop. The recording then proceeds normally. A second clean recording starts without another prompt.

## Expected behavior

If `check_permissions {"prompt":true}` returns both `screen_recording_capturable: true` and `direct_capture_status: "ready"`, an immediate `start_recording` should not raise another permission dialog.

If the direct-capture consent is still pending, the probe should either trigger and complete that consent flow or return a non-ready status such as `consent_required`.

## Actual behavior

The probe returns `ready`, while the consent dialog is deferred until the first ScreenCaptureKit recording begins.

## Impact

Automated VM certification and demo setup can conclude that capture is ready, then have the first recording obscured or blocked by a system modal. The recording response itself reports `video_active: true`, so callers have no structured indication that interactive consent is still pending.

## Suggested regression test

On a fresh Tahoe VM:

1. Complete the explicit permission-grant flow.
2. Assert that a prompt-capable `check_permissions` result of `direct_capture_status: "ready"` is followed by a prompt-free `start_recording(record_video=true)`.
3. Otherwise require the permission probe to return a pending/non-ready direct-capture status.

title: fix(cua-driver): advertise delivery mode capability

## Change

- Use the same resolver for direct MCP, daemon, and proxy/fallback `tools/list` paths.
- Advertise the token only for tools whose live schema exposes `delivery_mode`.
- Add exact-set and parity regressions covering all three platform backends and the shared browser-dialog tool.

title: fix(cua-driver): animate the macOS agent cursor for typed browser actions
body:
## Summary

On macOS, typed browser tools (`browser_type`, `browser_click`, and `browser_pointer`) update the page but do not provide visible agent-cursor feedback. On macOS Tahoe, a normal-level transparent cursor overlay can also remain behind an already-frontmost cross-process browser even after relative window ordering.

A local implementation has been verified in a fresh Tahoe VM and is ready to be turned into a focused pull request.

## Reproduction

Tested with Cua Driver 0.10.0 at source SHA `d5a5e33d6d0b5dc4998c4985bc0704d6df2b0a1d` on macOS Tahoe 26.5.2.

1. Prepare an isolated Chromium profile with driver-owned loopback remote debugging.
2. Exact-bind a native browser window to its CDP target.
3. Invoke `browser_type`, `browser_pointer`, and `browser_click`.
4. Inspect the physical pointer, agent cursor state, app focus, and captured video.

### Actual

Before the local fix, typed browser actions never invoked the agent cursor overlay. After initial cursor wiring, cursor state advanced correctly but the transparent overlay remained behind an already-frontmost Chrome window on Tahoe.

### Expected

The visual agent cursor should glide or pulse at provable top-level DOM targets while browser input continues through the typed CDP route. The physical mouse pointer, focus, and application z-order must remain unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- Map top-level CSS viewport points to screen coordinates using live native-window bounds and CDP layout metrics.
- Animate typed browser type, click, hover, right-click, double-click, scroll, and drag actions where the target geometry is provable.
- Fail closed for unprovable child/OOPIF geometry.
- Do not alter browser trust, input delivery, focus, activation, or the physical pointer.
- Keep the cursor overlay visible over an already-frontmost target browser without covering an unrelated foreground app.
- Add focused core and macOS regression tests.
- Verify the behavior in a Tahoe recording, including a background-browser isolation oracle.

title: fix(cua-driver): preserve native browser target metadata in recording turns
body:
## Summary

Exact-bound typed browser actions are recorded without the native target PID and window metadata already proven by the browser binding.

This leaves recording turns with screenshots but without target-specific state or click evidence, making reliable crops, highlights, and generated action captions harder.

## Reproduction

Tested with Cua Driver 0.10.0 at source SHA `d5a5e33d6d0b5dc4998c4985bc0704d6df2b0a1d` on macOS Tahoe 26.5.2.

1. Start a Cua Driver recording.
2. Exact-bind a native Chromium window to a CDP target.
3. Perform `browser_type`, `browser_pointer`, and `browser_click`.
4. Stop the recording and inspect each turn's action and evidence metadata.

### Actual

- `action.json` lacks the bound native PID and window ID.
- Before/after state evidence and click evidence are classified as `no_target_pid`.
- Screenshots are still captured, so the recording completes successfully.

### Expected

The recorder should receive the exact native PID and window ID from the already-validated browser binding. That metadata should enable target-specific state capture and evidence without weakening the browser security model.

## Acceptance criteria

- Thread the exact validated native PID and window ID into recording metadata for typed browser actions.
- Include sanitized native target metadata in `action.json`.
- Capture target state and click evidence where the platform supports it.
- Do not weaken binding, consent, routing, or browser-generation checks.
- Add coverage for exact-bound targets and for unprovable targets that must remain targetless.

title: docs: add RFC process and propose typed native Cua Driver core
body:
## Summary

- establish an in-repository RFC process with numbered proposal documents and sidecar assets
- add a GitHub issue form for RFC discussion and decision records
- propose one typed native Cua Driver runtime with embedded SDK and official MCP adapter surfaces
- add reviewer diagrams for architecture and lifecycle ownership

## Why

The current imported SDK is a Rust-authored daemon client, not an embedded desktop runtime. The proposed generic `list_tools_json()` and `call_tool(name, JSON)` boundary also duplicates MCP discovery and invocation semantics. This RFC separates those concerns: typed desktop behavior belongs in the reusable Rust library, while generic protocol behavior belongs in the downstream MCP adapter.

The repository-local RFC process keeps discussion, implementation, tests, and historical decisions together. The GitHub issue remains the discussion and decision record; the Markdown RFC is the stable technical specification.

Related to #2447.

title: docs: make MCP downstream of the Cua Driver SDK
body:
## Summary

- amend RFC 2447 so the public typed `cua-driver-sdk` contract is the architectural boundary
- require Rust, Python, and TypeScript MCP servers to consume the same SDK contract as applications
- prohibit `cua-driver-mcp` from importing private runtime or platform crates directly
- replace the architecture figure and add dependency-boundary acceptance checks

## Why

Review feedback identified that the original diagram still showed the embedded bindings and MCP adapter as peer interfaces over private implementation. That shape could recreate contract drift at a new layer.

The amended RFC makes MCP downstream of the public typed SDK. A Rust MCP server calls the Rust SDK directly; Python and TypeScript servers use generated UniFFI bindings. Rust therefore does not incur an unnecessary C ABI round-trip, while every language consumes one canonical SDK contract.

This amendment incorporates architecture feedback from @r33drichards, preserved in the commit co-author metadata and RFC decision record.

Related to #2447. Amends the RFC introduced in #2450.

## Validation

- parsed RFC frontmatter as YAML
- ran `git diff --check`
- verified all referenced RFC assets exist
- visually inspected the replacement architecture figure
- verified the generated PNG dimensions and checksum

## Release impact

RFC documentation only. No runtime or published package behavior changes.

title: fix(cua-driver): support Electron UniFFI buffers
body:
## Summary

- build a copy-mode variant of the pinned UBRN N-API runtime for Electron hosts
- route generated Cua Driver UniFFI loaders through the packaged compatibility runtime
- preserve the Rust-owned embedded daemon, private endpoint, connection, and MCP semantics
- add Electron-main success/failure lifecycle coverage and package the runtime across release platforms

## Root cause

`@ubjs/node` 0.31.0-3 uses external ArrayBuffers for RustBuffer handoff. Electron 20+ rejects those buffers under its V8 memory cage. The compatibility runtime copies into V8-owned Uint8Arrays and releases Rust-owned return buffers without changing the public SDK API.

## User impact

Electron main processes can use the current daemon-backed TypeScript SDK without `Failed to create external ArrayBuffer`, while preserving the existing public API and lifecycle behavior.

## Verification

- `npm test`
- UniFFI generation check
- TypeScript typecheck and audit
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-sdk`
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --test embedded_host_sdk_mcp_test`
- native npm tarball contents/install smoke

## Lifecycle

The Electron main fixture proves both orderly stop and incompatible-daemon startup failure terminate the Rust-owned child and remove its private endpoint.

## Attribution

The compatibility runtime is built from pinned `uniffi-bindgen-react-native` 0.31.0-3 source under MPL-2.0. The package includes the license notice and deterministic source transformation used to build it.

## Remaining risk

Windows and cross-architecture runtime builds are wired into release CI but were not executed locally.

title: fix(cua-driver): wait for generic type_text completion
body:
## Summary

- wait for the complete AX-observable payload after macOS synthesized-key `type_text` delivery instead of treating any field growth as success
- return a structured `type_text_incomplete` error with requested and delivered character counts when draining stops at a prefix
- add focused synthetic prefix/drain tests and a standalone Chrome fixture row with an ~840-character `BEGIN...END` contenteditable payload and an immediate DOM oracle

## Root cause

macOS posts the generic CGEvent key sequence asynchronously. `type_text` read AXValue once after posting and considered any growth to be verified, so Chromium could still be consuming a queued suffix when the tool reported completion.

Closes #2255.

title: fix(cua-driver): deliver foreground pixel hotkeys through HID
body:
## Summary

- keep the exact macOS target window foreground while pixel-addressed foreground hotkeys are delivered through the HID queue
- prefer non-destructive AX pixel focus before falling back to a real foreground click, preserving Cmd+A selections for same-coordinate typing and Cmd+V
- add deterministic Electron fixture coverage for Cmd+A replacement and Cmd+V paste, plus an installed-Chrome native omnibox regression that reads back AXValue
- retain `verified: false` and `effect: "unverifiable"` for generic hotkeys because the production tool does not read an application postcondition

Fixes #2239.

## Root cause

The foreground pixel-focus click restored the prior application before `hotkey` dispatched its chord. `hotkey` then treated that completed click as sufficient foregrounding and downgraded the chord to PID-routed background events, which native Chromium fields can ignore. A follow-up pixel-addressed `type_text` could also real-click the field again and collapse the Cmd+A selection before inserting text.

title: feat(cua-driver): add versioned native ABI
body:
## Summary

- add a stable v1 C ABI below the public typed Cua Driver SDK
- route the safe Rust embedded SDK through the exported C symbols
- define explicit versioning, ownership, status, panic, cancellation, and lifecycle behavior
- ship the public header in every platform release archive
- compile and run an external C client in CI, alongside existing Python, TypeScript, and Electron coverage

## Architecture

This implements the next slice of RFC #2447. The native core remains private; the safe Rust SDK imports the same versioned ABI seam used by foreign runtimes. UniFFI continues to generate the public Python and TypeScript SDKs above that typed Rust contract. MCP remains downstream and is not reimplemented by the ABI.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-sdk` (16 passed)
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --test embedded_host_sdk_mcp_test` (5 passed)
- `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-driver-sdk --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`
- external C11 smoke: version, create, metadata, inventory, async invoke, shutdown, and idempotent release
- generated UniFFI bindings drift check
- Python real-loader tests (3 passed)
- TypeScript/Node/Electron tests (5 passed) and typecheck
- release archive header-layout smoke

Closes part of #2447.

title: fix(cua-driver): point canonical macOS E2E at the local-install daemon socket
body:
## Problem

The canonical macOS Lume runner installs `CuaDriverLocal.app`, whose daemon listens in the `cua-driver-local` namespace, then invokes `scripts/ci/macos/run-rust-e2e.sh` without setting `CUA_E2E_MACOS_DAEMON_SOCKET`. The testkit therefore probes the release namespace (`~/Library/Caches/cua-driver/cua-driver.sock`) and the strict environment preflight fails even though the installed local daemon is healthy.

Reproduced at source SHA `8d7f120f84a42f0d26c2743f6462736a330137dc` after a successful exact-source `install-local.sh --release --autostart` and successful permission/direct-capture checks.

## Expected

`libs/cua-driver/tests/runners/macos-lume/run-all.sh` exports the socket for the product it just installed before delegating to the lower-level matrix, e.g. the local namespace socket. A manual rerun with that explicit socket passes the strict preflight and proceeds into the GUI matrix.

## Acceptance criteria

- The canonical runner derives or explicitly exports the local-install daemon socket.
- The preflight verifies the same daemon installed and permission-checked by the wrapper.
- A regression test covers release-vs-local namespace selection.
- Contributor-focused runs may still override the socket with `CUA_E2E_MACOS_DAEMON_SOCKET`.

title: fix(cua-driver): make macOS SDK artifacts standalone and correctly tagged
body:
## Problem

The macOS UniFFI SDK dylib currently carries an unresolved `@rpath/libswift_Concurrency.dylib` dependency but no `LC_RPATH`. Loading the locally built Python package from a standalone Python distribution therefore fails before any SDK method can run.

A controlled copy of the same dylib loads successfully after adding `/usr/lib/swift` and `@loader_path` rpaths, confirming the missing final-linker arguments are the immediate cause. The CLI already re-emits equivalent Swift runtime linker arguments because transitive Cargo build-script arguments do not reach final artifacts; the SDK cdylib does not.

The current dylib also declares `LC_BUILD_VERSION minos 13.0`, while the Python wheel is tagged `macosx_11_0_universal2`.

## Expected

- The released macOS SDK dylib loads from a clean standalone Python and Node installation without Xcode-specific environment variables.
- The SDK artifact has stable runtime search paths appropriate for its distribution layout.
- The Python wheel platform tag matches the actual dylib deployment target.
- Release CI asserts both the loader behavior and deployment-target/tag parity before publishing.

## Reproduction

1. Build or stage the macOS SDK package.
2. Inspect the dylib with `otool -L` and `otool -l`.
3. Load it with `ctypes.CDLL(...)` from a standalone Python distribution.
4. Observe dyld failing to resolve `@rpath/libswift_Concurrency.dylib`.

This is a release blocker for the first public SDK package cut.

title: fix(cua-driver): tolerate captured or fileno-less stdio in the Python binary wrapper
body:
## Problem

`cua_driver.run_cua_driver(...)` always passes `sys.stdin`, `sys.stdout`, and `sys.stderr` directly to `subprocess.run`. Hosts such as pytest capture, notebooks, and some embedded Python runtimes replace those streams with file-like objects that do not implement `fileno()`. The wrapper catches the resulting exception and returns exit code 1 before the bundled binary starts.

## Reproduction

With a bundled binary present, call `run_cua_driver(["--version"])` under pytest's default capture. The call reports that redirected stdin has no `fileno()` and returns 1. The same test passes with capture disabled.

## Expected

The wrapper should preserve direct stdio inheritance when real descriptors are available and fall back safely when one or more streams are fileno-less. Add tests for both cases without changing the subprocess exit-code contract.

title: test(cua-driver): make the macOS foreground sentinel report initial focus deterministically
body:
## Problem

The canonical macOS matrix intermittently records `foreground sentinel did not become focus` even though the Electron sentinel is ready and continues emitting heartbeats. The affected rows fail before driver dispatch and therefore provide no action or oracle signal.

The sentinel registers its DOM `focus` listener before `DOMContentLoaded`, then writes `ready`, activates the native window, and waits for a later `focus` event. If Electron is already focused when the renderer becomes ready, re-activating that same window does not have to emit another DOM focus event. The journal then contains only `ready` and `heartbeat` until the timeout.

## Expected

When the renderer becomes ready, journal its current `document.hasFocus()` state as a focus event before relying on subsequent focus transitions. Keep the native activation, z-order, focus-loss, leaked-input, and heartbeat oracles unchanged so a genuinely unfocused sentinel still fails closed.

Add focused coverage and require the affected macOS cells to pass in the canonical logged-in E2E lane.

title: install-local can stage a stale binary when CARGO_TARGET_DIR is set
body:
## Summary

`libs/cua-driver/scripts/install-local.sh` forwards `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` to Cargo, but `_install-local-rust.sh` always stages the binary from `$REPO_ROOT/target/$BUILD_CONFIG/cua-driver`.

When a custom target directory is set, the script can build the requested source successfully and then install an older binary left in the workspace-local `target/` directory.

## Reproduction

1. Leave an older `cua-driver` binary under `libs/cua-driver/rust/target/release/`.
2. Set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` to a fresh absolute build directory.
3. Run `libs/cua-driver/scripts/install-local.sh --release`.
4. Compare the binary in `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release/cua-driver` with the installed/staged binary.

## Expected

The installer stages the binary Cargo just built, including when `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is set.

## Actual

Cargo builds into the custom target directory, while the installer copies from the hardcoded workspace `target/` path. Exact-source provenance checks can therefore report the previous commit after a successful local install.

## Suggested direction

Resolve the target directory through Cargo (or honor `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`) once, then use that same canonical path for the build-output existence check and staging copy. Add a regression test with a stale workspace target and a fresh custom target.

title: macOS Lume gate rejects successful direct CLI permission payload
body:
## Summary

The canonical macOS Lume runner rejects a successful live permission probe because it expects the old MCP envelope shape from the `call` CLI.

## Reproduction

On Cua Driver 0.12.2, run the canonical gate with Accessibility and Screen Recording granted. The command:

```bash
cua-driver-local call check_permissions '{"prompt":true}'
```

prints the structured permission payload directly, including:

```json
{
  "accessibility": true,
  "screen_recording": true,
  "screen_recording_capturable": true,
  "direct_capture_status": "ready"
}
```

The runner checks `.structuredContent.screen_recording_capturable` and `.structuredContent.direct_capture_status`, so the assertion fails even though both capabilities are ready.

## Expected

The gate should validate the CLI's documented direct payload shape. For transition safety it may accept both the direct object and an enveloped `structuredContent` object.

## Impact

A healthy exact-commit macOS certification run is reported as failed, blocking release verification.

## Suggested fix

Normalize with `(.structuredContent // .)` before checking the two fields, then keep the capability assertions unchanged.

title: computer-server: macOS handler import can segfault during Python finalization
body:
## Summary

Importing the macOS automation handler can complete successfully and then exit with SIGSEGV during Python finalization. This makes otherwise-passing computer-server processes and tests intermittently report exit 139.

## Reproduction

Tested from main commit `6f75428493441810a4ec2f2317f85e0dfc658fb5` with Python 3.12 and PyObjC 12.2.1 on macOS 26.5:

```bash
python -c "from computer_server.handlers.macos import MacOSAutomationHandler; print(MacOSAutomationHandler.__name__, flush=True)"
```

The class name is printed, then the process terminates with SIGSEGV. Importing `AppKit` alone exits normally.

## Sanitized crash signature

```text
EXC_BAD_ACCESS / SIGSEGV at 0x20
objc_release
object_dealloc (objc-object.m)
dict_tp_clear
gc_collect_main
finalize_modules
Py_FinalizeEx
```

## Likely cause

The module-level accessibility permission probe creates a CoreGraphics event through PyObjC and also calls `CFRelease(me)` manually. The Python proxy appears to release the same object again at shutdown. Removing the manual release should be tested against both the crash and the permission-prompt behavior.

## Expected

Importing or cleanly shutting down computer-server on macOS exits 0 after all handlers/runtime resources are closed.

## Acceptance criteria

- The minimal import exits 0 repeatedly.
- The full computer-server test suite no longer intermittently exits 139 after all tests pass.
- macOS accessibility permission prompting still works when intentionally exercised.

- adds an optional `cua-driver` backend backed by the published generated Python SDK

- exposes desktop state and explicit scope escalation through both HTTP and MCP while preserving legacy fallbacks only for actions absent from the driver contract
- shares and closes one runtime across HTTP/MCP lifecycles

Closes #2489

title: lume: stale resize guard blocks stop and force-delete
body:
## Summary

Lume 0.3.15 can leave a zero-byte `.resize.guard` after a disk resize reaches its recorded target. Both `lume stop <vm>` and `lume delete <vm> --force` then refuse to operate with:

```
A previous disk resize of <vm> did not finish. Re-run the same command to roll it back and restore the disk from its backup.
```

This can make a disposable VM impossible to clean up through the CLI even when its current `config.json` and `config.json.backup` agree on the disk size.

## Observed

- Lume version: 0.3.15
- VM remained running and usable.
- The guard was an empty file.
- Current and backup configuration recorded the same completed disk size.
- `get` reported no active provisioning operation.
- `stop` and force-delete both returned the unfinished-resize error.

## Expected

Lume should either:

1. recognize a stale/completed guard and clear it safely, or
2. expose an explicit recovery command that identifies the interrupted resize parameters.

Force-delete of an explicitly named disposable VM should not require reconstructing an unknown historical resize command.

## Workaround

Moving the stale guard aside, then running `stop` and `delete --force`, succeeded. This should be handled and validated by Lume rather than requiring filesystem intervention.

## Suggested coverage

Add an integration test with a stale guard where current and backup config sizes agree, covering `stop`, recovery diagnostics, and force-delete.

title: fix(cua-driver): fail loudly when local signing falls back to ad-hoc TCC identity
body:
## Problem

On macOS, `install-local.sh` silently falls back to an ad-hoc signature when `ensure_local_signing_identity` returns `-`. The install succeeds without the existing explicit reset warning, but the app designated requirement becomes `cdhash H"…"`. Every rebuild then changes that requirement, invalidates Accessibility and Screen Recording, and leaves System Settings showing a stale enabled-looking row while `permissions status --json` reports both grants as false.

This reproduces with Cua Driver 0.12.2 on a fresh disposable macOS 26 VM. It is adjacent to #2230, but the release/local namespace split from that issue is already present; the remaining failure is silent local-identity provisioning/fallback.

## Minimal reproduction

1. On a fresh macOS VM, run `bash libs/cua-driver/scripts/install-local.sh --autostart` without a preconfigured signing keychain.
2. Grant Accessibility and Screen Recording to `CuaDriverLocal.app`.
3. Confirm `codesign -d -r- /Applications/CuaDriverLocal.app` prints a `cdhash` requirement.
4. Change and rebuild the driver with the same install command.
5. The new app has a different `cdhash`; `cua-driver-local permissions status --json` reports the grants as false even though the existing Settings row may still look enabled.

## Expected behavior

- A normal local rebuild either uses a persistent certificate-backed identity and preserves TCC, or stops before replacing a working installation.
- The installer must never present an ad-hoc fallback as an ordinary successful install when the intended workflow requires persistent TCC.

## Suggested direction

- Always emit a prominent warning when `SIGN_ID == "-"`; today the explicit “permissions will reset” message is only emitted when a non-`-` identity was found but signing failed.
- Add a strict flag/environment mode for behavior/E2E lanes that refuses an ad-hoc app signature.
- Run a post-install designated-requirement check and print the exact remediation: configure/unlock `CUA_DRIVER_LOCAL_SIGNING_KEYCHAIN`, trust the local certificate, set the key partition list, rerun install, then grant once.
- Consider making the dedicated signing-keychain bootstrap a repository command instead of a multi-step manual README sequence.
- Add a shell test covering the `SIGN_ID == "-"` branch and asserting that ad-hoc signing can never be silent.

## Acceptance criteria

- Certificate-backed local rebuilds keep the same designated requirement and preserve TCC.
- An ad-hoc fallback is unmistakable in installer output.
- Strict E2E mode fails before installing an ad-hoc bundle.
- The post-install check distinguishes certificate-backed (`certificate leaf`) from `cdhash` requirements.

title: fix(cua-driver): prevent silent ad-hoc local signing
body:
## Summary

- make every macOS ad-hoc local-signing fallback prominent and explain that Accessibility and Screen Recording grants will be invalidated on rebuild
- add `--require-stable-signing` / `CUA_DRIVER_REQUIRE_STABLE_SIGNING=1` so behavior and E2E lanes stop before replacing the live app without a certificate-backed identity
- prefer an existing dedicated local signing keychain and document the bootstrap/partition-list flow
- verify the staged and copied designated requirements, restoring the prior app if the installed signature differs

## Root cause

When local identity discovery or certificate-backed `codesign` failed with no existing certificate-signed app, the installer could silently sign ad-hoc. That creates a `cdhash` designated requirement which changes on every rebuild, invalidating TCC grants while leaving stale enabled-looking rows in System Settings.

## User impact

Normal local development can still opt into ad-hoc signing, but it is no longer silent. Strict verification lanes fail safely with actionable dedicated-keychain bootstrap instructions, and successful installs report whether their designated requirement is stable or rebuild-dependent.

Fixes #2494.

title: fix(cua-driver): diagnose stale release MCP registrations after local identity migration
body:
## Summary

After the local/release identity split in #2404, `install-local` correctly installs a separate `cua-driver-local` product. However, it can leave an existing MCP client configured to the old release command while the release app and CLI are absent.

The local installation succeeds and is healthy, but the client still launches a missing `cua-driver` path and fails at startup with `ENOENT`. The resulting host state is confusing: `CuaDriverLocal.app` and `cua-driver-local` exist, while `CuaDriver.app` and `cua-driver` do not.

## Minimal reproduction

On macOS:

1. Configure an MCP client to launch `$HOME/.local/bin/cua-driver mcp`.
2. Ensure the published product is not installed:
   - `/Applications/CuaDriver.app` is absent.
   - `$HOME/.local/bin/cua-driver` is absent.
3. Run the current source installer:

   ```bash
   ./libs/cua-driver/scripts/install-local.sh --release
   ```

4. Confirm the local product was installed:
   - `/Applications/CuaDriverLocal.app` exists.
   - `$HOME/.local/bin/cua-driver-local` exists.
5. Restart the MCP client.

Actual: the client still launches the absent release command and Cua Driver is unavailable.

Expected: the local installer detects that the release CLI is absent and clearly identifies the identity migration. It should provide exact commands for either reconfiguring the client to `cua-driver-local` or reinstalling the published product.

## Root cause

#2404 deliberately stopped source builds from writing the release namespace. That is the correct ownership boundary, but the post-install flow assumes clients are already configured for the new local binary. It does not diagnose the common legacy registration that still points at `cua-driver`.

This is distinct from #2230: that issue addressed macOS TCC identity transitions. This issue covers client operability after the namespace migration.

## Constraints

- Do not create a `cua-driver -> cua-driver-local` compatibility symlink; that would collapse the identity boundary again.
- Do not overwrite an installed release product.
- Do not silently rewrite client configuration.
- Keep local and release uninstall ownership separate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unix/macOS and Windows local installers run a post-install release-CLI preflight.
- [ ] When the release CLI is absent, output explicitly says existing clients configured for `cua-driver` will not use the local build.
- [ ] Output gives the exact local `mcp-config` command and the published-install alternative.
- [ ] No migration warning is shown when the release CLI exists.
- [ ] Regression tests cover both states and preserve the release/local ownership boundary.

Related: #2230, #2404.

title: docs(cua-driver): add agentic Python and TypeScript tutorials beyond capture
body:
## Goal

Extend the Cua Driver SDK documentation from a first lifecycle/capture success into a deterministic perceive → act → verify workflow, then show how agent applications integrate the same driver through the native SDK and MCP routes.

## Documentation shape (Diátaxis)

### Tutorials

Use one safe local fixture and one observable task across languages—for example, inspect a small desktop app, enter known text, submit it, and verify the resulting UI state. The learner should see:

1. session creation with an explicit capture scope
2. perception of the current state
3. one or more typed actions
4. an external postcondition proving the action was consumed
5. orderly session and runtime teardown

The tutorial must demonstrate more than returning screen dimensions or a screenshot. It should be deterministic, reversible, and runnable without private services.

### Agentic how-to guides

Provide runnable Python and TypeScript examples for:

- Claude Agent SDK
- Codex SDK

Show the two integration routes where the agent SDK supports them:

1. **Native application route:** the agent harness registers narrowly scoped tool callbacks backed by same-process `CuaDriver.create()`.
2. **MCP route:** the agent runtime connects to `cua-driver mcp`, using the standard daemon-backed agent boundary.

Do not force false symmetry. Claude Agent SDK exposes Python/TypeScript custom tools and MCP. Codex SDK is published for Python and TypeScript, but its supported extension boundary may make MCP the correct Cua Driver route. Confirm the current public SDK contract and document any provider-specific limitation instead of building a bespoke tool loop. If direct tool callbacks are not supported, use the OpenAI Agents SDK for the native-callback comparison and keep Codex on MCP.

Current upstream references:

- Claude Agent SDK: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/sdk
- Codex SDK: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex-sdk

### Explanation/reference

Keep the examples consistent with the architecture docs:

- native SDK is the primary same-process client-app route
- MCP + host is the primary external-agent route
- an app-local native tool adapter is useful only when the application already owns the agent loop and driver lifecycle
- do not present generated language clients as an alternative MCP client

## Lifecycle ergonomics

The TypeScript tutorial currently needs both `await driver.shutdown()` and `driver.uniffiDestroy()`. Before expanding the examples, either:

- add a public `close()` / async-disposal wrapper that drains the runtime and releases the UniFFI handle, or
- clearly document the two responsibilities and keep `uniffiDestroy()` as a generated low-level escape hatch.

Prefer a public API that does not expose UniFFI terminology in ordinary application code. Python should have an equivalent context-manager story where practical.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Python and TypeScript perceive → act → verify tutorials use the same deterministic fixture
- [ ] examples exercise published `cua-driver` and `@trycua/cua-driver` packages
- [ ] Claude Agent SDK examples cover Python and TypeScript
- [ ] Codex SDK examples cover Python and TypeScript through its supported Cua Driver boundary
- [ ] native and MCP routes are compared without duplicating the Cua Driver implementation
- [ ] every example has explicit session, permission, shutdown, timeout, and unknown-action-outcome handling
- [ ] code snippets are extracted from executable examples or compiled/tested in CI
- [ ] tests use no committed credentials and skip provider-backed execution cleanly when secrets are absent
- [ ] tutorials, how-to guides, reference, and explanation remain separate Diátaxis modes

title: cua-driver skills install fails on prerelease versions (resolves wrong monorepo component as "latest")
body:
**Version**: cua-driver-rs 0.12.2 (macOS arm64)

`cua-driver skills install` fails with:

`cua-driver skills install: failed to fetch skill pack to ~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver
`
(also fails with --from main, --json, --no-cache, after clearing the local dir, and with RUST_LOG=debug — no underlying reason is ever surfaced)

**Cause**: 
cua-driver-rs-v0.12.2 was published with prerelease: true. /repos/trycua/cua/releases/latest returns the most recent non-prerelease release repo-wide — currently an unrelated npm-fleet-v0.0.3 release, since this monorepo tags multiple components together. Skill-pack lookup resolves to the wrong release and finds no asset.

Confirmed the correct release + asset exist fine directly:

`curl -sL https://api.github.com/repos/trycua/cua/releases/tags/cua-driver-rs-v0.12.2
`
→ 200 OK, includes cua-driver-rs-v0.12.2-skills.tar.gz.

**Fix suggestion**: 
resolve by the installed cua-driver's own tag (/releases/tags/cua-driver-rs-v<version>) instead of the repo-wide /releases/latest.

**Workaround**:
```
curl -sL -o /tmp/cua-skills.tar.gz \
  https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/download/cua-driver-rs-v0.12.2/cua-driver-rs-v0.12.2-skills.tar.gz
mkdir -p ~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver
tar -xzf /tmp/cua-skills.tar.gz -C ~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver
mv ~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver/cua-driver-rs-v0.12.2-skills/* ~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver/
rmdir ~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver/cua-driver-rs-v0.12.2-skills
```

After the commands above `cua-driver skills status` should verify the correct installation.

title: cua-driver: foreground pixel type_text false-confirms on Chromium web editor
body:
### Problem

On macOS, the pixel form of `type_text` can return `path: key_events_fg`, `verified: true`, and `effect: confirmed` for a Chromium web editor even though a fresh screenshot shows the editor is still empty.

This is distinct from the AX-write echo fixed in #2081: the false confirmation occurs after foreground CGEvent keystrokes.

### Environment

- cua-driver 0.10.0 (aarch64-macos)
- macOS 26.5.2
- Google Chrome
- Exact browser window targeted by pid + window_id

### Minimal trace

1. Capture the browser window; confirm a visible web editor is empty.
2. Call `type_text` with pid, window_id, editor screenshot coordinates, non-empty text, and `delivery_mode: foreground`.
3. The tool returns:

```json
{
  "characters": 149,
  "effect": "confirmed",
  "path": "key_events_fg",
  "verified": true
}
```

4. Capture the same window immediately afterward. The editor is still empty.
5. Activating the editor action confirms the application also sees an empty query, so this is not only a rendering lag.

### Expected

When application-level delivery cannot be proven, return `verified: false` / `effect: unverifiable` and require screenshot or DOM confirmation.

### Likely gap

`cgevent_type_verified` validates CGEvent delivery by reading `AXValue` from the focused element. The web-surface distrust check currently only downgrades confirmations when `path == PATH_AX`. A focused Chromium web element can apparently expose an AX value that grows even though the renderer-owned editor state did not change, so the key-event path can still make the same class of false claim.

Consider applying the AXWebArea distrust rule to `PATH_KEY_EVENTS` and `PATH_KEY_EVENTS_FG` when verification depends only on AXValue, or cross-checking an independent DOM/renderer signal before reporting `confirmed`.

title: cua-driver: semantic outline includes enabled button but refs omit it
body:
## Summary

A complete `semantic_v2` browser snapshot can include a visible, enabled, focusable button in `outline` while omitting that same button from both `refs` and `content_refs`. The agent can see that the control exists but cannot target it with `browser_click`.

## Environment

- Cua Driver: `0.10.0`
- Browser: Chromium on macOS
- Binding: exact existing-profile browser target
- Snapshot: `semantic_v2`, `complete: true`

## Minimal sanitized trace

Before typing, the snapshot exposes the form field as an actionable ref:

```text
outline:
  - textbox "Enter sitemap URL"
  - button "SUBMIT" [focusable=true]

refs:
  - ref: p59:69
    role: textbox
    name: Enter sitemap URL
    actions: [type, pointer]

content_refs:
  # no entry for SUBMIT

snapshot:
  complete: true
  selected_nodes: 203
  total_nodes: 203
```

After typing a valid value, the outline still shows the enabled button, but neither ref collection includes it:

```text
outline:
  - textbox "Enter sitemap URL": sitemap.xml
  - button "SUBMIT" [focusable=true]

refs:
  - ref: p55:1
    role: textbox
    name: Enter sitemap URL
    value: sitemap.xml
    actions: [type, pointer]

content_refs:
  # no entry for SUBMIT

snapshot:
  complete: true
  selected_nodes: 203
  total_nodes: 203
```

The omission persisted across multiple fresh snapshots.

## Expected behavior

Every visible, enabled, focusable element that appears as an actionable control in the semantic outline should receive a current ref with the corresponding declared action, or the snapshot should explain why it was excluded.

## Actual behavior

The button is present in the complete outline but absent from both ref collections, so:

- `browser_click` cannot target it;
- the macOS trusted coordinate route correctly refuses background delivery because it may activate the standalone browser window;
- the background-safe `dom_event` route cannot be used because it requires a ref.

## Impact

This leaves an otherwise exact, background-bound workflow stuck even though the snapshot proves that the actionable control exists. It also creates an internal consistency problem: `outline` says the control is present and focusable, while the ref surface says it is untargetable without an explicit refusal reason.

## Suggested direction

- Derive `outline` and actionable refs from the same inclusion decision, or
- return an exclusion/refusal diagnostic for outline controls that are intentionally omitted from refs.
- Add a regression fixture where a Material-style form button transitions from disabled to enabled after input, and assert that the enabled button receives a click ref.

Related but distinct: #2176 covers escalation when background input delivery is unavailable; this report is about an actionable element disappearing from the exact ref surface before dispatch.

title: Windows: `hotkey`/`press_key` reject letter keys ("Unknown key: <letter>") — Ctrl+A/C/V/S unusable
body:
## Summary

On Windows, both `hotkey` and `press_key` reject **letter keys** (`a`–`z`) with the error `Unknown key: <letter>`, before any input is dispatched. This makes every `Ctrl`/`Alt`/`Win` + letter combination (Ctrl+A, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+S, …) impossible to send. Non-letter combinations work fine, so the failure is specifically in parsing the letter key, not in the modifier/dispatch machinery.

Both tool schemas explicitly advertise letters as valid, so this is also a docs-vs-behavior mismatch:

- `press_key`: *"Key vocabulary: return, tab, escape, up/down/left/right, space, delete, home, end, pageup, pagedown, f1-f12, **plus any letter or digit**."*
- `hotkey`: *"Non-modifier keys use the same vocabulary as `press_key` (…, **letters, digits**). Order: modifiers first, one non-modifier last."*

## Environment

- cua-driver **0.12.3** (windows x86_64), installed via `install.ps1`
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200
- Invoked through the MCP server (`cua-driver mcp`); daemon running in interactive session 1
- Target window: a legacy Win32 app (1C:Enterprise thick client), but since the error fires during key parsing — before dispatch — the target type is irrelevant.

## Steps to reproduce

```
hotkey    { keys: ["ctrl", "a"] }        ->  error: "Unknown key: a"
hotkey    { keys: ["ctrl", "c"] }        ->  error: "Unknown key: c"
press_key { key: "c", modifiers: ["ctrl"] } ->  error: "Unknown key: c"
```

## Actual result

`Unknown key: a` / `Unknown key: c` — the call errors out; no key event is delivered.

## Expected result

The combination is dispatched to the target window (e.g. Ctrl+A selects all in the focused control), as the schema documents.

## Evidence that only letter parsing is broken

A non-letter combination on the **same window, same session** succeeds:

```
hotkey { keys: ["shift", "home"] }  ->  "✅ Pressed shift+home on pid <…> via PostMessage (Win32 target)."
```

So modifiers, target resolution, and the Win32 delivery path all work — the regression is isolated to how single-letter key names are resolved. The same `Unknown key` failure occurs on both the `hotkey` and `press_key` code paths, which suggests a shared key-name lookup table that is missing the `a`–`z` entries on Windows.

## Impact

Any workflow that relies on clipboard or app accelerators bound to Ctrl+letter (Ctrl+A/C/V/X, Ctrl+S, Ctrl+F, …) cannot be driven on Windows.

## Workarounds currently in use

- Select-all: `End` then `Shift+Home` (both non-letter keys work).
- Clear field: `End` then `Backspace` × N.
- Save (Ctrl+S): invoke the toolbar/menu button via `element_index` instead.
- Copy/read: read the value out of the UIA tree (`get_window_state`) instead of Ctrl+C.
- Paste/insert text: use `type_text` (routes through `WM_CHAR`, which is unaffected — the letter *vocabulary* limitation is only in the key-name path).

This is a longstanding issue: the same `Unknown key: <letter>` behavior was present in 0.6.8 and still reproduces on 0.12.3.

title: fix(cua-sandbox): use pool template for Fleet claims
body:
## Root Cause

The live E2E pool `cua-pr2519-e2e-1784871193` was healthy enough to boot, but its claim used the wrong template key:

- Authoritative Loki evidence shows the operator created `ecr-credentials` and Sandbox `cua-pr2519-e2e-1784871193-ddca1963` at 05:33:44 UTC. KubeVirt started the domain around 05:34:40 UTC; the guest agent, network, qemu-guest-agent, noVNC, and computer services then started.
- The claim started at 05:35:49 UTC but repeatedly reported an empty warm pool until its 600-second bind deadline; cleanup completed at 05:45:57 UTC.
- `FleetCloudTransport` passed `sandboxTemplateRef.name = pool.metadata.name`, while the generated Cyclops SDK's default claim path uses `<pool>-template`. The controller hashes that ref to select `WARM_QUEUE`, so the explicit pool name searched a different queue than the Ready sandbox's template.

This is not the already-fixed per-pool `ExternalSecret` regression in Cloud PR #5780.

## Fix

- Let `CyclopsClient.create_claim` apply its canonical `spec=None` default, which derives `<pool>-template` from the pool name.
- Add a regression test that exercises `FleetCloudTransport.connect()` and asserts no mismatched explicit claim spec is sent.

## Validation

- RED before the fix: `tests/test_fleet_cloud_transport.py::test_connect_uses_generated_pool_template_claim_default` failed with `ClaimSpec()` instead of `None`.
- GREEN after the fix: the same test passed.
- `PYTHONPATH=. /tmp/cua-pr2519-fleet-test-venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_fleet_cloud_transport.py tests/test_fleet_cloud_client.py` - `10 passed`.
- Ruff check and format check passed for both changed files; `compileall` passed.

## Constraints

- The broad local `cua-sandbox` suite is not a valid signal in this container: 110 passed, 83 skipped, 29 failed, and 19 errored due to absent local-runtime dependencies / an incompatible test loop environment. `uv lock --check` also fails on unchanged `main` because the lockfile is stale. No packaging or timeout changes are included.
- A live rerun requires deployment of this PR plus authorized Fleet credentials that can create and delete an isolated pool/claim. No live E2E was run from this branch.

title: Cua Driver: native ConsoleHost drops type_text on Windows 11 ARM64 without a hard failure
body:
## Summary

On Windows 11 Pro ARM64, Cua Driver 0.12.4 can snapshot a native Windows PowerShell ConsoleHost window, but `type_text` does not reach the prompt. The call completes without a hard delivery refusal, while a fresh snapshot and independent screen observation both show an unchanged blank prompt.

This reproduced twice in an interactive user session. Typed browser input through the first-class CDP route works normally on the same machine, so the failure appears specific to native ConsoleHost input delivery.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro ARM64
- Cua Driver 0.12.4 from the published `windows-arm64` release asset
- `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`
- Daemon and target process both running in the interactive user session
- Native Windows PowerShell / ConsoleHost target

## Reproduction

1. Start Cua Driver in an interactive Windows user session.
2. Declare a session.
3. Launch native Windows PowerShell through `launch_app`.
4. Take a fresh `get_window_state` snapshot and select the prompt/window.
5. Call `type_text` against the target. Re-test once with explicit foreground delivery.
6. Take another `get_window_state` snapshot.

## Actual

The input call completes without a hard failure that tells the caller the characters were dropped. No text appears at the PowerShell prompt. The unchanged state was confirmed after both attempts.

## Expected

Either:

- the requested text is delivered and visible in the post-action snapshot, or
- the action returns a hard, actionable refusal/no-op classification so an agent can safely choose another setup channel.

## Notes

This did not block browser automation. Exact Edge binding, CDP typing, trusted clicking, and cursor overlay all passed on the same ARM64 release binary. The issue is scoped to the native ConsoleHost path.

title: fix(cua-driver): enforce authorization in embedded SDK
body:
## Summary

- enforce managed/user policy, permission mode, bounded manifests, hard invariants, and reviewed-risk checks at the native tool-registry boundary used by `CuaDriver.create()`
- validate authorization configuration before constructing a same-process SDK runtime
- publish one machine-readable permission-adapter inventory through SDK and daemon tool discovery plus authorization status
- classify screenshot-to-file operations as R3 file egress instead of ordinary R2 observation
- document the exact active, metadata-only, and not-exposed surface and the reviewed delivery plan for #2385 and #2437

## Why

RFC 2447 made the same-process SDK the canonical application path, but that path invoked the native registry without passing through `authorize_tool_call`. Daemon transports performed the check, so direct Python/TypeScript/Rust SDK callers could bypass the process authorization stack.

This change moves the authoritative check to the shared native dispatch boundary. Transport checks remain defense-in-depth and have no consent side effects.

The adapter inventory remains deliberately narrow:

- `browser_prepare.existing_profile` is the only active protected-consent adapter
- observation, desktop input, file/egress, and consequential-browser groups remain `metadata_only`
- device, shell, and generic network groups remain `not_exposed`

No new user-owned capability is labeled active before a certified protected host and platform certification exist.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core` — 348 unit tests, 2 contract tests, and 3 session lifecycle tests passed
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-sdk` — 17 tests passed
- `cargo test -p cua-driver sdk_adapter::tests` — passed
- `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core -p cua-driver-sdk -p cua-driver --all-targets -- -D warnings -A clippy::missing_safety_doc` — passed
- `npm run docs:check-hygiene` — passed
- `npm run docs:check-links` — passed
- `npm run docs:check` — generated Cua Driver and Lume references have no drift

The unmodified current `platform-macos` source has two pre-existing `missing_safety_doc` warnings, so the scoped Clippy run allows only that lint while denying every other warning.

## Review and follow-up

Claude Code Opus independently reviewed the plan against the exact base SHA and confirmed the same-process bypass. Its accepted findings are incorporated in the checked-in plan.

This is the first dependency-safe slice. It progresses #2385 and #2437 but does not close either umbrella:

- trusted mixed-mode session selection still requires an authenticated action connection (#2410 or an equivalent multiplexed channel)
- user-owned active adapters still require the protected host/indicator work in #2411
- concurrent bounded sessions require replacing the process-global manifest with an immutable per-session store

title: health_report blocks forever on GNOME/Wayland after first xdg-desktop-portal screenshot (stale request path)
body:
{
  "title": "health_report blocks forever on GNOME/Wayland after first xdg-desktop-portal screenshot (stale request path)",
  "body": "## Description

On GNOME 50 / Wayland (Ubuntu 26.04), cua-driver 0.12.4 `health_report` blocks indefinitely after the first screenshot capture is performed. The root cause is that the xdg-desktop-portal Screenshot `request` object path becomes stale after the first use, and subsequent calls hang waiting for a portal response that never arrives.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, GNOME 50 (Wayland session, `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`)
- Compositor: Mutter/GNOME Shell (no `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1`, no `zwlr_screencopy_manager_v1`)
- cua-driver: 0.12.4
- Wayland utils: `grim` + `slurp` installed (fallback path)
- Portal: `xdg-desktop-portal-gnome` + `xdg-desktop-portal-gtk` running
- Env: `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`, `DISPLAY=:0`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start daemon: `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1 cua-driver serve` (with `--dangerously-bypass-approvals`)
2. Approve the xdg-desktop-portal screenshot consent dialog (appears on first capture)
3. Run a successful capture (e.g. `cua-driver call get_window_state ...`)
4. Run `cua-driver call health_report`

## Expected

`health_report` returns the report immediately (works correctly on a fresh daemon before any capture).

## Actual

`health_report` blocks forever. Daemon log shows:
```
WARN  zbus::proxy  Failed to populate properties cache via GetAll: 
  org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.UnknownMethod: Object does not exist at path 
  "/org/freedesktop/portal/desktop/request/1_474/ashpd_dU52bNMZHN"
```

The portal request object was consumed by the previous screenshot call.

## Workaround

Restart the daemon before calling `health_report`.

## Additional Context

Also affects `hermes computer-use doctor` which spawns `cua-driver mcp` and calls `health_report`.",
  "labels": ["bug", "linux", "wayland"]
}

title: feat(cua-driver): make SDK-owned runtime the default
body:
## Summary

Implements RFC #2549 end to end while preserving the released CLI, MCP, Python, TypeScript, and daemon compatibility contracts:

- makes the SDK-owned same-process runtime the primary application topology
- makes bare stdio MCP own that runtime directly on Windows and Linux while preserving the signed macOS service/TCC path
- adds a supervised private-worker topology over inherited stdin/stdout, with no listener, discovery, or reconnect surface
- adds trusted, immutable, session-bound authorization for same-process, private-worker, and authenticated embedded-service hosts
- adds a transport-free Rust remote carrier seam with authenticated principal, connection generation, deadlines, and unknown-completion handling
- retains the explicit daemon/socket topology for compatibility, shared app hosting, and stable OS identity
- keeps one direct runtime per process until the remaining process-global facilities are isolated

## Security and lifecycle

Authority remains downstream of model-controlled inputs. Public session labels, tool arguments, environment overrides, MCP metadata, and ordinary socket clients cannot mint, replay, select, or widen a trusted session.

- trusted sessions bind one immutable mode and policy to one runtime generation and action connection
- expiration, revocation, duplicate live labels, session substitution, and use after shutdown fail before platform dispatch
- private workers receive their runtime configuration only over the inherited channel and terminate when the owning host channel closes
- caller-provided child environments cannot override authorization controls; process-admin managed policy and disablement variables are inherited by private workers and embedded services
- embedded-service authority requires the original host process connection, same Unix UID or Windows SID, and an exact available parent PID
- Unix service I/O uses bounded polling with an overall action deadline and preserves partial UTF-8 frames; lost action responses report `completion=unknown`
- Windows CI executes the trusted-host PID/SID regression tests
- loopback HTTP MCP remains disabled without an explicit 32–4096-character bearer token
- runtime drop revokes its own authorization generation, releases browser claim markers, terminates private workers, and finalizes runtime-owned recordings without touching a replacement runtime

## Compatibility and release impact

This is an additive SDK/ABI capability and a user-visible topology change, so the `feat(cua-driver)` title intentionally requests a minor Cua Driver release.

- existing CLI commands and MCP tool/envelope shapes remain available
- existing Python and TypeScript constructors, exports, signatures, and declarations remain compatible
- `CuaDriver.create()` remains the same-process constructor; `connect()` remains the daemon compatibility path
- private workers are additive through `create_private_worker()` / `createPrivateWorker()`
- trusted-session creation stays a top-level factory, so released structural interfaces gain no required member
- the C ABI advances additively from 1.0 to 1.1
- bare `cua-driver mcp` no longer discovers a default service on Windows/Linux; callers intentionally sharing a service continue to use `--socket`
- `mcp --embedded` without its host-provided private endpoint now fails closed
- no concrete gRPC dependency or generated Python/TypeScript remote constructor is introduced; carriers remain transport-orthogonal

## Verification

Local evidence on the final implementation:

- Cua Driver SDK unit tests: 27 passed
- Cua Driver binary unit tests: 130 passed
- private-worker/service integration: 3 passed, subprocess trust probe passed, 1 helper ignored
- daemon-required authorization integration: 8 passed
- Cua Driver core serialized unit suite: 369 passed
- Python package: 28 passed, 3 skipped
- TypeScript package: 6 passed
- generated UniFFI Python/TypeScript bindings: current
- generated Cua Driver and Lume reference docs: current
- Rust formatting/checks and `git diff --check`: passed

CI additionally compiles and exercises the platform-specific paths on Linux, macOS, and Windows. The Nix Rust-test source now includes the compatibility fixtures used by compile-time contract tests.

## Independent review

Claude Code Opus 5 performed two read-only architecture/security passes. The first pass returned NO-GO on two release blockers:

1. embedded-service socket poll timeouts were incorrectly acting as total action deadlines
2. the Windows host-PID predicate could accept unavailable values

Both were fixed with regressions. The focused second pass returned **GO** with no new release blockers. Its additional hardening observations incorporated here include Windows execution of the PID test, partial UTF-8 preservation, async offloading of session-close I/O, managed-policy inheritance across child topologies, and runtime-scoped recording cleanup.

Implements #2549 and progresses #2437. The merged RFC in #2550 supersedes the earlier daemonless proposal.

body:
## Primary area

Cua Driver

## Summary

Make the typed `CuaDriver` SDK and its owned native runtime the default application boundary. Keep private workers and authenticated long-lived services as explicit optional topologies. This RFC supersedes #2447 while retaining its typed SDK, generated binding, private native core, versioned C ABI, and downstream-adapter decisions.

## Motivation and current state

The daemon originally provided useful lifecycle ownership, stable platform identity, shared state, and crash isolation. Requiring that topology for every integration now adds process, socket, version, reconnect, and delegation complexity to applications that already own their automation lifecycle.

The SDK can now construct the native runtime in the importing process. The architecture needs a focused decision about who owns that state, how permission modes are isolated, when MCP can own a runtime, and when a worker or service is still the right boundary.

## Goals

- Make direct SDK creation the documented default.
- Start with one direct runtime per process.
- Put different permission modes in separate runtime-owner processes.
- Keep standalone macOS MCP under the stable CuaDriver.app identity.
- Preserve one typed contract and one authorization path across topologies.
- Define lifecycle, platform, service-authentication, and rollback gates.

## Non-goals

- Remove daemon or service support.
- Support multiple direct runtimes in one process in the first milestone.
- Treat in-process objects as a security boundary against their host.
- Let an agent select or widen its permission mode.
- Change the active protected-consent coverage tracked by #2385.

## Proposal

Applications use `CuaDriver.create(options)` and own one stateful runtime until shutdown. Hosts that need process isolation use a private, non-reattachable worker. Deployments that intentionally serve external clients use an authenticated service.

MCP owns a runtime directly on Windows, Linux, and embedded macOS paths. Standalone installed MCP on macOS continues through CuaDriver.app so TCC grants retain a stable responsible identity. Gateways with mixed permission modes use separate runtime-owner processes, with unrestricted mode requiring explicit launch-time acknowledgement.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep the shared daemon as the default for every integration.
- Delegate mixed permission modes through sessions in one shared daemon.
- Remove every daemon and worker topology.
- Make desktop actions stateless.
- Maintain separate SDK and transport contracts.

The detailed RFC explains why none is the right universal default.

## Compatibility and migration

The rollout is additive. Canonical authorization and a single-runtime guard land first, followed by the direct SDK default, platform-aware MCP ownership, private workers, and authenticated service cleanup. `CuaDriver.connect()` remains available while compatibility use is measured. Each phase can return to service-default documentation without weakening authorization.

## Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

Trusted host code selects immutable runtime authorization. Agent-visible arguments, session IDs, environment metadata, and reconnect requests cannot widen it. Different trust levels use separate processes. Service endpoints authenticate peers before accepting runtime work.

Telemetry is limited to topology, versions, generation, permission mode, policy digests, counts, and structured lifecycle outcomes. It excludes screenshots, accessibility trees, typed text, clipboard data, cookies, browser storage, page content, file contents, protected-consent responses, and serializable authority values.

## Validation and acceptance evidence

- Contract parity across Rust, Python, TypeScript, MCP, worker, and service paths.
- Authorization, configuration-precedence, lifecycle, and generation tests.
- macOS TCC attribution and main-thread overlay tests.
- Windows interactive-session and UIAccess boundary tests.
- Linux display, compositor, and Wayland portal-scope tests.
- Service peer-authentication and remote-principal tests.
- Browser and CDP bindings remain generation-scoped.

## Unresolved questions

- Which platform callbacks need an explicit process coordinator?
- What protocol should the private worker use?
- Which daemon administrative tools still need typed SDK replacements?
- What measured usage should precede a future `connect()` deprecation RFC?
- Does any current consumer require mixed permission modes in one shared service after separate workers ship?

## RFC document pull request

#2550

## Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and RFCs.
- [x] This public proposal contains no credentials, private user or partner data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [x] I described the problem, alternatives, migration, and required evidence, not only an implementation preference.

title: docs: supersede RFC 2447 with SDK-owned runtime RFC
body:
## Summary

- add RFC 2549, making the typed SDK-owned runtime the default application boundary
- make authorization portable as a runtime ceiling plus immutable session contexts
- preserve released behavior through a compatibility session for existing CLI, MCP, daemon, Rust, Python, and TypeScript callers
- require trusted host creation and authenticated action binding before advertising mixed permission modes in one runtime
- retain separate runtime-owner processes as the safe fallback and private workers and authenticated services as explicit optional topologies
- start with one direct runtime per process
- preserve the standalone macOS CuaDriver.app identity while allowing direct ownership for embedded hosts
- keep gRPC, MCP, HTTP, local sockets, and environment forwarding outside the transport-free native runtime and public SDK contract
- coordinate generated remote Driver connections with #2513 without creating a second desktop-control vocabulary
- mark RFC 2447 as superseded while carrying forward its typed SDK, generated binding, native core, and versioned C ABI decisions
- add a diagram-driven north-star note for the target topology and migration path

## Why

RFC 2447 combined the typed SDK contract, ABI direction, runtime ownership, MCP topology, permission-mode isolation, and platform lifecycle into one broad proposal. RFC 2549 keeps the contract decisions that have proven useful and replaces the less focused runtime and process-topology guidance with explicit ownership, lifecycle, platform, authentication, migration, and acceptance gates.

The permission contract is deliberately separated from the process topology. Effective authority is the intersection of an immutable runtime ceiling, an immutable session context, managed policy, and user policy. A model-visible tool argument, public session ID, MCP metadata field, or reconnect token is never authority.

Discussion: #2549
Supersedes: #2447
Related remote-connection proposal: #2513
Canonical authorization prerequisite: #2542
Portable session-authorization foundation: #2545

## Compatibility promise

This refactor is not allowed to disrupt current CLI, MCP, Rust, Python, or TypeScript users. Existing commands, defaults, flags, sockets, platform identity, exit codes, schemas, constructors, typed methods, package exports, result envelopes, structured errors, and lifecycle behavior are explicit release gates.

Released callers that do not use a future trusted host session API inherit a compatibility session with today's behavior and require no source changes. The host-only session factory is additive. Mixed modes are exposed only on topologies whose session-to-action binding passes substitution, replay, expiry, revocation, generation, and reconnect tests.

Browser-use improvements may continue shipping through the current CLI and daemon topology. Canonical dispatch authorization (#2542) and the portable session-authorization foundation (#2545) can land before the larger SDK-owned-runtime refactor; direct SDK ownership, private workers, remote connections, and service cleanup do not block the browser release.

## Security and disclosure review

The public issue, RFC, north-star note, and staged diff were scanned for credentials, private paths, private user or partner context, sensitive screenshots, raw session material, and vulnerability details. The proposal states target security requirements without publishing implementation-state vulnerability claims.

## Validation

- `npm --prefix docs run docs:check-hygiene`
- `npm --prefix docs run docs:check-links`
- `npm --prefix docs run docs:check`
- Markdown whitespace checks for the new and modified RFC files
- staged-file sensitive-content scan
- independent Claude Code Fable architecture review, followed by a blocker-closure review with a ready verdict

title: docs: document monorepo component release resolution
body:
## Summary

- document that Cua's components have independent release streams
- prohibit using GitHub's repository-wide `Latest` badge or `/releases/latest` as component release evidence
- require agents to inspect canonical installers, baked-version precedence, component tag prefixes, and exact release assets
- record Cua Driver's `cua-driver-rs-v*` resolution behavior

## Why

The repository-wide GitHub release badge does not determine what the monorepo's component installers deliver. Release-status claims must reflect the component-specific distribution path users actually invoke.

## Validation

- inspected the Unix and Windows Cua Driver installers on current `origin/main`
- confirmed baked-version precedence and the prefix-filtered GitHub Releases API fallback
- ran `git diff --check`

title: feat(cua-driver): implement SDK-owned runtime RFC
body:
## Summary

- implement RFC 2549’s SDK-owned runtime architecture while preserving CLI/MCP as the preferred standalone-agent integrations
- add immutable runtime/session authorization, direct and private-worker ownership, remote envelope negotiation/cancellation, authenticated service sessions, and deterministic shutdown semantics
- preserve standalone macOS TCC ownership while adding explicit `cua-driver mcp --direct` for hosts that deliberately own attribution
- harden local service and Windows UIAccess boundaries, fail closed in Windows Session 0, and make platform-facility limitations structured and explicit
- retain the earlier browser-scale and nested-Wayland E2E fixes already carried by this PR

## Compatibility

- released CLI/MCP defaults, constructors, package exports, schemas, and result envelopes remain covered by frozen fixtures
- previous-release Rust, Python, and TypeScript application sources compile or run unchanged against the candidate packages
- daemon-backed CLI/SDK actions negotiate compatibility before dispatch, including replacement daemons at the same endpoint
- legacy remote-carrier implementations remain source-compatible but fail closed until they advertise cancellation support

## Documentation and examples

- document when imported applications should use direct SDK ownership versus standalone CLI/MCP
- document macOS TCC attribution, Windows interactive-session requirements, Linux display ownership, service authentication, and runtime lifecycle
- update the reusable Cua Driver skill and in-process SDK examples
- add previous-release application fixtures for Rust, Python, and TypeScript

## Local and standard CI verification

- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked`
- SDK, CLI compatibility, private-worker, macOS overlay, contract, core parity, and browser setup-UI suites
- generated contract, UniFFI binding, and public C ABI checks
- TypeScript typecheck and SDK tests
- Python UniFFI loader tests
- agent SDK Python/TypeScript example checks
- docs internal/external links, public hygiene, and production build
- release metadata, platform unit/compile, Nix policy/package, script, attribution, and fleet-mirror checks
- `git diff --check` and sensitive-content scan

## Independent review

Claude Code Opus 5 reviewed the complete RFC diff and follow-up macOS setup-UI hardening. All blocking findings were fixed; the final verdict is **GO**.

title: docs: propose RFC 2562 self-hosted paired multi-host Driver
body:
## Summary

- Propose **RFC 2562**: self-hosted **paired multi-host** remote connection for physical PCs (comp1 → comp2/comp3)

title: Windows installer loses executable-path quotes when enabling autostart for profiles containing spaces
body:
## Summary

On Windows, the cua-driver installer fails to register autostart when the user profile path contains a space, such as `C:\Users\First Last`.

This also blocks callers such as `hermes update` on an Administrator PowerShell window until the user presses Enter.

## Environment

- Windows 11
- cua-driver 0.12.6
- Installer launched from a non-elevated PowerShell session
- Default autostart enabled

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Windows account whose profile path contains a space.
2. From a non-elevated PowerShell session, run the official Windows installer.
3. Approve the UAC request.
4. Observe the elevated PowerShell error.

## Actual result

The elevated process receives an unquoted command similar to:

```powershell
& C:\Users\First Last\...\cua-driver.exe autostart enable
```

PowerShell treats `C:\Users\First` as the command and reports `CommandNotFoundException`.

The installer then waits at:

```text
cua-driver autostart enable failed; press Enter to close
```

The driver files are installed, but `cua-driver autostart status` reports `not-registered`.

## Expected result

The scheduled task should be registered regardless of spaces in the Windows profile path, and a non-interactive caller should not be blocked by a failure prompt.

## Root cause

`Register-CuaDriverAutostart` builds a quoted PowerShell command in `$elevCmd`, then passes it through `Start-Process -ArgumentList`:

https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/libs/cua-driver/scripts/install.ps1#L580-L584

PowerShell documents that `Start-Process` joins ArgumentList values and does not automatically retain outer quotes:

https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/start-process#-argumentlist

## Tested fix direction

Elevating the installed executable directly avoids the second PowerShell command-string boundary:

```powershell
$proc = Start-Process `
    -FilePath $InstalledBinary `
    -ArgumentList @("autostart", "enable") `
    -Verb RunAs `
    -Wait `
    -PassThru `
    -ErrorAction Stop

if ($proc.ExitCode -ne 0) {
    throw "cua-driver autostart enable failed (exit $($proc.ExitCode))"
}
```

This was tested with an executable path containing spaces. Registration returned exit code 0, the `cua-driver-serve` task was created at `RunLevel=Highest`, and `cua-driver status` confirmed the daemon was running.

## Related report

Hermes Agent has the same user-visible failure tracked at:

https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/60808

title: fix(cua-driver): declare WinRects support for GNOME Shell 49 and 50
body:
## Problem

`libs/cua-driver/wayland-helper/winrects@cua/metadata.json` declares
`shell-version: ["45","46","47","48"]`, so GNOME Shell 49 and 50 refuse to load
the helper.

Without the helper, cua-driver has no target-addressable activation adapter on
GNOME and — correctly — refuses foreground dispatch:

```
wayland_backend: The RemoteDesktop portal is reachable, but this compositor has
no verified target-activation adapter (foreign-toplevel=false, screencopy=false,
ext-image-copy=false, ext-output-source=false, virtual-pointer=false,
wl_shm=true). Portal/libei input is global and would otherwise affect whichever
window is focused, potentially the wrong application, so cua-driver refuses
foreground dispatch.
```

That makes Linux input effectively unavailable on current Ubuntu — 26.04 LTS
ships GNOME Shell 50.1.

## Change

Metadata only: `shell-version` gains `"49"` and `"50"`. No code change.

## Verification

The extension was installed **unmodified** (only this metadata line differs) on
Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, GNOME Shell 50.1, Wayland session, with cua-driver 0.12.6.
The full D-Bus surface was exercised:

| Method | Result on Shell 50.1 |
|---|---|
| load | `gnome-extensions info winrects@cua` -> `State: ACTIVE` |
| `GetVersion` | `u 4` |
| `GetRects` | frame + buffer origins, `focused`, `stacking`, `minimized` per window |
| `Capture` | valid PNG via the Shell screenshot API (correct signature, ~1.1 MB base64) |
| `Activate` | activates the target; `bring_to_front` then returns success where it previously failed with the message above |

End-to-end input, which is what the helper exists for:

```
bring_to_front -> type_text -> press_key Return
```

into a **native GTK4 Wayland** `zenity --entry` returned exactly the typed
string via zenity's stdout, layout-correct on a German QWERTZ keymap
(`Y`/`Z` not transposed, `_` correct).

## Note on 49

50.1 is the version actually tested. 49 is included because the APIs the
extension uses are unchanged across 48-50 — the ESM `Extension` class,
`global.get_window_actors`, `global.display.sort_windows_by_stacking`,
`Meta.Window.get_buffer_rect`, `Shell.Screenshot`,
`Main.layoutManager.addTopChrome`, `Gio.DBusExportedObject` — and a gap between
48 and 50 would be arbitrary. Happy to drop `"49"` if you would rather only
declare versions with a test run behind them.
