title: feat(cua-driver)!: standardize action results
body:
## Summary

- replace legacy action-specific structured outputs with one closed `ActionResult` across all 18 pointer, keyboard, value, and browser-input tools
- keep task postconditions separate in `verify_state`, while preserving diagnostic MCP text/images and an internal rich execution record
- expose typed `action` and `verification` views in Rust, Python, and TypeScript; intentionally reject legacy or missing action payloads
- advertise and validate the same action output schema at the live MCP boundary, and retain a deliberately lossy `verified` adapter only in `computer-server` compatibility output
- document the 0.14 → 0.15 migration and update the canonical agent skill for stop/retry/escalation ownership

## Why

The old `verified` boolean and platform-specific request echoes mixed dispatch acknowledgement with evidence of effect. That made no-op or under-verified actions easy for harnesses to mistake for success. This cutover narrows the public contract to stable outcome facts (`effect`, `route`, optional delivery/evidence/escalation) and leaves visual interpretation and task completion to the multimodal agent harness.

## Breaking impact

The outer MCP `ToolResult` envelope is unchanged. For the 18 action tools, `structuredContent` is intentionally breaking: legacy fields and action-specific output types are removed. SDK callers migrate from `result.verified` to `result.action.effect`; postcondition callers use `result.verification.status`. Daemon and SDK must be upgraded together because 0.15 clients fail closed on 0.14 action payloads.

This PR now targets `main` directly and includes the internal action-truth layer that previously lived in #2711. Its prerequisite verification work landed through #2705 before this branch was rebased.

- Windows `PostMessage` text is confirmed only when read-back changed and contains the complete requested text.

title: cua-driver (Linux/X11): pixel click panics the worker in evdev — assertion failed: name_bytes.len() + 1 < UINPUT_MAX_NAME_SIZE
body:
## Summary

On Linux/X11, escalating an accessibility click to a **pixel** click kills a `tokio-rt-worker` with a panic inside `evdev`, in the code path that creates the ephemeral uinput pointer:

```
thread 'tokio-rt-worker' panicked at
/github/home/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/evdev-0.12.2/src/uinput.rs:209:9:
assertion failed: name_bytes.len() + 1 < UINPUT_MAX_NAME_SIZE
```

After the panic the daemon keeps listening but is effectively dead for input: every subsequent call fails with

```
A connection to the bus can't be made
```

Reproduced twice, deterministically, on the same setup.

## Why this is worth fixing regardless of the name

Two separate problems, and the second one is the expensive one:

1. The uinput device name exceeds the kernel's `UINPUT_MAX_NAME_SIZE` (80 bytes). Whatever the name is built from should be clamped or truncated.
2. **An `assert!` inside a dependency takes down a worker thread instead of the call returning an error.** From the caller's side this does not look like "the click failed" — it looks like the *application under test* stopped responding, because the driver goes quiet and every later call reports a bus error. It cost a full debugging session to attribute the symptom correctly: a GUI app was suspected of a main-loop freeze, when in fact the harness's own cleanup had killed it after the driver died.

Returning a structured error here (`{"code": "uinput_unavailable", ...}`) would make the failure self-describing even if the name issue is not addressed.

## What triggers it

The accessibility action is tried first and the driver reports:

```json
{"effect":"suspected_noop","path":"ax",
 "escalation":{"reason":"non-AX surface — act by pixel (x,y) off the screenshot in this response (an element px action).",
               "recommended":"px"}}
```

The caller then follows that recommendation and issues a pixel `click` with `{pid, window_id, x, y, session}`. That is the call that panics. Elements which *do* expose a real AT-SPI action never reach the uinput path and work fine — so this only bites on surfaces where the driver itself asks for pixel escalation.

## Not the cause

The daemon socket path length. First observed with a 57-character socket path under `~/.cache/...`; moving it to `/tmp/rv-cua.sock` (12 characters) and shortening the session id to two characters reproduced the identical panic. So the over-long string comes from somewhere else in the name construction.

`strings` on the binary shows the pointers are pooled in a `HashMap<String, Arc<Mutex<evdev::uinput::VirtualDevice>>>` behind `platform_linux::input::uinput_pointers` (`OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<..>>>`), alongside literals `" uinput pointer"` and `"missing uinput pointer for '"`. If the map key doubles as the device name, that key is the thing to clamp.

I could not build a minimal reproducer without a real toolkit window: `click` with `scope=desktop` is refused with `desktop_escalation_required`, and a window-scoped click needs a live window plus an element index, so the uinput path is not reachable from a bare daemon.

## Environment

| | |
| --- | --- |
| cua-driver | 0.14.1 |
| OS | Manjaro Linux, kernel 6.18.39-1-MANJARO, x86_64 |
| Display | Xvfb 800x600/1600x900 + openbox, private session bus, private `at-spi-bus-launcher` + `at-spi2-registryd` |
| `/dev/uinput` | `crw-rw----+ root:input`, user **is** in `input` |
| Session | X11 (not the Wayland backend) |

`health_report` reports `overall: ok` — AT-SPI and screen capture both pass — right up until the first pixel click.

## Suggested fix

- Clamp the uinput device name to `UINPUT_MAX_NAME_SIZE - 1` bytes (truncate on a char boundary) before handing it to `evdev`.
- Wrap the `VirtualDevice` construction so a failure returns an error to the caller rather than unwinding a runtime worker; a panicking worker leaves the daemon in a state that reports a misleading bus error for the rest of its life.

Possibly related but distinct: #2304 (ephemeral uinput pointer, Qt/Plasma SIGSEGV).

title: fix(cua-driver): open Finder folder URLs reliably
body:
## Summary

- normalize local `launch_app.urls` before handing them to macOS, including `~/...` paths
- dispatch Finder folder opens to Finder's synchronous native selector on the AppKit main queue, with a bounded wait
- avoid blocking that selector with the wildcard activation observer, while retaining targeted post-launch focus restoration

## Root cause

The existing macOS preflight expanded a leading `~`, but the original string was still handed to `NSURL.fileURLWithPath`. Finder therefore received a literal home-relative target and `NSWorkspace` reported that Finder could not be launched.

Using `NSWorkspace.openURLs(...withApplicationAt:)` for an already-running Finder also fails to complete reliably. The fallback process reconciliation cannot prove that a folder-open action occurred because Finder was already running. Finder's synchronous `selectFile(nil, inFileViewerRootedAtPath:)` selector returns an actionable success boolean for this Finder-specific folder operation, but AppKit requires it on the main thread. The driver therefore dispatches the narrow Finder handoff to its existing AppKit main queue, bounds the wait, and restores the prior foreground app after Finder performs it.

This is a follow-up to #1719 (local URL preflight) and #2697 (launch callback reconciliation). Repository issue/PR searches found no duplicate for Finder folder URL handoff.

## User impact

`launch_app` can open an existing local folder in Finder when the caller supplies either an absolute path or a home-relative path, without timing out on Finder's missing NSWorkspace callback and while restoring foreground focus.

## Benchmark relevance and scope

This is the first driver-owned failure in the valid task-15 full-system trace (`20260731-211044-full-system-cua-skill-15-move-conflict-t1`):

1. Immediately after session setup, the agent called `launch_app` with bundle ID `com.apple.finder` and `urls: ["~/Desktop/BenchInbox"]`.
2. That exact request failed twice with `The application “Finder” could not be launched because it was not found.`
3. The agent then spent the run navigating overlapping Finder windows manually; the run timed out after 500 seconds and never moved the renamed PNG.

The focused normalization regression below uses the benchmark's exact `~/Desktop/BenchInbox` input, while the Finder handoff regression proves that an existing local directory is selected only for `com.apple.finder`. The source-built live proof confirms the combined public-tool path opens the requested folder.

This PR deliberately does not claim to fix task 15 end to end. In the GUI-common trace, benchmark setup had already opened both `BenchInbox` and `BenchImages`, so no Finder URL launch was attempted. That run successfully renamed `a.png` to `a-new.png`, then repeatedly received `effect: unverifiable` for cross-window copy/move hotkeys and timed out without moving it. Stable Finder item selection and verified cross-window move are a separate driver-owned issue and should be handled independently.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p platform-macos apps::tests::finder_folder_handoff_is_narrowly_selected`
- `cargo test -p platform-macos tools::launch_app::tests::launch_url_normalization_expands_home_relative_paths`
- `cargo test -p platform-macos apps::nsworkspace::tests`
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` — 268 passed on merged head `c50bf5fc2c1ad8a40f0c96dc7a1eecbc13a582a4`
- `cargo check -p platform-macos --lib`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `git diff --check`

Fresh Lume macOS 26.5.2 verification used a signed source build from the exact pushed head `c50bf5fc2c1ad8a40f0c96dc7a1eecbc13a582a4` (`get_config.source_sha` matched; SHA-256 `791b1cd7d41b288bced1dd4232518a8f6f108248d34bd5bb0a36ca1718fb27dc`). Before the action no window had the target title. The exact home-relative request `~/Desktop/CuaFinderExactProof.2754.provenance` returned Finder PID 433 with `requested`, `process_running`, and `window_ready` all true; a follow-up `list_windows` observed window 423 titled `CuaFinderExactProof.2754.provenance`, and `get_window_state` resolved 57 accessibility elements with a valid screenshot frame.

title: fix(cua-driver): define list_windows z-index contract
body:
## Summary

- advertise one narrow live MCP output schema for `list_windows.windows[].z_index`: integer values increase toward the front, while `null` means stacking order is unavailable and array order must not be inferred
- validate that runtime shape without publishing the broader platform-specific window record as a generated typed-SDK contract
- document the same consumer rule across platform tool descriptions, the generated MCP reference, and the shipped Cua Driver skill
- lock the existing macOS, Windows, and X11 normalization directions with focused tests and verify native Wayland `None` serializes as `null`
- keep `launch_app.windows` aligned by preserving macOS z-index records and normalizing multi-window Windows launch results

## Root cause

The platform implementations mostly normalized native enumeration correctly, but the shared tool contract did not state direction or nullability. Consumers could therefore sort in the wrong direction or treat unavailable Wayland order as zero. The related `launch_app.windows` surface also omitted z-index on macOS and flattened multiple Windows records to zero despite claiming the `list_windows` shape.

This deliberately avoids the broader response-shape and platform-enumeration changes proposed in #2172 and #2173, and does not overlap the popup/rebind action-result work in #2746.

## Validation

- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-contract -p cua-driver-core` — 27 contract tests, 463 core tests, contract parity and session integration tests passed
- focused Rust formatting check for every modified source file
- runtime-schema assertion for `integer | null` z-index plus generated manifest/version unchanged from `main`

Closes #2199.

title: macOS menu traversal can lose safe handles after queried snapshots
body:
## Summary

Native macOS menu traversal can lose the current safe element handles when a queried `get_window_state` response is persisted for size. A caller without filesystem access may then reuse remembered bare numeric indices after a re-snapshot, silently targeting different controls.

This is an agent-operability issue, not an AX delivery failure: the Driver correctly refuses a disabled target, but another shifted index can remain enabled and perform the wrong action.

## Version and environment

- Cua Driver 0.16.0
- macOS 26.5
- Native TextEdit window

## Minimal synthetic reproduction

1. Snapshot a frontmost TextEdit window.
2. Find the `AXMenuBarItem "Window"` and invoke `pick`.
3. Re-snapshot with `include_screenshot:false, query:"Left"`.
4. Traverse `Window > Move & Resize > Left`.

Observed index movement across two snapshots:

| Index | Earlier snapshot | Later snapshot |
|---:|---|---|
| 279 | `Move & Resize` | `Zoom All` |
| 282 | `Left` | disabled separator |
| 283 | `Right` | `Move & Resize` |
| 286 | another menu row | `Left` |

The queried later response was approximately 52 KB because `query` filters `tree_markdown` but retains the complete structured `elements` payload. The MCP host persisted the response rather than returning the matching rows inline. In a tool-only environment without file access, the caller could not recover the new token/index from the persisted result.

The installed macOS guidance also says closed menu subtrees are skipped until opened, but the initial snapshot included closed `Move & Resize` descendants as disabled actionable rows. That makes pre-open indices look reusable even though every re-snapshot replaces the index cache.

## Expected

A tool-only caller should be able to complete the documented two-snapshot menu flow without reading a persisted file and without relying on bare numeric indices from an earlier snapshot.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- Provide an opt-in query mode that returns matching structured elements plus their ancestor chain while preserving original indices and tokens.
- Ensure menu-flow examples use `element_token`, so a stale handle fails explicitly after any re-snapshot.
- Align the closed-menu-subtree behavior with the installed guidance, or update the guidance to describe the actual platform behavior.
- Add a macOS test covering `Window > Move & Resize > Left` across successive snapshots and proving that an old handle cannot activate a different menu item.

## Impact

The caller can perform an unintended but non-destructive menu action and exhaust its task deadline even though the desired menu item is present and actionable.

- preserve real modifier-key state for foreground pointer selection on macOS, Windows, and X11, and refuse routes that cannot represent it safely
- bind foreground key and menu delivery to the exact target window so inline editing and native menu actions cannot land in a different foreground app
- confirm macOS modified selection only after a settled target transition while every previously selected peer remains selected
- keep caller-owned filesystem operations at the headless rung, with explicit conflict policy and source/destination readback before claiming success
- add AppKit, WPF, and GTK fixtures plus representative editing and modified-selection E2E coverage
- lock the packaged skill's filesystem strategy and GUI proof boundaries with focused regression tests

Native Wayland currently has no route that can pair virtual-pointer delivery with keyboard modifier state, so modified pointer clicks fail explicitly there instead of degrading to a plain click.

## Local verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p platform-macos` (286 passed)
- `cargo test -p platform-linux` (16 passed)
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core` (482 passed)
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-contract` (29 passed)
- packaged-skill regression tests
- AppKit, GTK, and WPF harness test compilation

## Exact-head desktop certification

Source: `58b77c5dee1da00b2bfb513d479e5ae904772fc3`

- [Linux X11 full matrix](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/30761470479): 84 delivered, 42 expected refusals, 0 failed, 0 skipped across native, shared, and capture lanes
- [Linux Wayland/sway full matrix](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/30761470483): 83 delivered, 43 expected refusals, 0 failed, 0 skipped across native, shared, and capture lanes
- [Windows full matrix](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/30761470491): 107 delivered, 25 expected refusals, 0 failed, 0 skipped across native, shared, capture, and install lanes
- Logged-in macOS VM: the exact-window menu, inline-edit commit, and modified-selection rows passed with fixture-state oracles; the clean full run executed 157 rows and passed 156 behavior rows. The unrelated installed TextEdit setup opened without a document window, and five otherwise-passing rows hit the existing trajectory-video finalization flake, so the aggregate report remained red. A clean-session focused Tauri rerun also passed after the VM display/WebKit session was restored.

All ordinary pull-request checks are green. The macOS caveats above are outside this pull request's changed behavior and are retained in the private certification evidence rather than being relabeled as product passes.

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): update --apply always aborts — the current version's own ~/.cua-driver-rs cache is misdetected as a v0.2.13 legacy layout, and the migration taskkills the updater itself
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver update --apply` never completes on Windows. It stops at the legacy-migration step and exits
with code 1; the installed version is unchanged. Two independent defects combine:

1. `install.ps1` treats the existence of `~/.cua-driver-rs` as "legacy layout v0.2.13 or earlier" —
   but **the current version creates that directory itself** (update-check cache + telemetry).
2. The migration branch runs `taskkill /F /IM "cua-driver.exe" /T`, which kills the very
   `cua-driver update --apply` process that launched the installer.

So every `update --apply` walks into the migration path and then terminates itself.

## Environment

- `cua-driver-rs` 0.14.1 → attempted upgrade to 0.16.0, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
- Windows 11 26100, non-elevated user shell, per-user install (no admin)

## Clean-room reproduction (host that never had cua-driver installed)

```
STATE BEFORE: modern=False legacy=False bin=False
install.ps1 -Release 0.16.0 -NoAutoStart        → cua-driver 0.16.0, ~/.cua-driver-rs absent
cua-driver check-update                          → ~/.cua-driver-rs created (version_check.json)
cua-driver update --apply                        → exit 1, version still 0.16.0
```

So a brand-new install is one ordinary command away from a permanently broken `update --apply`.

Confirming the causal chain: setting `CUA_DRIVER_RS_HOME` / `CUA_DRIVER_RS_INSTALL_DIR` to the paths
already in use makes the migration branch return early (see the guard below) and `update --apply`
then succeeds — 0.16.0 → 0.17.0 in one run.

## Reproduction (existing install)

```
> cua-driver update --apply
Current version: 0.14.1
Checking for updates…
New version available: 0.16.0
Downloading and installing cua-driver 0.16.0…
==> cua-driver-rs installer (Windows)
==>   install dir : C:\Users\<u>\AppData\Local\Programs\Cua\cua-driver\bin
==>   package home: C:\Users\<u>\.cua-driver
==> detected legacy install layout (v0.2.13 or earlier); migrating to Cua\cua-driver
   ← output ends here, exit code 1

> cua-driver --version
cua-driver 0.14.1        # unchanged
```

Repeats identically every time.

## Root cause 1 — the "legacy" marker is written by the current version

`install.ps1`:

```powershell
$LegacyHomeDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".cua-driver-rs"
...
$hasLegacy = (Test-Path -LiteralPath $LegacyVisibleBinDir) -or (Test-Path -LiteralPath $LegacyHomeDir)
if (-not $hasLegacy) { return }
Write-Step "detected legacy install layout (v0.2.13 or earlier); migrating to Cua\cua-driver"
```

`crates/cua-driver/src/version_check.rs`:

```rust
/// `~/.cua-driver-rs/` — same subdirectory the telemetry client uses,
/// kept separate from the `~/.cua-driver/` config tree that the Swift
/// reference owns.
const HOME_SUBDIRECTORY: &str = ".cua-driver-rs";
```

On this machine `~/.cua-driver-rs` contains exactly one file — `version_check.json`, timestamped
minutes ago by `cua-driver check-update`. There is no legacy install: the modern layout
(`~/.cua-driver/packages/...` + `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Cua\cua-driver\bin`) is the only one present,
and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\trycua\...` does not exist.

Because `update --apply` runs a version check first, the directory is guaranteed to exist by the time
the installer inspects it — the false positive is self-inflicted and permanent.

## Root cause 2 — the migration kills the updater

Inside the same branch:

```powershell
& schtasks.exe /End /TN "cua-driver-serve" 2>$null | Out-Null
& taskkill.exe /F /IM "cua-driver.exe" /T 2>$null | Out-Null
```

`cua-driver update --apply` is itself `cua-driver.exe`, so `/IM cua-driver.exe /T` terminates the
parent of the running installer. That explains the truncated output and exit 1 immediately after the
`Write-Step` line.

## Suggested fix

1. Detect legacy by an actual legacy artifact rather than the directory alone — e.g. require
   `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\trycua\cua-driver-rs\bin\cua-driver.exe` or a `packages/` tree inside
   `~/.cua-driver-rs`; a lone `version_check.json` must not trigger migration. Alternatively move the
   update-check/telemetry cache into `~/.cua-driver/` so the two namespaces stop overlapping.
2. Exclude the current process from the kill in the migration path (e.g. `taskkill /FI "PID ne <self>"`,
   or enumerate and skip `$PID`), so a self-invoked `update --apply` can survive it.

## Why this may have gone unnoticed

The documented upgrade path (`irm https://cua.ai/driver/install.ps1 | iex`) is unaffected: there the
installer runs inside `powershell.exe`, so `taskkill /IM cua-driver.exe` does not kill it. The failure
is specific to the installer being a child of `cua-driver.exe`, i.e. exactly `update --apply`.

## Workaround

Set both env vars to the paths already in use before updating — the migration branch returns early:

```powershell
$env:CUA_DRIVER_RS_HOME = "$env:USERPROFILE\.cua-driver"
$env:CUA_DRIVER_RS_INSTALL_DIR = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Cua\cua-driver\bin"
cua-driver update --apply     # 0.16.0 → 0.17.0, no migration attempted
```

## Alternative workaround

Manual layout swap: download the release zip, unpack into
`~/.cua-driver/packages/releases/<ver>-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, repoint the `current` and `bin`
junctions, restart the daemon. Works reliably.

title: cua-overlay-wl burns ~17-28% of one core indefinitely on KDE Wayland; --no-overlay doesn't gate it
body:
### Summary
On KDE Plasma (KWin) under Wayland, the `cua-overlay-wl` thread — the Wayland agent-cursor overlay — enters an **unbounded redraw loop** after certain capture/cursor activity, burning ~17-28% of one core forever, even with zero calls in flight. `--no-overlay` suppresses only the X11 overlay variant; the wl thread is unaffected. Reproduced on **cua-driver 0.17.0** (latest release as of 2026-08-03).

### Environment
- cua-driver 0.17.0 (`check-update` confirms latest)
- KDE Plasma 6.7.3 / KWin 6.7.3, Wayland session
- CachyOS (Arch-based), NVIDIA RTX 3060 Ti (proprietary), fractional scale 1.6
- Daemon spawned as stdio child of an MCP host (`cua-driver mcp --no-overlay` / embedded `serve`)

### Evidence
- **Thread census** after ~23 min of burn: `cua-overlay-wl` at **14,917 CPU ticks**; every other thread ≤26 ticks → the overlay thread is 100% of the burn.
- **Sustained burn measured at reap:** daemon spawned 02:10:40, last tool call 02:11:46, still burning at 02:30:57 → `age=1217s, cpu=33,433 ticks` ≈ **27.5% of one core for 20+ minutes with zero activity**.
- `set_agent_cursor_enabled(False)` does **not** stop it.
- **NOT version-deterministic:** same 0.17.0 binary, same host, same day — a second daemon sat at **0 ticks** the entire time. The trigger is situational (some capture/cursor patterns kick the loop; most don't).
- Note: KWin 6.7.3 **does** expose `zwlr_layer_shell_v1` (v5) — the overlay can attach; this is a pacing/redraw defect, not a display failure.

### Relationship to PR #2331
PR #2331 ("bound X11 overlay render work", merged Jul 18) fixed this bug class for `cua-overlay-x11` (idle 99.5% → 0%). The Wayland overlay is a **separate code path** and still reproduces on 0.17.0.

### Suggested fixes (any would help)
1. **Idle-bounding** for the wl render loop — mirror #2331: skip redraws when the cursor hasn't moved; pace on `wl_surface.frame` callbacks instead of busy redraw.
2. Make `--no-overlay` **authoritative for both variants** (it currently only kills the x11 thread).
3. Don't start the overlay thread when agent-cursor visuals are disabled.

### Repro
1. KDE Plasma 6.7 Wayland.
2. `cua-driver serve` (0.17.0).
3. Start a session; run a few captures/cursor moves with the agent cursor enabled.
4. Stop all calls → within minutes `cua-overlay-wl` burns a core indefinitely.
5. Confirm: `for t in /proc/<pid>/task/*; do cat "$t/comm"; done` → `cua-overlay-wl` present; `/proc/<pid>/stat` fields 14+15 delta ≈ 17 ticks/s.

### Mitigation (until fixed)
Daemon lifecycle management is required on KDE Wayland — kill the daemon when idle (a watchdog that kills daemons aged >5 min with >120s CPU works; it respawns on next use). Happy to test a patch.

title: cua-driver: press_key can report delivery_failed after the key is delivered
body:
## Summary

On macOS, a background pixel-addressed `press_key` can deliver Return successfully while returning `effect: "unverifiable"` with `escalation.reason: "delivery_failed"` and recommending foreground delivery.

## Environment

- Cua Driver 0.17.0 (signed release artifact)
- macOS 26.5.2, arm64
- Declared window-scoped session
- Terminal.app target

## Reproduction

1. Start a window-scoped session.
2. Launch or select a Terminal window and take a fresh `get_window_state` snapshot.
3. Use pixel-addressed `type_text` to enter a harmless long-running shell command; verify the text delivery.
4. Take another fresh window snapshot.
5. Call pixel-addressed `press_key` with `key: "return"` and background delivery.
6. Verify execution through an external oracle such as the Terminal title and the spawned child process.

## Actual result

The key was delivered and the command executed, but `press_key` returned:

```json
{
  "delivery": {"mode": "background"},
  "effect": "unverifiable",
  "escalation": {
    "reason": "delivery_failed",
    "target": "foreground"
  },
  "route": "synthetic_events"
}
```

## Expected result

When delivery cannot be positively confirmed, the result should remain explicitly unverifiable without asserting `delivery_failed`. If a delivery oracle exists, the action should report the confirmed outcome. A successful background key should not trigger unnecessary foreground escalation.

title: bug(cua-driver): macOS bring_to_front reports exact-window success without raising it
body:
## Summary

On macOS, `bring_to_front` can return `activated: true` with `path: "skylight"` even though the requested window remains behind other ordinary layer-0 windows.

The target process becomes the frontmost application, but the exact requested window is not raised. This contradicts the tool contract, which says the app genuinely holds foreground and that `window_id` fronts the exact macOS window.

## Reproduction

Reproduced with `cua-driver 0.12.3` using two ordinary applications, where application B had two visible windows:

1. Put application A in the foreground.
2. Record the WindowServer order with `list_windows`.
3. Call `bring_to_front` for application B's lower window, passing both `pid` and `window_id`.
4. Read the frontmost process and call `list_windows` again.

The tool returned:

```json
{
  "activated": true,
  "path": "skylight",
  "window_id": "B2"
}
```

macOS reported application B as the frontmost process, but the relevant WindowServer order was unchanged:

```text
B1  z_index 31
A   z_index 30
B2  z_index 26  <- requested exact window
```

The requested B2 window remained behind both B1 and application A.

## Current source behavior

The same result contract remains on current `main` at `e7b42ca04f306084b8bd5dc60c47b18bbdf9aed1`:

- `platform-macos/src/tools/bring_to_front.rs` maps `set_front_process_persistently(...) == true` directly to `activated: true`.
- `platform-macos/src/input/skylight.rs` returns `true` when `SLPSSetFrontProcessWithOptions` returns zero.
- There is no bounded post-action check that the requested window became key/frontmost or moved to the expected z-order.

In other words, `activated` currently proves that WindowServer accepted the request, not that the documented exact-window postcondition occurred.

## Expected behavior

When `window_id` is supplied, `activated: true` should mean that the requested window was verified as the frontmost window for the target application and is no longer behind another ordinary layer-0 application window.

If macOS activates the process but does not raise the exact window, the tool should either complete a bounded exact-window activation sequence or return an honest partial/failure result rather than `activated: true`.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- [ ] Verify both target-process activation and exact requested-window identity after a bounded settle.
- [ ] Distinguish request acceptance from verified effect in the structured result.
- [ ] Return a structured partial/failure result when the process activates but the exact window remains behind another layer-0 application window.
- [ ] Add a macOS E2E test with two applications and two target-process windows, using the frontmost process and WindowServer z-order as independent oracles.
- [ ] Cover a modal sheet or floating-window case in addition to ordinary windows.

## Related

- #2206 covers action-scoped foreground delivery and restoration. This issue covers the separate persistent `bring_to_front` exact-window contract.

title: docs(cua-driver): document elements[].frame coordinate space
body:
## Problem

`get_window_state` returns per-element geometry in `structuredContent.elements[].frame`, but the reference docs did not state which coordinate space it uses.

The frames are screen-absolute. Pixel actions addressed with `pid` and `window_id` instead take window-local screenshot pixels. Passing a frame center directly into `click({pid, window_id, x, y})` can therefore land off-target by the window origin and capture scale without producing a structural error.

This is the remaining documentation gap related to #1564: the geometry shipped, but its coordinate space was not written down.

## What this changes

Documentation only — one new section in `docs/content/docs/reference/cua-driver/limits.mdx`:

- a table of coordinate spaces and units for `elements[].frame`, window-scoped pixel arguments, and desktop-scoped pixel arguments
- `element_token` as the preferred route, or `element_index` with its matching `snapshot_id`
- the correct window-scoped conversion: rebase against `list_windows` bounds, then rescale to the `get_window_state` PNG
- the correct desktop-scoped conversion: rescale the frame center into the `get_desktop_state` PNG; this matters on macOS Retina displays because frames are logical points while the desktop capture is native pixels
- clarification that `double_click` uses the same window-local pixel conversion even though its generated argument description currently says “Screen”
- a note that `window_bounds` is emitted by `get_window_state` on macOS only

No production files are touched.

## Validation

The coordinate-space claims were checked against the current implementations and canonical harnesses on macOS, Windows, and Linux.

Local checks:

- `git diff --check`
- Cua Driver generated-reference drift check
- docs internal-link check
- public docs hygiene check
- production docs build compiled and type-checked successfully; static generation then encountered the pre-existing unrelated `/reference/lume/cli-reference` error, `ReferenceError: vm is not defined`

Refs #1564

title: cua-driver 0.17.0 Linux/X11: serve hangs forever in AT-SPI listener activation (works when AT-SPI connect fails)
body:
# cua-driver 0.17.0 Linux/X11: `serve` hangs forever in AT-SPI listener activation (works when AT-SPI connect fails)

## Environment
- OS: Linux Mint 22.3 (Zena), kernel 7.0.0-28-generic
- Desktop: XFCE 4 (xfce4-session), X11 (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11`, `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=XFCE`)
- cua-driver: 0.17.0 (also reproduced on 0.16.0 and 0.14.1)
- at-spi2-core: 2.52.0-1build1
- D-Bus: 1.14.10
- GTK3: 3.24.41-4ubuntu1.3
- Access path: SSH session with `DISPLAY=:0`, `XAUTHORITY` set, session bus reachable (`unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus`)

## Symptom
`cua-driver serve` never reaches "listening". Process stays alive, zero stdout/stderr, socket file never appears. `health_report` reports daemon not running. `hermes computer-use doctor` also times out. Same result for `cua-driver mcp` (MCP stdio mode).

## Root cause isolation
`cua-driver doctor` passes everything: X11 connected (3 visible top-level windows), `org.a11y.Bus` reachable via session bus. `pyatspi` works fine (26 desktop children).

The hang is in cua-driver's own AT-SPI listener activation. Evidence:

**Experiment 1 — normal session bus (hangs):**
```bash
DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS="unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus" timeout 8 cua-driver serve --socket /tmp/repro-ok.sock --permission-mode standard --no-overlay
# → no output, killed by timeout (hang)
```

**Experiment 2 — broken session bus (works):**
```bash
DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS="unix:path=/run/user/1000/nonexistent-bus" timeout 8 cua-driver serve --socket /tmp/repro-bad.sock --permission-mode standard --no-overlay
# → WARN: could not activate the persistent AT-SPI listener: AT-SPI connect failed
# → Cua Driver daemon listening on /tmp/repro-bad.sock
```

**Experiment 3 — pyatspi control (works):**
```bash
DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS="unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus" python3 -c "import pyatspi; print(pyatspi.Registry.getDesktop(0).childCount)"
# → 26
```

So: when AT-SPI connect *fails*, serve starts fine (listener activation is best-effort and skipped). When AT-SPI *succeeds*, serve hangs forever waiting on something in the AT-SPI interaction.

## strace evidence (normal session bus)
strace shows: connects to session bus → `GetAddress` on `org.a11y.Bus` returns `unix:path=/run/user/1000/at-spi/bus_0` → connects to the AT-SPI bus → AUTH EXTERNAL / NEGOTIATE_UNIX_FD handshake succeeds → sends a D-Bus method call targeting an `/org/a11y/...` object → then blocks in `recvmsg` + `futex`/`epoll_wait` forever. No reply ever arrives from the AT-SPI side. The session's AT-SPI bus (`org.a11y.atspi.Registry` on bus_0) is up and responds to other clients.

## Version testing
Reproduced identically on 0.17.0, 0.16.0, and 0.14.1 — not a recent regression.

## Workarounds tried
- `CUA_DRIVER_RS_DISABLE_A11Y_ADVERTISE=1` → no effect (the hang is not the advertise step; advertise runs on a separate thread and the binary logs `unknown CUA_DRIVER_RS_A11Y_ADVERTISE_MODE; using desktop default` for other values)
- `--no-overlay` → no effect
- Broken `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` → works, but loses the AT-SPI element tree entirely (ax_capability fails; screenshot still works, element-index/SOM interaction does not)

## Request
Please investigate the AT-SPI listener activation path on Linux/X11 — it appears to block forever when the AT-SPI bus is reachable but something in the initial interaction (register listener / enumerate registry?) never completes. Happy to provide full strace logs or run any diagnostic you suggest.

title: chore(deps): bump undici from 7.28.0 to 7.29.0 in /libs/cua-driver/typescript
body:
Bumps [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici) from 7.28.0 to 7.29.0.
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v7.29.0

⚠️ Security fixes

High severity

  • GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272: malformed qualified private Cache-Control directives could cause cross-user information disclosure in shared caches or a parse-time crash. The cache parser now treats empty qualified directives conservatively and safely handles mixed qualified and unqualified directives. Fixed by 9f10f1e9, with regression coverage in 466e99d1.

Medium severity

  • GHSA-m8rv-5g2x-5cg5: a malicious type property on a duck-typed blob-like HTTP/1.1 request body could inject CRLF sequences into the generated content-type header. Undici now coerces and validates the value before adding it to the request. Fixed by 33928bc2.
  • GHSA-jr45-8vmc-qm54: optional whitespace around = in qualified no-cache and private directives could bypass shared-cache restrictions and disclose authenticated data across users. Cache-Control parsing now normalizes these forms and applies conservative cache decisions. Fixed by 98011a86.
  • GHSA-8xcm-r25x-g524: the retry interceptor could expose a stale Content-Length after resuming a partial response, potentially causing downstream response desynchronization, hangs, or corruption. title: Add a reusable Cua Driver release-certification skill for Lume macOS Tahoe
body:
## Problem

Cua Driver has strong low-level guidance for macOS, recording, browser mode, and the repository-owned Lume runner, plus a public how-to guide. The internal `trycua/skills` catalog currently has no reusable scenario skill for certifying Cua Driver from source in a clean Lume macOS Tahoe Cua VM.

As a result, agents must reconstruct the release-certification workflow each time and commonly lose time on VM selection, host capacity, signing/TCC setup, provenance checks, recording finalization, and evidence packaging.

## Proposed skill

Add a focused skill such as `cua-driver-lume-release-qa` to `trycua/skills`. Keep it above the core Cua Driver contract and reference the canonical repository docs rather than duplicating them.

The workflow should:

1. Resolve and freeze the requested Cua source SHA/version, with a clean named worktree and an exact source marker.
2. Preflight host disk headroom and the Apple two-active-VM limit before starting or pulling a VM.
3. Pull a pinned `macos-tahoe-cua` image tag, verify its OCI manifest/config, and use a task-specific VM name.
4. Sync the exact source and run `install-local.sh --release --autostart --require-stable-signing`.
5. Establish a certificate-backed stable local identity and verify installed binary/app provenance.
6. Grant Accessibility and Screen Recording through VNC in the disposable guest, then verify both grants.
7. Restart the installed daemon in unrestricted mode with `--dangerously-bypass-approvals` for QA.
8. Run representative Calculator and typed-browser Chrome workflows using snapshot/action/snapshot, independent postcondition oracles, and explicit sessions.
9. Start recording before the first action, stop/finalize it, validate `recording.mp4` with ffprobe, and retain trajectory/screenshot evidence.
10. Produce a sanitized evidence bundle containing source SHA, installed version/provenance, signing/TCC state, action/oracle summaries, and playable videos.
11. Define safe cleanup behavior without deleting VM disks or unrelated evidence by default.

## Guardrails

- Never infer installation success from an installer exit code alone.
- Never accept a result from a VM whose guest filesystem reported write/I/O corruption.
- Never overlap another task's active VM or stop its process without authorization.
- Never include credentials, IPs, VM names from private environments, raw session traces, or machine-specific paths in reusable artifacts.
- Use VNC only for disposable guest setup and observation. Cua Driver actions plus independent oracles remain the certification proof.
- Keep browser QA on a disposable driver-owned profile unless an authenticated-profile test is explicitly required.

## Acceptance criteria

- New skill lands in `trycua/skills` with `agents/openai.yaml`.
- It references the canonical Cua Driver skill, Lume runner, and public Tahoe QA guide.
- Repository and skill-creator validators pass.
- The skill is dogfooded from a clean pulled Tahoe Cua image against an exact source SHA.
- One successful run produces independently validated Calculator and Chrome MP4s plus a sanitized provenance/evidence summary.

title: Windows 10: list_apps UWP scan logs 0x80070005 and blocks for ~30 seconds
body:
### Environment

- OS: Windows 10 Pro, 22H2, build 19045
- cua-driver: 0.14.2 (reproduced) and 0.17.0 (reproduced; latest release at time of testing)
- Install form: per-user installation at `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Cua\cua-driver\bin\cua-driver.exe`
- Daemon: started natively on Windows via the logon scheduled task, standard permission mode. The same delay was also observed from a daemon launched through a WSL-initiated process path.
- Client: `cua-driver call` CLI, and an MCP client whose tool-call deadline is 30 seconds.

### Summary

- `--version`, `list-tools`, and `status` complete quickly (0.04 s to ~1.3 s).
- `call list_apps` consistently takes about 30 seconds and logs the WinRT access-denied warning. `call list_windows` independently shows similar 31–32 second latency, but current source does not route it through the installed-app scan, so it may be a separate symptom.
- During `list_apps`, the daemon logs `WARN installed_apps: scan_uwp_packages: WinRT error: Access is denied. (0x80070005)`.
- A client with a 30-second tool-call deadline times out on these calls.

### Minimal reproduction

Terminal A — daemon (if not already running):

```
cua-driver serve
```

Terminal B — client:

```
cua-driver call list_apps
cua-driver call list_windows
cua-driver status
```

All commands above were executed against both 0.14.2 and 0.17.0 during testing. Both `call list_apps` and `call list_windows` exhibited the delay in this minimal reproduction. The UWP scan warning was observed for `list_apps`; the similar `list_windows` latency is reported as a separate observation.

### Expected behavior

`list_apps` should return promptly, or fail promptly with an actionable error when the optional UWP enumeration is unavailable. `list_windows` should also return promptly; its similar latency is not attributed here to the UWP scan.

### Actual behavior

| Command | Observed duration |
|---|---|
| `cua-driver --version` | 0.036 s |
| `cua-driver list-tools` | 0.043 s |
| `cua-driver status` | 1.3 s |
| `cua-driver call list_apps` (0.14.2) | 30.5 s (two runs: 30.46, 30.62) |
| `cua-driver call list_windows` (0.14.2) | 31.8 s |
| `cua-driver call list_apps` (0.17.0) | 30.3 s (two runs: 30.30, 30.28) |
| `cua-driver call list_windows` (0.17.0) | 31.7 s |
| PowerShell `Get-AppxPackage` (same user session, comparison) | 0.37 s |

### Relevant daemon log

```
WARN installed_apps: scan_uwp_packages: WinRT error: Access is denied. (0x80070005)
```

### Additional configurations tested

- Unrestricted permission mode (daemon started with `--permission-mode unrestricted --dangerously-bypass-approvals`): same ~30 s delay.
- cua-driver 0.14.2 vs 0.17.0: identical behavior.
- Native Windows daemon startup (logon scheduled task) vs WSL-initiated process path: identical behavior.
- AppX-related services (AppXSvc, StateRepository) were running at test time; `Get-AppxPackage` from PowerShell in the same user session enumerated 202 packages in ~0.37 s, indicating general AppX package enumeration is available.
- Note: these observations do not fully exclude permission/token-level causes; an elevated-process comparison has not been performed.

### Suspected source area

Verified against current `main` (commit `53e6736f0bc549d5be01fcc550a180b7cac4f10f`):

- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/win32/installed_apps.rs`: `list_installed_apps()` unconditionally calls `scan_start_menu()` then `scan_uwp_packages()`; `scan_uwp_packages()` calls WinRT `PackageManager::FindPackagesWithPackageTypes(PackageTypes::Main)` and swallows errors (best-effort enumeration). No option to skip or disable the UWP scan was found in the current source or driver config schema.
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs`: `ListAppsTool::invoke` calls `crate::win32::list_installed_apps()` as part of its merge step.
- The warning line above was introduced by #1643 (observability for #1636), so it is expected to appear whenever the WinRT call fails.

This is localization evidence, not a final root-cause proof. The exact underlying cause remains unresolved and could involve the specific WinRT API path, initialization/threading behavior, or token interaction.

Note: `list_windows` does not call the installed-app enumeration path in current source (`win32/windows.rs` uses EnumWindows + UI Automation; the `ListWindowsTool` implementation uses `list_windows` plus the process table only). Its similar ~31 s delay has not been independently isolated; it may share an underlying environment factor or be a separate issue.

### Workaround

- Using a non-semantic coordinate backend (from the MCP client side) avoids this code path.
- Raising the client timeout beyond 30 s allows the calls to complete, but leaves poor latency; not considered a satisfactory fix.

### Unresolved questions

1. Is Windows 10 22H2 expected to support the WinRT `PackageManager` enumeration path used here?
2. Is there a supported way to disable or skip the UWP package scan?
3. Could the best-effort UWP scan use a shorter timeout, or return immediately after an access-denied error?
4. Could the UWP scan be isolated from `list_apps` (and any callers that do not strictly need it) when its result is optional?
5. Would maintainers prefer: a minimal C#/PowerShell reproduction, additional debug logs (e.g. `RUST_LOG=cua_driver=debug`), an elevated-process comparison, Windows event-log evidence, or a diagnostic build?

### Related

- #1636 (closed): `list_apps` misses UWP apps for non-RID-500 admin users — same enumeration path and the same observability log line, but the symptom differs (empty UWP section vs ~30 s blocking delay). Related, not a duplicate.

title: feat(cua-sandbox): migrate to the native fleet CRDs (fleet_sdk post cloud#6316)
body:
`fleet_sdk` (shipped in the `cua-fleet` wheel) now speaks the `osgym.cua.ai` CRDs directly — see trycua/cloud#6316. `PoolSpec` and `PoolTemplate` no longer exist, so `cua_sandbox` does not import today against the new binding. This migrates the package.

## What changed in the underlying API

A warm pool no longer carries a VM shape. It holds `replicas` plus a `sandboxTemplateRef`, and the VM shape moved into an `OSGymSandboxTemplate` at `spec.vmTemplate` — with the service list now living *inside* the VM template rather than beside it. Pool status reports `replicas`/`readyReplicas` instead of `availableCount`.

## Consumer-facing API change

`PoolSpec` and `PoolTemplate` are removed from `cua_sandbox`. Replace them with a template reconcile followed by a pool reconcile:

```python
# before
await Pool.reconcile(CreatePoolRequest(
    namespace="foo",
    spec=PoolSpec(
        replicas=1,
        services=[SandboxService(name="server", target_port=8000, protocol=ServiceProtocol.TCP)],
        template=PoolTemplate(container_disk_image="registry.example/workspace:latest", ...),
        autoscaling=None,
    ),
))

# after
await Template.reconcile(CreateTemplateRequest(
    namespace="foo",
    name="workspace",
    spec=OsGymSandboxTemplateSpec(
        vm_template=VmTemplate(
            container_disk_image="registry.example/workspace:latest",
            services=[SandboxService(name="server", target_port=8000, protocol=ServiceProtocol.TCP)],
            ...,
        ),
    ),
))

pool = await Pool.reconcile(CreatePoolRequest(
    namespace="foo",
    spec=OsGymSandboxWarmPoolSpec(
        replicas=1,
        sandbox_template_ref=SandboxTemplateRef(name="workspace"),
        autoscaling=None,
    ),
))
```

`pool.claim()` is unchanged. Claiming without an explicit spec still does the right thing: `create_claim` now defaults `sandboxTemplateRef` from the pool's own spec, so the default is correct by construction rather than by convention.

## Per-file

- **`cua_sandbox/__init__.py`** — dropped the `PoolSpec`/`PoolTemplate` re-exports; added `CreateTemplateRequest`, `OsGymSandboxTemplateSpec`, `OsGymSandboxWarmPoolSpec`, `VmTemplate`. `Template` is the new wrapper class; the SDK record is re-exported as `TemplateResource`, mirroring how `Pool` wraps the pool resource.
- **`cua_sandbox/pool.py`** — added a `Template` wrapper mirroring `Pool`, with a type-checked `Template.reconcile(CreateTemplateRequest)`. `Pool` is otherwise unchanged.
- **`cua_sandbox/transport/fleet_cloud.py`** — `_FleetClient` gained `create_template`, `reconcile_template`, `get_template`, and `delete_template` passthroughs. `wait_pool` reads `ready_replicas`. `_pool_request()` now emits only replicas plus the template ref; the VM shape moved to a new `_template_request()`. `connect()` creates the template before the pool, `_cleanup_resources()` deletes it after the pool, and `delete_sandbox` resolves the template through the pool's `sandboxTemplateRef`.
- **`cua_sandbox/sandbox.py`** — the Fleet listing state machine reads `readyReplicas` instead of `availableCount`.
- **`cua_sandbox/sync/__init__.py`** — added a blocking `Template` facade alongside `Pool`.
- **`README.md`** — the pool section now documents the template-then-pool flow with native request objects (it previously showed a dict form that the typed API had already outgrown).
- **tests** — `test_pool.py`, `test_fleet_cloud_transport.py`, and `test_fleet_cloud_client.py` migrated to the new shapes, with coverage added for template reconcile, template-before-pool ordering, cleanup ordering, and `readyReplicas` polling.

## Versions

Bumped to `0.1.25` and pinned `cua-fleet==0.0.9`.

**`uv.lock` is deliberately untouched**: `cua-fleet` 0.0.9 is being released in parallel and is not on PyPI yet, so `uv lock` cannot resolve it (`no version of cua-fleet==0.0.9`). Someone needs to re-run `uv lock` in `libs/python/cua-sandbox` once the wheel publishes, and move the `0.0.8` assertion in `tests/test_fleet_sdk_packaging.py::test_lock_uses_the_published_fleet_bundle` to `0.0.9` at the same time. The lock was already stale relative to `pyproject.toml` before this PR (it pins `cua-sandbox` 0.1.21 against a declared 0.1.24), and it is not consumed by CI.

## Also in this PR

`tests/test_fleet_cloud_client.py::test_pool_lookup_matches_sdk_resources` was deleted. It asserted that `get_pool` falls back to listing pools, which stopped being true when the SDK gained named-pool lookup; it has been failing with `AttributeError: no attribute '_client'` independently of this migration, and `test_pool.py::test_fleet_client_get_pool_uses_name_lookup_without_listing` asserts the current behaviour.

## Validation

Run against a local build of the post-#6316 `fleet_sdk` binding (`libcyclops_sdk.dylib` built from `cyclops-cs` at the migration commit), since the `cua-fleet` 0.0.9 wheel is not published yet:

- `python3 -m py_compile` over all changed Python files — clean.
- `pytest tests/test_pool.py tests/test_fleet_cloud_client.py tests/test_fleet_cloud_transport.py tests/test_fleet_sdk_packaging.py` — **45 passed**.
- Wider unit run (excluding integration/runtime suites needing Docker, QEMU, adb, or cloud credentials) — **125 passed, 12 skipped**. The one failure, `test_fleet_sdk_distribution`, is an artifact of the harness: it asserts `fleet_sdk` is provided by an installed `cua-fleet` distribution, and the binding was injected on `PYTHONPATH` rather than pip-installed.
- Not run: `test_vm_cleanup` (8 pre-existing failures in the legacy API-key `CloudTransport` path, unrelated to Fleet), `test_runtime`, `test_android_multitouch`, and the integration suites — all need local hypervisors, devices, or credentials.
- `grep -rE "\bPoolSpec\b|\bPoolTemplate\b" libs/python/cua-sandbox/` — 0 matches. Same for `availableCount`/`spec.template`.
- `ruff`, `black`, and `isort --check-only` clean on every changed file.

title: feat(cua-driver): drop the session orb from the cursor badge
body:
## What

Removes the session orb — the 10pt session-colored dot at the leading edge of the cursor badge — on every platform, and moves the identity signal it carried into the pill itself.

## Why

The orb duplicated a signal the badge already carried:

- Any state with an active **delivery chip** already renders the pure session color, since that chip is filled with it at 220 alpha (`badge_glyphs.rs`).
- `session_badge_layout` returns `None` when there is no label *and* no chips, so the contracted state documented in the badge restructuring plan always contains that filled chip. The orb contributed nothing there.

That left exactly one state where the orb was load-bearing: **label-only display** (session reveal, hover restore). Rather than keep 17pt of permanent width for one state, that state's identity moves into the pill:

- Gradient accent weights raised `0.52/0.40/0.18` → `0.66/0.52/0.26`.
- The 1px rim is now tinted 55% toward the session color instead of plain white. The rim costs no width and does not sit under the label, so text contrast is unaffected regardless of how bright a session color hashes to.

Net effect: identity is present in *every* state the badge renders, and the label gets back 17pt of a 188pt budget (~9%) before it ellipsizes.

## Before / after

Same state — `background` delivery, `ax` target, label `Research`:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Orb + white rim, label pushed right | No orb, label at the leading padding, session-tinted rim |

Rendered from `cargo run -p cursor-overlay --example export_gallery_frames --features theme-authoring`.

## Every OS

The orb existed in two places, both updated:

- `rust/crates/cursor-overlay/src/session_badge.rs` — the shared renderer consumed by **macOS**, **Windows**, **Linux X11**, and **Linux Wayland** overlays. Verified: no platform crate duplicates the badge geometry; they all call `session_badge_layout` / `paint_session_badge`.
- `wayland-helper/winrects@cua/extension.js` — the GNOME Shell actor that hand-mirrors the Rust design (`_badgeDot` removed, `badgeStyle` gradient + rim brought in line).

## Tests

- `cargo test -p cursor-overlay` — 42 passed, 0 failed.
- New guard `label_starts_at_the_leading_padding_with_no_reserved_marker` pins the invariant that nothing reserves space ahead of the label.
- The existing `badge_gradient_tracks_session_color_and_zero_alpha_paints_nothing` covers the label-only state and still distinguishes two session colors — now via gradient + rim rather than the orb.
- Installed locally via `scripts/install-local.sh` (exit 0).

Two `cua-driver` integration tests (`set_value_via_element_index`, `type_text_chars_tool`) fail in this environment, and `platform-linux` examples don't compile on macOS (`x11rb`). Both confirmed pre-existing on a stashed clean baseline — unrelated to this change.

## Follow-up not in this PR

The two badge screenshots in `docs/content/docs/how-to-guides/driver/personalize-cursor.mdx` are externally hosted GitHub assets that still show the orb. The prose needs no change (it never described the orb), but those images want regenerating. Flagging rather than silently leaving them stale.

title: docs(cua-driver): fix bounded manifest examples that cannot load
body:
## Problem

Three published bounded-manifest examples are refused by the runtime at startup, so anyone following them gets a daemon that will not start.

| Page | Failure |
| --- | --- |
| `how-to-guides/driver/write-a-bounded-manifest.mdx` | `origin-scoped bounded manifests cannot allow 'click' because it bypasses the typed browser origin adapter` |
| `reference/cua-driver/permission-modes.mdx` | same refusal |
| `how-to-guides/driver/drive-a-web-page.mdx` | `unsupported application terminate scope 'never'; expected deny, driver_launched, or any` |

The first two paired `resources.browser.origins` with `click`, `type_text`, `press_key`, and `get_window_state`. `session_manifest.rs:813-841` rejects that combination at load time.

## Why the examples had to be restructured rather than trimmed

Every navigation is checked against the origin set (`session_manifest.rs:141`), so a manifest allowing `browser_navigate` with no origins refuses every navigation — verified live:

```
call browser_navigate {url: https://example.com}  # manifest declares no origins
→ Permission denied: the live browser origin is outside the bounded session policy
```

A browser manifest therefore always needs origins, and declaring origins always excludes generic input. Browser work and desktop work cannot share one manifest. The how-to now presents an application manifest in step 1 and a complete typed-browser-only manifest in step 2.

## Also documented

- The full excluded tool set.
- Why observation (`get_window_state`, `verify_state`, `get_desktop_state`) is excluded alongside input: a browser-window screenshot or AX tree exposes whichever tab is open, regardless of the allow-list.
- That the check reads `allow.tools` alone and does not analyze whether a browser is reachable, so a manifest naming only a non-browser application is refused on the same terms. Verified: a TextEdit-only manifest with `desktop.display: false` still cannot list `click` beside origins, even though `click` against an out-of-scope pid is independently refused with `bounded_resource_outside_manifest`. Noted as deliberate fail-closed behavior rather than presented as a tight invariant.
- `list_windows` as the substitute for `get_window_state` when a browser call needs a `window_id`.

## Verification

Every complete manifest example on all three pages was extracted from the MDX and loaded against cua-driver 0.17.0 in bounded mode. All four now start; before this change, three of four failed.

```
howto-0.yaml Cua Driver daemon listening on ...
howto-1.yaml Cua Driver daemon listening on ...
ref-0.yaml   Cua Driver daemon listening on ...
web-0.yaml   Cua Driver daemon listening on ...
```

Docs-only; no runtime behavior changes.

title: feat(cua-sandbox): 0.1.26 — service request headers passthrough, cua-fleet 0.0.10
body:
Two changes needed by the hermes-kubevirt fleet e2e:

- `Services.request` / `Transport.request_service` gain an optional `headers` mapping, appended to the lease-authenticated request by the fleet transport. Callers need this to satisfy spec-compliant streamable-HTTP MCP servers (`accept: application/json, text/event-stream` + `mcp-session-id`) — without it the sandbox MCP answers 406/400, which is exactly how the hermes computer-use smoke failed.
- Repin to cua-fleet 0.0.10 (cua-train 0.1.6: random petname claim names, trycua/cloud#6368), fixing 409 AlreadyExists on retried/concurrent Fleet leases.

title: ci: restore PR #2805 release attribution

- retain the existing fail-closed behavior for other unresolved human coauthor emails

The Cua Driver 0.18.0 release PR #2836 cannot collect attribution for squash commit `aebd9962d2686e75ff9e17e0a3735e303ff96981`. This restores the contributor credit from #2805 without weakening the collector's other attribution checks. It changes release infrastructure and tests only; it does not change product behavior or request another product release.
